en: Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, addressed the Blessed One in this way:

“It is wonderful, Blessed One, how these bodhisattva mahāsattvas, while taking up, retaining, reciting, mastering, and properly attending to this perfection of wisdom, acquire here such righteous qualities and bring sentient beings to maturity.”
They purify the buddha-fields and travel from buddha-field to buddha-field,

attending upon the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones; and by whichever roots of merit they desire to honor, revere, respect, and worship those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, those roots of merit become fulfilled for them, and whatever [they wish]...
They hear the Dharma from those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and do not forget it until they have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment and have attained excellence of lineage.
They embrace excellence of mother, they embrace excellence of birth, they embrace excellence of retinue, they embrace excellence of marks,
and they embrace excellence of radiance.
They acquire perfection of the eye, they acquire perfection of voice, they acquire perfection of meditative concentration,
and they acquire perfection of dhāraṇīs; and through skill in means, having manifested themselves in the form of a Buddha,
they travel from world-system to world-system.
Where there is no arising or appearance of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, they go there and speak in praise of the perfection of generosity,
and they speak in praise of the perfection of ethical discipline.
They speak in praise of the perfection of patience,
they speak in praise of the perfection of vigor, and they speak in praise of the perfection of meditative concentration.
They speak in praise of the perfection of wisdom;
they speak in praise of internal emptiness; they speak in praise of external emptiness.
They speak in praise of internal-external emptiness;
they speak in praise of the emptiness of emptiness; they speak in praise of great emptiness.
They speak in praise of the emptiness of the ultimate truth,
they speak in praise of the emptiness of the conditioned, and they speak in praise of the emptiness of the unconditioned.
They speak in praise of absolute emptiness;
they speak in praise of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end;
they speak in praise of the emptiness of non-dispersal.
They speak in praise of the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
they speak in praise of the emptiness of all phenomena; [they speak in praise] of the emptiness of specific characteristics.
They speak in praise of [all] colors;
they speak in praise of the emptiness of non-apprehension; they speak in praise of the emptiness of non-existence.
They speak in praise of the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
they speak in praise of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
They speak in praise of the four dhyānas.
They speak in praise of the four immeasurables; they speak in praise of the four formless attainments; they speak in praise of the five superknowledges.
They speak in praise of the four foundations of mindfulness;
they speak in praise of the four right efforts;
they speak in praise of the four bases of psychic power.
They speak in praise of the five faculties, they speak in praise of the five powers,
and they speak in praise of the seven factors of enlightenment.
They speak in praise of the noble eightfold path;
they speak in praise of the four noble truths;
they speak in praise of the eight liberations.
They speak in praise of the nine successive meditative attainments;
they speak in praise of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; they speak in praise of the concentrations.
They speak in praise of the gateways of dhāraṇīs;
they speak in praise of the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
they speak in praise of the four grounds of self-confidence.
They speak in praise of the four analytical knowledges;
they speak in praise of great loving-kindness; they speak in praise of great compassion.

They speak in praise of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*). Through skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*), they teach the Dharma to sentient beings and discipline them within the three vehicles (*yāna*):
the vehicle of the disciples (*śrāvakayāna*), the vehicle of the solitary buddhas (*pratyekabuddhayāna*), and the Great Vehicle (*mahāyāna*).
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, again addressed the Blessed One as follows:
It is wonderful, Blessed One, how all six perfections are encompassed when the perfection of wisdom is encompassed;
how the internal emptinesses are encompassed,
and the external emptinesses are encompassed.
The internal-external emptinesses are fully embraced; the emptiness of emptiness is fully embraced;
the great emptiness is fully embraced.
The emptiness of the ultimate truth is embraced; the emptiness of the conditioned is embraced;
the emptiness of the unconditioned is embraced.
The emptiness of the ultimate is fully embraced; the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is fully embraced;
the emptiness of non-dispersal is fully embraced.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is fully embraced; the emptiness of all phenomena is fully embraced; the emptiness of specific characteristics is fully embraced.
The emptiness of non-apprehension is fully embraced; the emptiness of non-existence is fully embraced;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is fully embraced.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is fully embraced;
the applications of mindfulness are fully embraced,
and the right efforts are fully embraced.
The bases of psychic power are mastered; the faculties are mastered;
the powers are mastered.
The factors of enlightenment are fully embraced;
the noble eightfold path is fully embraced; the noble truths are fully embraced.
The meditative absorptions are fully embraced;
the immeasurables are fully embraced; the formless attainments are fully embraced.
The liberations are fully embraced; the successive meditative attainments are fully embraced;
and the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are fully embraced.
The superknowledges are fully embraced; the meditative concentrations are fully embraced;
the gateways of mnemonic formulas are fully embraced.
The powers of a Tathāgata are fully embraced; the grounds of self-confidence are fully embraced; the analytical knowledges are fully embraced.
Great loving-kindness is embraced, great compassion is embraced,
and the unique qualities of a Buddha are embraced.
The fruit of stream-entry is fully grasped; the fruit of once-returning is fully grasped;
the fruit of non-returning is fully grasped.
Arhatship is fully embraced;
Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is fully embraced; and the knowledge of the aspects of the path is fully embraced.
"Thus omniscience becomes fully embraced.
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"So it is, Kauśika, so it is."
Kauśika, when the perfection of wisdom is embraced, all six perfections are embraced. Internal emptiness is embraced,
and external emptiness is embraced.
Internal-and-external emptiness is fully embraced; the emptiness of emptiness is fully embraced;
great emptiness is fully embraced.
Ultimate emptiness is embraced, conditioned emptiness is embraced,
and unconditioned emptiness is embraced.
absolute emptiness is embraced, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end is embraced,
and the emptiness of non-dispersal is embraced.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is embraced; the emptiness of all phenomena is embraced; the emptiness of specific characteristics is embraced.
The emptiness of non-apprehension is embraced; the emptiness of non-existence is embraced;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is embraced.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is embraced;
the foundations of mindfulness are embraced;
the right efforts are embraced.
The bases of psychic power are fully grasped; the faculties are fully grasped;
the powers are fully grasped.
The factors of enlightenment are embraced, the noble eightfold path is embraced,
and the noble truths are embraced.
The meditative absorptions (dhyāna) are fully embraced;
the immeasurables (apramāṇa) are fully embraced; the formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpatti) are fully embraced.
The liberations are fully embraced,
and the attainments of the successive dwellings are fully embraced.
The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are fully embraced; the supernormal knowledges are fully embraced;
and the meditative concentrations are fully embraced.
The gateways of dhāraṇī are fully grasped;
the powers of a Tathāgata are fully grasped; the grounds of self-confidence are fully grasped.
The analytical knowledges are fully embraced;
great loving-kindness is fully embraced; great compassion is fully embraced.
The unique qualities of a Buddha are embraced;
the fruit of stream-entry is embraced;
the fruit of once-returning is embraced.
The fruit of non-returning is fully grasped; arhatship is fully grasped;
and solitary enlightenment is fully grasped.
The knowledge of the aspects of the path is fully embraced,
and the knowledge of all aspects is fully embraced.

Furthermore, Kauśika, listen well and pay close attention as I explain those qualities—pertaining to the present life—which that son of good family or daughter of good family acquires when the perfection of wisdom is embraced, upheld, recited, mastered, and properly attended to through mental reflection. The input text contains no Sanskrit terms requiring IAST diacritics. The output is the requested English translation.
"So be it, Blessed One," Śakra, lord of the gods, replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this to him:
"For whoever, Kauśika, be they a follower of another sect, a wandering mendicant, Māra, or a deity belonging to Māra’s host who is full of conceit—"
Or, there will be individuals who desire to dispute this perfection of wisdom, who desire to alienate it, who desire to quarrel over it, and who desire to oppose it; for those who desire to dispute,
alienate, quarrel, and oppose it, their arising instances of dispute, alienation, quarrel, and opposition will quickly [be extinguished].
Furthermore, through their very disappearance, they will go to destruction;
for those who desire to quarrel, to create dissension, to dispute, and to oppose, their intentions shall not be fulfilled. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, it is because the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has for a long time practiced the perfection of generosity and the perfection of ethical discipline.
While practicing the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom,
[he does so] for the sake of those beings who for a long time have fallen into quarrels, disputes, conflicts, and arguments.

By renouncing those internal and external phenomena, the bodhisattva mahāsattva establishes sentient beings in the perfection of generosity; by renouncing those internal and external phenomena for the sake of which sentient beings have fallen into immorality for a long time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva establishes sentient beings in the perfection of ethical discipline.
For the sake of those beings who for a long time fall into anger, malice, and violence,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva relinquishes internal and external phenomena and establishes those beings in the perfection of patience.

For the sake of those beings for whose sake they have fallen into indolence for a long time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva relinquishes internal and external phenomena; those beings are established in the perfection of vigor.
For the sake of those beings for whose sake they have fallen into distraction for a long time...
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva renounces those internal and external phenomena for the sake of establishing sentient beings in the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*);
and for the sake of those sentient beings who have fallen into a state of impaired wisdom for a long time,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva renounces those internal and external phenomena for the sake of establishing sentient beings in the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

O Kauśika, for the sake of those beings who wander in saṃsāra— namely, due to the underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) and the outbursts of passion (*paryutthāna*)— a bodhisattva mahāsattva, through skill in means (*upāyakauśalya*), restrains the underlying tendencies and outbursts of those beings; he establishes them in the four dhyānas, encourages them to undertake the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), encourages them to undertake the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), and [establishes them] in the five superknowledges (*abhijñā*).
They were established in the four foundations of mindfulness; they were established in the four right efforts;

they were established in the four bases of psychic power; they were established in the five faculties; they were established in the five powers; they were established in the seven factors of enlightenment; they were established in the noble eightfold path; and they were established in the four noble truths.
They have been established in the nine successive meditative attainments; they have been encouraged toward all samādhis; they have been encouraged toward all the gateways of dhāraṇīs;
they have been encouraged toward the ten powers of a Tathāgata; they have been established in the four grounds of self-confidence; and they have been established in the four analytical knowledges.
They were established in great loving-kindness, established in great compassion,
and incited to undertake the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They were established in the fruit of stream-entry, established in the fruit of once-returning,
and established in the fruit of non-returning.
They are established in arhatship, established in pratyekabodhi, and established in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
These, Kauśika, will be the qualities and benefits pertaining to the present life for that bodhisattva mahāsattva who practices the conduct of a bodhisattva.

And in the future life, having awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment and turned the wheel of Dharma, he will establish sentient beings in their respective foundations and attain final nirvana in the realm of nirvana without remainder.
Kauśika, these will be the benefits and advantages for a bodhisattva mahāsattva pertaining to the future life.
Furthermore, Kauśika, in whatever region of the earth a son of good family or a daughter of good family shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom,
in that region of the earth neither Māra nor the deities belonging to Māra’s host, nor any heterodox teachers or wandering mendicants [shall have power].
Or, conceited persons may attempt to oppose, dispute, contradict, or cause the disappearance of this perfection of wisdom; yet they will subsequently experience further qualities and benefits,
when, through hearing, grasping, and cultivating this perfection of wisdom, they gradually go forth by means of the three vehicles.
They will bring an end to suffering.

Kauśika, it is just as if there were a medicinal herb called *maghi* that pacifies all poisons; and therein, some venomous snake or creature overcome by hunger and seeking food should see some kind of living being. That creature—

He would follow it with the desire to devour it. Then, that creature, terrified by the fear of death, would approach the medicinal herb named Maghī; at that point, the venomous snake, by the mere scent of that herb, would think to turn back. For what reason?
For it is like this: whatever medicinal quality that herb possesses, it certainly overcomes the poison of that venomous snake; for, Kauśika, that Maghī herb is powerful.

In the very same way, Kauśika, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom—Kauśika, regarding them, whatever disputes, quarrels, or conflicts may arise as they occur, [this perfection of wisdom will overcome them].
Through the splendor of the perfection of wisdom and the power of the perfection of wisdom, they will very quickly vanish and be pacified;
wherever they may arise, right there they shall disappear.
They will not increase. For what reason?

Because, Kauśika, the perfection of wisdom is the pacifier of all unwholesome states and not their increaser; that is to say, it is the pacifier of passion, hatred, and delusion and not their increaser.
It is the pacifier of ignorance and not its increaser.
It is the pacifier of volitional formations, not their increaser;
the pacifier of consciousness, not its increaser; the pacifier of name-and-form, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier of the six sense bases, not their increaser;
the pacifier of contact, not its increaser; the pacifier of feeling, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier of craving, not its increaser;
the pacifier of grasping, not its increaser;
the pacifier of becoming, not its increaser.
It is a pacifier of birth, not its increaser; it is a pacifier of old age and death, not their increaser.
It is a pacifier of one's own lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, not their increaser.
It leads to the pacification, not the increase, of this entire great mass of suffering;
it leads to the pacification, not the increase, of the hindrances; it leads to the pacification, not the increase, of the obscurations.
It is the pacifier of the latent tendencies and not their increaser; the pacifier of the outbursts and not their increaser;
the pacifier of the view of non-self.
It does not increase the view of a sentient being; it pacifies the view of a sentient being and does not increase it.
It does not increase the view of a living soul; it pacifies the view of a living soul and does not increase it.
It is the pacifier of the view of a living being, not its increaser;
the pacifier of the view of a soul, not its increaser;
the pacifier of the view of a person, not its increaser.
It pacifies the view of a person and does not increase it; it pacifies the view of a human and does not increase it; it pacifies the view of a man and does not increase it.
It is the pacifier of the view of an agent, not its increaser;
the pacifier of the view of an experiencer, not its increaser;
the pacifier of the view of a knower, not its increaser.
It is a pacifier of the view of a beholder, not an increaser;
it is a pacifier of the view of annihilationism, not an increaser;
it is a pacifier of the view of eternalism, not an increaser.
It is the pacifier of the view of existence, not its increaser;
the pacifier of the view of non-existence, not its increaser;
the pacifier of all modes of views, not their increaser.
It is a pacifier of stinginess, not its increaser;
a pacifier of immorality, not its increaser;
a pacifier of ill-will, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier of laziness, not its increaser;
the pacifier of distraction, not its increaser;
and the pacifier of faulty wisdom, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier of the perception of permanence, not its increaser;
the pacifier of the perception of pleasure, not its increaser; the pacifier of the perception of self, not its increaser.
It is a pacifier of the perception of beauty, not its increaser;
it is a pacifier of the wanderings of craving, not their increaser;
it is a pacifier of the grasping at form, not its increaser.

It is the pacifier of the grasping at sensation, not its increaser; the pacifier of the grasping at perception, not its increaser; the pacifier of the grasping at mental formations, not their increaser.
It is the pacifier of the grasping at consciousness, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of the grasping at the perfection of generosity, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of the grasping at the perfection of ethical discipline, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier of grasping at the perfection of patience, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of grasping at the perfection of vigor, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of grasping at the perfection of meditation, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier of grasping at the perfection of wisdom, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of grasping at internal emptiness, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of grasping at external emptiness, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at internal-external emptiness;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of emptiness;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at great emptiness.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of the ultimate;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of the conditioned;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of the unconditioned.
It is the pacifier of the grasping at absolute emptiness, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of the grasping at emptiness without beginning or end, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of the grasping at non-dispersal emptiness, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of all phenomena.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of specific characteristics;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of non-apprehension;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of non-existence.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the applications of mindfulness.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of grasping at the right efforts;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of grasping at the bases of psychic power;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of grasping at the faculties.
It is the pacifier of the grasping at strength, not its increaser; it is the pacifier of the grasping at the factors of enlightenment, not their increaser;
it is the pacifier of the grasping at the noble eightfold path, not its increaser.
It is the pacifier of grasping at the noble truths, not their increaser; the pacifier of grasping at meditative absorptions, not their increaser;
the pacifier of grasping at the immeasurables, not their increaser.
It is the pacifier of the grasping at the formless attainments, not their increaser; it is the pacifier of the grasping at the liberations, not their increaser;
it is the pacifier of the grasping at the serial attainments, not their increaser.
The gateways to liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—
are the pacifiers of grasping at supernormal powers and not their increasers; they are the pacifiers of grasping at meditative concentrations and not their increasers.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the gateways of dhāraṇīs; it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the powers of a Tathāgata;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the grounds of self-confidence.
It is the pacifier of grasping at the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), not their increaser; it is the pacifier of grasping at great loving-kindness (*mahāmaitrī*), not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of grasping at great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*), not its increaser.
It is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the unique attributes of a Buddha;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at omniscience;
it is the pacifier, not the increaser, of the grasping at the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
It is the pacifier of the grasping at omniscience, not its increaser;
it is the pacifier of the grasping at nirvāṇa, not its increaser.

Kauśika, for all these qualities belonging to the hosts of Māra, this perfection of wisdom is a pacifier, not an increaser; and as many as there are in the triple-thousand great-thousand world system the four Great Kings, Śakra the lord of the gods, Brahmā the lord of the Sahā world, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Bṛhatphala gods, and the Śuddhāvāsa gods— [all these are pacified by it].

All of them will constantly and continuously provide protection, shelter, and defense for that son of good family or daughter of good family— whether it be a son of good family or a daughter of good family— who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and correctly attend to this perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, he will be freed from unwholesome states and will increase in wholesome states.
That is to say: by means of the perfection of generosity, he will increase and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension;
by means of the perfection of ethical discipline, he will increase and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension;
by means of the perfection of patience, he will increase and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension.
Through the perfection of vigor, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension;
through the perfection of meditation, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension;
through the perfection of wisdom, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension.
Through internal emptiness, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension;
through external emptiness, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension;
through internal-and-external emptiness, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension.

Through the yoga of non-apprehension, it will increase by means of the emptiness of emptiness and will not diminish; through the yoga of non-apprehension, it will increase by means of great emptiness and will not diminish;
through the yoga of non-apprehension, it will increase by means of the emptiness of the ultimate and will not diminish.

Through the emptiness of the conditioned, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension; through the emptiness of the unconditioned, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension;
through absolute emptiness, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension.
Through the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension;
through the emptiness of non-dispersal, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension;
through the emptiness of intrinsic nature, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension.
Through the emptiness of all phenomena, he will increase and not decline by means of the yoga of non-apprehension;
through the emptiness of specific characteristics, he will increase and not decline by means of the yoga of non-apprehension;
through the emptiness of non-apprehension, he will increase and not decline by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.
Through the emptiness of non-existence, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension;

through the emptiness of intrinsic nature, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension; through the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence, it will increase and not diminish by way of non-apprehension.
He will increase in the applications of mindfulness and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension;
he will increase in the right efforts and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension;
he will increase in the bases of psychic power and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension.
He will increase in the faculties and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension;
he will increase in the powers and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension;
he will increase in the factors of enlightenment and not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension.

By means of the non-apprehension of objects, he will increase in the noble eightfold path and not decline; by means of the non-apprehension of objects, he will increase in the noble truths and not decline;
by means of the non-apprehension of objects, he will increase in the meditative concentrations and not decline.
He will increase through the immeasurables and not decline, by way of non-apprehension;
he will increase through the formless attainments and not decline, by way of non-apprehension;
he will increase through the liberations.
He will not decline through the yoga of non-apprehension;
he will increase and not decline through the successive attainments of meditative dwelling through the yoga of non-apprehension;
he will increase and not decline through the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—through the yoga of non-apprehension.
Through the superknowledges, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension;
through the meditative concentrations, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension;
through the gateways of dhāraṇīs, he will increase and not decline by way of non-apprehension.

He will increase in the powers of a Tathāgata and not decline, by way of non-apprehension; he will increase in the grounds of self-confidence and not decline, by way of non-apprehension; he will increase in the analytical knowledges and not decline, by way of non-apprehension.
He will increase in great loving-kindness and not diminish, by way of non-apprehension; he will increase in great compassion and not diminish, by way of non-apprehension;
he will increase in the unique attributes of a buddha and not diminish, by way of non-apprehension.
Through the non-apprehension of objects, he will increase in omniscience and not diminish;
through the non-apprehension of objects, he will increase in the knowledge of the aspects of the path and not diminish;
through the non-apprehension of objects, he will increase in the knowledge of all aspects and not diminish.
His speech will be authoritative and measured; he will not be one whose speech is scattered, nor will he be overcome by anger,
nor will he be overcome by pride.
He will not be stingy, he will not be envious,
and he himself will abstain from taking life.
He encourages others to abstain from taking life,
he will speak in praise of abstaining from taking life,
and he will [rejoice] in those others who shall refrain from taking life.
He will speak in praise of them and give his approval;

he himself will abstain from taking what is not given, and he will encourage others to refrain from taking what is not given. He will also proclaim the excellence of refraining from taking what is not given.
Furthermore, he will speak in praise of and approve of others who abstain from taking what is not given;
he himself will abstain from sexual misconduct, and he will encourage others to refrain from sexual misconduct and speak in praise of refraining from sexual misconduct.
And those others who will abstain from sexual misconduct, he will also praise them and approve of them;
he himself will abstain from false speech, and he will encourage others to refrain from false speech and speak in praise of refraining from false speech.
And for those others who will abstain from false speech, he will also speak their praise and give his approval;
and he himself will abstain from malicious speech.
He will encourage others to refrain from malicious speech,
he will speak in praise of refraining from malicious speech, and he will [encourage] others who have desisted from malicious speech.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval; he himself will abstain from harsh speech, and he will encourage others to undertake the abstinence from harsh speech.
He will speak in praise of abstaining from harsh speech,
and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves those others who refrain from harsh speech.
He himself will abstain from frivolous speech,
he will encourage others to refrain from frivolous speech,
and he will speak in praise of refraining from frivolous speech.
And those others who will abstain from frivolous chatter, he will also speak in praise of them and approve of them;
and he himself will abstain from covetousness.
He will encourage others to refrain from covetousness,
he will speak in praise of refraining from covetousness,
and he will [rejoice in] those others who have desisted from covetousness.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval; he himself will abstain from malice,
and he will encourage others to refrain from malice as well.
He will speak in praise of abstaining from malice,
and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who refrain from malice.
He himself will abstain from wrong view,
he will encourage others to abstain from wrong view,
and he will speak in praise of abstaining from wrong view.
And those others who will abstain from wrong view, he will also speak in praise of them and approve of them.
And he himself will practice the perfection of giving.
He will encourage others to undertake the perfection of generosity,
he will speak in praise of the perfection of generosity,
and he will [rejoice in] those others who abide in the perfection of generosity.

He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval; he himself will abide in the perfection of ethical discipline, and he will encourage others to undertake the perfection of ethical discipline.
He will speak in praise of the perfection of ethical discipline,
and he will be a speaker of praise and one who approves of those others who abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
He will himself practice the perfection of patience, he will encourage others to undertake the perfection of patience,
and he will speak in praise of the perfection of patience.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of others who will practice the perfection of patience,
and he himself will practice the perfection of vigor.
He will encourage others to undertake the perfection of vigor,
he will speak in praise of the perfection of vigor,
and he will [rejoice in] those others who are practicing the perfection of vigor.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval;
he himself will practice the perfection of meditation, and he will encourage others to undertake the perfection of meditation.
He will speak in praise of the perfection of meditation,
and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who practice the perfection of meditation.
He will himself abide in the perfection of wisdom and will also encourage others to take up the perfection of wisdom.
He will speak in praise of the perfection of wisdom,
and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who engage in the perfection of wisdom.
He will personally cultivate internal emptiness,
he will encourage others to undertake internal emptiness,
and he will speak in praise of internal emptiness.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of others who cultivate internal emptiness; he himself will cultivate external emptiness, and he will encourage others to do so as well.
He will speak in praise of external emptiness;
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who cultivate external emptiness;
and he himself will cultivate internal-and-external emptiness.
He will encourage others to take up internal-external emptiness,
he will speak in praise of internal-external emptiness,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate internal-external emptiness.
He himself will cultivate the emptiness of emptiness, he will encourage others to take up the emptiness of emptiness,
and he will speak in praise of the emptiness of emptiness.

He will also speak in praise of and approve of those others who will cultivate the emptiness of emptiness; he himself will cultivate the great emptiness, and he will encourage others to do so as well.
He will speak in praise of great emptiness;
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who cultivate great emptiness;
and he himself will cultivate ultimate emptiness.
He will encourage others to undertake the ultimate emptiness,
he will speak in praise of the ultimate emptiness,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the ultimate emptiness.
He himself will cultivate the emptiness of conditioned phenomena, he will encourage others to undertake the emptiness of conditioned phenomena,
and he will speak in praise of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena.

He will speak in praise of and give his approval to others who cultivate the emptiness of the conditioned; he himself will cultivate the emptiness of the unconditioned, and he will encourage others to do so as well.
He will speak in praise of the emptiness of the unconditioned;
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the emptiness of the unconditioned;
and he himself will cultivate the emptiness of the ultimate.
He will also encourage others to take up extreme emptiness,
he will speak in praise of extreme emptiness,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate extreme emptiness.
He himself will cultivate the emptiness that is without beginning or end, he will encourage others to undertake the emptiness that is without beginning or end,
and he will speak in praise of the emptiness that is without beginning or end.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of others who cultivate the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end;
he himself will cultivate the emptiness of non-dispersal, and he will encourage others to take up the emptiness of non-dispersal.

He will speak in praise of the emptiness of non-dispersal (*anavakāra-śūnyatā*), and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who cultivate the emptiness of non-dispersal; furthermore,
he himself will cultivate the emptiness of intrinsic nature (*prakṛti-śūnyatā*).
He will encourage others to undertake the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
he will speak in praise of the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
He will himself cultivate the emptiness of all phenomena, he will encourage others to undertake the emptiness of all phenomena,
and he will speak in praise of the emptiness of all phenomena.

He will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who cultivate the emptiness of all phenomena; he himself will cultivate the emptiness of specific characteristics, and he will encourage others to do so as well.
He will speak in praise of the emptiness of specific characteristics (*svalakṣaṇa-śūnyatā*),
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the emptiness of specific characteristics; furthermore,
he himself will cultivate the emptiness of non-apprehension (*anupalambha-śūnyatā*).
He will encourage others to take up the emptiness of non-apprehension,
he will speak in praise of the emptiness of non-apprehension,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the emptiness of non-apprehension.
He will himself cultivate the emptiness of non-existence, he will encourage others toward the emptiness of non-existence,
and he will speak in praise of the emptiness of non-existence.

He will also speak in praise of and approve of others who cultivate the emptiness of non-existence; he himself will cultivate the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and he will encourage others to do so as well.
He will speak in praise of the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and he himself will cultivate the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
He will encourage others to take up the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
he will speak in praise of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
He himself will enter into all meditative absorptions and will encourage others to enter into the attainment of all meditative absorptions;
he will also speak in praise of the attainment of all meditative absorptions.
He will speak in praise of and approve of all other meditative concentrations that others may enter;
he himself will attain the dhāraṇīs,
and he will encourage others to attain the dhāraṇīs as well.
He will speak in praise of the attainment of dhāraṇīs,
and he will be a speaker of praise and one who gives his approval to others who cultivate the attainment of dhāraṇīs.
And he himself will first enter the first dhyāna.
He will encourage others to undertake the first dhyāna and will speak in praise of the first dhyāna.
He will speak in praise of and approve of others who enter the first dhyāna;
he himself will enter the second dhyāna,
and he will encourage others to enter the second dhyāna.
He will speak in praise of the second dhyāna;
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who enter the second dhyāna;
and he himself will enter the third dhyāna.
He will encourage others to enter the third dhyāna,
he will speak in praise of the third dhyāna,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who attain the third dhyāna.
He will himself enter the fourth dhyāna,
he will encourage others to enter the fourth dhyāna,
and he will speak in praise of the fourth dhyāna.
He will speak in praise of and approve of others who enter the fourth dhyāna;
he himself will enter the meditative attainment of loving-kindness,
and he will encourage others to enter the meditative attainment of loving-kindness.
He will speak in praise of the meditative attainment of loving-kindness (*maitrī-samāpatti*),
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who enter into great loving-kindness; furthermore,
he himself will enter into the meditative attainment of compassion (*karuṇā*).
He will encourage others to enter into compassion,
he will speak in praise of the meditative attainment of compassion,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who likewise enter into compassion.
He will himself enter the meditative attainment of sympathetic joy,
he will encourage others to enter the meditative attainment of sympathetic joy, and he will speak in praise of the meditative attainment of sympathetic joy.
He will speak in praise of others who enter into sympathetic joy and will approve of them;
he himself will enter into equanimity,
and he will encourage others to enter into the attainment of equanimity.
He will speak in praise of the attainment of equanimity,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who shall likewise attain equanimity.
He himself will also enter the attainment of the sphere of infinite space.
He will encourage others to attain the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space,
he will speak in praise of the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite space,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who likewise attain the sphere of infinite space.

He himself will attain the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite consciousness, he will encourage others to attain the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite consciousness, and he will speak in praise of the meditative absorption of the sphere of infinite consciousness.
He will speak in praise of and approve of others who enter the sphere of infinite consciousness;
he himself will enter the attainment of the sphere of nothingness,
and he will encourage others to enter the attainment of the sphere of nothingness.
He will speak in praise of the attainment of the sphere of nothingness,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of, and approves of, those others who shall attain the sphere of nothingness.
He himself will enter the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, he will encourage others to enter the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception,
and he will speak in praise of the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of others who shall attain the meditative absorption of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
He himself will cultivate the four foundations of mindfulness, and he will encourage others to undertake the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness.
He will speak in praise of the cultivation of the foundations of mindfulness;
he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who cultivate the foundations of mindfulness;
and he himself will cultivate the right efforts.
He will encourage others to cultivate the right efforts,
he will speak in praise of the cultivation of the right efforts,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the right efforts.
He will himself cultivate the four bases of psychic power,
he will encourage others to practice the cultivation of the bases of psychic power,
and he will speak in praise of the cultivation of the bases of psychic power.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of others who cultivate the bases of psychic power; he himself will cultivate the five faculties,
and he will encourage others to practice the cultivation of the five faculties.
He will speak in praise of the cultivation of the five faculties,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who cultivate the five faculties;
and he himself will cultivate the five powers.
He will encourage others to cultivate the powers, he will speak in praise of the cultivation of the powers,
and he will [rejoice in] those others who cultivate the powers.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval; he himself will cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment,
and he will encourage others to undertake the cultivation of the seven factors of enlightenment.
He will speak in praise of the cultivation of the factors of enlightenment,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment.
He himself will cultivate the noble eightfold path,
he will encourage others to cultivate the noble eightfold path,
and he will speak in praise of the cultivation of the noble eightfold path.
And for those others who will cultivate the noble eightfold path, he will also be a speaker in their praise and one who gives his approval;
and he himself will cultivate the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
He will encourage others to undertake the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
he will speak in praise of the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
and he will [rejoice in] those others who cultivate the concentrations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval;
and he himself will enter into the eight liberations in both forward and reverse order.
He will encourage others to undertake the eight liberations,
he will speak in praise of the eight liberations,
and he will cause others to enter the eight liberations in both forward and reverse order.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval;
he himself will attain the nine successive meditative attainments (navānupūrvavihārasamāpatti), and he will encourage others to undertake the nine successive meditative attainments.
He will speak in praise of the attainments of the successive dwellings,
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who shall enter into the attainments of the successive dwellings.
He himself will attain the ten powers of a Tathāgata, he will encourage others to undertake the ten powers of a Tathāgata,
and he will speak in praise of the ten powers of a Tathāgata.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of others who attain the ten powers of a Tathāgata,
and he himself will cultivate the four grounds of self-confidence.
He will encourage others to undertake the grounds of self-confidence,
he will speak in praise of the grounds of self-confidence,
and he will [rejoice in] those others who cultivate the grounds of self-confidence.

He will speak in praise of them and give his approval; he himself will cultivate the four analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid), and he will encourage others to cultivate the analytical knowledges as well.
He will speak in praise of the cultivation of the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid),
and he will be one who speaks in praise of and approves of those others who cultivate the analytical knowledges.
He will himself attain the great loving-kindness, he will encourage others to attain the great loving-kindness,
and he will speak in praise of the attainment of the great loving-kindness.
He will also speak in praise of and approve of those others who cultivate great loving-kindness,
and he himself will cultivate great compassion.
He will encourage others to undertake great compassion,
he will speak in praise of great compassion,
and he will [encourage] others who cultivate great compassion.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval;
he himself will accomplish the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma), and he will encourage others to accomplish the unique qualities of a Buddha.
He will speak in praise of the accomplishment of the unique qualities of a Buddha,
and he will also be one who speaks in praise of and approves of others who accomplish those unique qualities of a Buddha.
He himself will possess the quality of non-forgetfulness, he will encourage others toward the state of non-forgetfulness,
and he will speak in praise of the quality of non-forgetfulness.
And as for others who will possess the quality of non-forgetfulness, he will speak in praise of them and give his approval;
and he himself will dwell always in equanimity.
He will encourage others to dwell in constant equanimity, he will speak in praise of dwelling in constant equanimity,
and he will [rejoice in] those others who shall dwell in constant equanimity.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval;
he will himself fulfill the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and he will encourage others to achieve the fulfillment of the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
And he will speak in praise of the fulfillment of the knowledge of the aspects of the path,
as well as of those others who will fulfill the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
He will also speak in praise of them and give his approval;
he himself will attain all-aspect omniscience,
and he will encourage others to attain all-aspect omniscience as well.
He will speak in praise of the attainment of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*),
and he will also be a speaker of praise and one who approves of those others who shall attain omniscience.

Practicing the six perfections, whatever gift he shall give, he will share it in common with all sentient beings and dedicate it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by means of the yoga of non-apprehension; whatever ethical discipline he shall maintain, he will share it in common with all sentient beings and dedicate it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.
Whatever patience he shall cultivate, he will share it with all sentient beings and dedicate it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by way of non-apprehension;
whatever vigor he shall undertake, he will share it with all sentient beings and dedicate it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by way of non-apprehension;
whatever meditative concentration he shall enter, he will share it with all sentient beings and dedicate it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by way of non-apprehension.
Whatever wisdom he shall cultivate, he will share it with all sentient beings and dedicate it toward unexcelled, perfect enlightenment by means of the yoga of non-apprehension.
As that noble son or noble daughter practices in this way within the six perfections, mindfulness will arise:
"If I do not give gifts, I will be reborn in low-born families; I will not bring sentient beings to maturity, nor will I purify the Buddha-field, nor will I attain the knowledge of all aspects."
If I do not guard my ethical discipline, I will be reborn in the three miserable destinies; I will not obtain a human birth,
nor will I bring sentient beings to maturity, nor purify a buddha-field, nor attain the knowledge of all aspects.
If I do not cultivate patience,
my faculties will be impaired, my facial countenance will become darkened, and I shall not attain excellence of form.

If, by means of such perfection of form while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, beings would not necessarily become destined for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment upon seeing me, and if I were not to ripen sentient beings through that perfection of form, nor purify a buddhafield, nor attain the knowledge of the aspects of the path; [then I would not have sought it].
If I should become lazy, I will not be able to reach the path to awakening, nor will there be the ripening of sentient beings for me,
nor the purification of the buddha-field, nor shall I attain omniscience in all its aspects;
if I should have a distracted mind, I will not be able to produce that concentration by which—
"I shall bring sentient beings to maturity, yet I shall not purify my Buddha-field, nor shall I attain omniscience;

if I am of poor wisdom, I will not be able— by means of skill in wisdom and expedient means— to transcend the level of the Śrāvakas and the level of the Pratyekabuddhas, and [thus] mature sentient beings and purify the Buddha-field."
In order to attain the knowledge of all aspects,
he will train himself thus:
"It would be improper for me, under the influence of stinginess or the influence of immorality, not to fulfill the perfection of generosity."

If, under the influence of ill will, I were not to fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline; if, under the influence of laziness, I were not to fulfill the perfection of patience; if, under the influence of distraction, I were not to fulfill the perfection of meditative concentration; or if, under the influence of faulty wisdom, I were not to fulfill the perfection of wisdom.

Without fulfilling the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom, I shall not emerge into the knowledge of all aspects. In this way, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family who will take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will obtain qualities and benefits both pertaining to the present life and to future lives.
And he will never be separated from the mind of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Śakra said: "It is wonderful, Blessed One, how this perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) has appeared for the sake of the complete taming and the non-exaltation of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas."
The Blessed One said:
"Furthermore, Kauśika, it is for the sake of the complete taming and the non-exaltation of bodhisattva mahāsattvas that the perfection of wisdom has appeared.
Śakra said: "In this regard, Blessed One, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the mundane perfection of generosity toward the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, the pratyekabuddhas, and the śrāvakas..."
He gives a gift, and it occurs to him:

"I am giving a gift to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to the Pratyekabuddhas, and to the Śrāvakas, as well as to the wretched, the beggars, the destitute, and those who ask. Because of that gift, he experiences an inflation of pride due to a lack of skillful means.

When practicing the mundane perfection of ethical discipline, it occurs to him: "I am practicing the perfection of ethical discipline; I am fulfilling the perfection of ethical discipline. He thereby becomes conceited. When practicing the mundane perfection of patience...
Thus he thinks, "I am practicing the perfection of patience; I am fulfilling the perfection of patience," and by that he becomes conceited.
While practicing the worldly perfection of vigor, he thinks, "I am practicing the perfection of vigor; I am fulfilling the perfection of vigor," and by that he becomes conceited.

While practicing the mundane perfection of meditative concentration, he thinks: "I am practicing the perfection of meditative concentration; I am fulfilling the perfection of meditative concentration. Because of that, he becomes conceited.
While practicing the mundane perfection of wisdom, he thinks: "I am practicing the perfection of wisdom; I am fulfilling the perfection of wisdom; I am cultivating the perfection of wisdom."
Through this perfection of wisdom, lacking skill in means, he becomes conceited.
He might cultivate the applications of mindfulness and think, "I am cultivating the applications of mindfulness," and by that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes conceited.
One should cultivate the right efforts;
thus it occurs to him, "I am cultivating the right efforts," and by that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes puffed up.
One should cultivate the bases of psychic power.
Thus he thinks, "I am cultivating the bases of psychic power," and through that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes puffed up;
[he thinks,] "I shall cultivate the faculties," and thus he thinks, "I am cultivating the faculties," and through that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes puffed up.
One should cultivate the powers;
thus it occurs that "I am cultivating the powers," and by means of that attachment to the notion of "I," one becomes puffed up.
One should cultivate the factors of enlightenment.
Thus it occurs to him: "I cultivate the factors of awakening," and by that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes uplifted;
"I shall cultivate the noble eightfold path," and thus it occurs to him: "I cultivate the noble eightfold path," and by that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes uplifted.
One should cultivate the noble truths; when one thinks, "I am cultivating the noble truths," one becomes puffed up by that attachment to the conceit of "I.
One should cultivate the meditative absorptions.
Thus he thinks, "I am cultivating the meditative absorptions," and by that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes puffed up;
"I shall cultivate the immeasurables," thus he thinks, "I am cultivating the immeasurables," and by that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes puffed up.
One might cultivate the formless attainments; if one thinks, "I am cultivating the formless attainments," one becomes puffed up by that attachment to the notion of "I.
One might cultivate the liberations...
Thus it occurs to him: "I am cultivating the formless attainments," and by that adherence to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up.
He thinks, "I am cultivating the successive meditative attainments," and by that adherence to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up.
One should cultivate the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
yet if one thinks, "I am cultivating the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness," one becomes puffed up by that attachment to the notion of "I.
One should cultivate the superknowledges...
Thus he thinks, "I cultivate the superknowledges," and by that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes puffed up;
he thinks, "I shall cultivate the meditative concentrations," and by that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes puffed up.
It occurs to him: "I shall attain all the dhāraṇīs," and by that adherence to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up.
It occurs to him: "I shall cultivate the ten powers of a Tathāgata," and by that adherence to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up.
It occurs to him thus... (ŚsP_II-4_20)
He thinks, "I shall cultivate the four grounds of self-confidence," and through that attachment to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up with pride.
He thinks, "I shall cultivate the four analytical knowledges," and through that attachment to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up with pride.
He thinks, "I shall cultivate great compassion," and through that attachment to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up with pride.
It occurs to him: "I shall cultivate the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha," and through that adherence to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up with pride.
It occurs to him: "I shall bring sentient beings to maturity," and through that adherence to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up with pride.
It occurs to him: "I shall purify a Buddha-field," and through that adherence to the conceit of "I," he becomes puffed up with pride.
It occurs to him: "I shall attain the knowledge of all aspects. Through that attachment to the notion of "I," he becomes uplifted.

Thus indeed, Blessed One, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva courses in worldly dharmas, he becomes uplifted through attachment to the notion of "I. For him, the perfection of wisdom is present for the sake of subduing [that pride], not for the sake of being uplifted.

Furthermore, Blessed One, here a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the supramundane perfection of giving does not perceive a giver, does not perceive a gift, and does not perceive a recipient, because he is well-cultivated in the perfection of wisdom. It is in this way that...
Blessed One, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of generosity, the perfection of wisdom stands as a support for the purpose of self-subduing and for the purpose of non-arrogance;
and when he practices the supramundane perfection of ethical discipline, because it is well-cultivated by the perfection of wisdom, he does not perceive that ethical discipline.

Ethical discipline is not apprehended. In this way, Blessed One, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of wisdom is present for the sake of self-subduing and for the sake of non-arrogance; practicing the supramundane perfection of patience, because it is well-cultivated by the perfection of wisdom, he does not apprehend patience.

Patience is not apprehended. In this way, Blessed One, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of patience, the perfection of wisdom is present for the sake of self-subduing and for the sake of non-arrogance;
while he practices the supramundane perfection of vigor, because it is well-cultivated by the perfection of wisdom, vigor is not apprehended.

He does not apprehend that vigor. Thus indeed, Blessed One, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of vigor, the perfection of wisdom is present for the sake of self-subduing and for the sake of non-exaltation;

while he practices the supramundane perfection of meditative concentration, because the perfection of wisdom is well-cultivated, he does not apprehend meditative concentration—he does not apprehend meditative concentration. Thus indeed, Blessed One.
For a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the perfection of meditation, the perfection of wisdom is present for the sake of self-subduing and for the sake of non-arrogance.
As he practices the supramundane perfection of wisdom, because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom, he does not apprehend wisdom;
he does not apprehend wisdom. It is in this way, Blessed One, that for a bodhisattva mahāsattva [the perfection of wisdom is present] in the perfection of wisdom.
As he practices the perfection of wisdom, it stands before him for the sake of complete subduing and for the sake of non-exaltation.
He cultivates the applications of mindfulness and yet does not perceive them, because the perfection of wisdom has been well-cultivated;
he cultivates the right efforts and yet does not perceive them, because the perfection of wisdom has been well-cultivated.

He cultivates the bases of psychic power and yet does not apprehend them, because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom; he cultivates the faculties and yet does not apprehend them, because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates the powers and yet does not apprehend them, because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
He cultivates the factors of enlightenment and yet does not apprehend them, because he has well cultivated the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates the noble eightfold path and yet does not apprehend it, because he has well cultivated the perfection of wisdom.
In this way indeed, Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom serves for the purpose of taming and for the purpose of non-arrogance in a bodhisattva mahāsattva.
And it becomes present before him. He cultivates the noble truths, yet he does not apprehend them because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;

he cultivates the meditative concentrations, yet he does not apprehend them because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom; he cultivates the immeasurables, yet he does not apprehend them because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
He cultivates the formless attainments and yet does not apprehend them, because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates the liberations and yet does not apprehend them, because of his cultivation of the perfections of wisdom;
he cultivates the successive meditative attainments and yet does not apprehend them, because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
He cultivates the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—and yet does not apprehend them, because he has well cultivated the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates the superknowledges and yet does not apprehend them, because he has well cultivated the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates the meditative concentrations and yet does not apprehend them, because he has well cultivated the perfection of wisdom.
He cultivates the gateways of dhāraṇī, yet he does not apprehend them because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom. In this way,
O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom stands ready for the sake of the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s self-subduing and for the sake of his non-arrogance.
He cultivates the powers of a Tathāgata and yet does not apprehend them, because he has well cultivated the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates the grounds of self-confidence and yet does not apprehend them, because he has well cultivated the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates the analytical knowledges and yet does not apprehend them, because he has well cultivated the perfection of wisdom.
He cultivates great loving-kindness, yet does not apprehend it, because he is well-cultivated in the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates great compassion, yet does not apprehend it, because he is well-cultivated in the perfection of wisdom;
he cultivates the unique qualities of a Buddha, yet does not apprehend them, because he is well-cultivated in the perfection of wisdom.
In this way, Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is present for the sake of complete taming and for the sake of non-arrogance.

He cultivates omniscience, yet he does not apprehend it because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom; he cultivates the knowledge of the aspects of the path, yet he does not apprehend it because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom.
He cultivates the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), yet he does not apprehend it because of his thorough cultivation of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). In this way,
O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom of a bodhisattva mahāsattva is present for the sake of complete subduing and for the sake of non-arrogance.
The seventeenth chapter of the *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods:

For any son of good family or daughter of good family, Kauśika, who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and study this profound perfection of wisdom, and who attends to it with correct mental attention—
such a person, when mounted in the midst of battle, having ascended to the front of a great conflict, [shall be invincible].

In that case, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, while reciting this profound perfection of wisdom, should enter into it and, having entered, remain therein, then that son or daughter of good family shall not suffer defeat;
rather, there will be victory for them, and they will emerge from that battle unhurt and unharmed.

It is impossible, Kauśika, it is out of the question that a son of good family or a daughter of good family who is reciting this perfection of wisdom, having entered into battle, should meet with an obstacle to life;
such a thing cannot occur.
Moreover, even if someone were to hurl a weapon or an arrow at their body, it would not strike their body. Why is that?
For it is because that son of good family or daughter of good family, practicing the six perfections for a long time,
has conquered the weapons of passion and the arrows of passion within himself and has conquered the weapons of passion and the arrows of passion in others;
and he has conquered the weapons of hatred and the arrows of hatred within himself and has conquered the weapons of hatred and the arrows of hatred in others.

He has conquered for himself the weapons of delusion and the arrows of delusion, and he has conquered the weapons of delusion and the arrows of delusion of others; he has conquered for himself the weapons of speculative views and the arrows of speculative views, and he has conquered the weapons of speculative views and the arrows of speculative views of others; he has conquered for himself the weapons of obsessive outbursts and the arrows of obsessive outbursts, and he has conquered the weapons of obsessive outbursts and the arrows of obsessive outbursts of others.

Having conquered the weapons of the latent tendencies and the shafts of the latent tendencies belonging to themselves, and having also conquered the weapons of the latent tendencies and the shafts of the latent tendencies belonging to others—

by relying on this very perfection of wisdom and by cultivating that perfection of wisdom— in this manner, Kauśika, no weapons or shafts hurled at that son of good family or daughter of good family while they are in the midst of battle shall fall upon their bodies.
Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom,

and remains never separated from the mind set on omniscience, then even if someone were to scatter harmful medicinal substances over them, or perform a magical incantation (*kākhorda*), or bring a pit of fire near them, or strike them with a weapon, or give them poison, or cast them into water— all that will not affect them. Why is that?

This, Kauśika, is a great spell; this, Kauśika, is a spell, namely the perfection of wisdom. This, Kauśika, is an unsurpassed spell; this, Kauśika, is a spell, namely the perfection of wisdom. This, Kauśika, is a supreme spell; this, Kauśika, is a spell, namely the perfection of wisdom.
And while training in this spell, a son of good family or a daughter of good family does not intend harm for themselves, does not intend harm for others, and does not intend harm for both. That...

For in this way, while training therein, he does not perceive a self, he does not perceive a sentient being, he does not perceive a life-principle, he does not perceive a creature, he does not perceive a nourisher, he does not perceive a person,
he does not perceive an individual, he does not perceive a human, he does not perceive a youth, he does not perceive an agent, and he does not perceive an experiencer.
One does not apprehend a knower, nor does one apprehend a seer.
One does not apprehend form,
nor does one apprehend feeling.
One does not perceive perception, one does not perceive mental formations,
and one does not perceive consciousness.
One does not apprehend the eye,
one does not apprehend the ear,
one does not apprehend the nose.
One does not apprehend the tongue,
one does not apprehend the body,
and one does not apprehend the mind.
One does not perceive form, one does not perceive sound,
one does not perceive odor.
One does not perceive taste,
one does not perceive touch, and one does not perceive mental phenomena.
One does not perceive eye-consciousness,
one does not perceive ear-consciousness,
and one does not perceive nose-consciousness.
He does not apprehend tongue-consciousness, he does not apprehend body-consciousness,
and he does not apprehend mind-consciousness.
One does not perceive visual contact,
one does not perceive auditory contact,
and one does not perceive olfactory contact.
He does not perceive tongue-contact,
he does not perceive body-contact, and he does not perceive mind-contact.
One does not perceive feeling born of eye-contact, one does not perceive feeling born of ear-contact,
and one does not perceive feeling born of nose-contact.
He does not perceive feeling born of tongue-contact,
he does not perceive feeling born of body-contact, and he does not perceive feeling born of mind-contact.
One does not perceive the earth element,
one does not perceive the water element, and one does not perceive the fire element.
One does not perceive the wind element, one does not perceive the space element,
and one does not perceive the consciousness element.
One does not perceive ignorance,
one does not perceive formative forces,
and one does not perceive consciousness.
One does not perceive name-and-form, one does not perceive the six sense bases, and one does not perceive contact.
One does not perceive feeling,
one does not perceive craving,
and one does not perceive grasping.
One does not perceive existence, one does not perceive birth,
and one does not perceive old age and death.
He does not perceive the perfection of generosity, he does not perceive the perfection of ethical discipline,
and he does not perceive the perfection of patience.
One does not apprehend the perfection of vigor,
nor does one apprehend the perfection of meditative concentration.
One does not apprehend the perfection of wisdom;
one does not apprehend internal emptiness, nor does one apprehend external emptiness.
One does not apprehend internal-and-external emptiness,
nor does one apprehend the emptiness of emptiness, nor does one apprehend great emptiness.
One does not apprehend the emptiness of the ultimate,
one does not apprehend the emptiness of the conditioned, and one does not apprehend the emptiness of the unconditioned.
He does not perceive absolute emptiness, he does not perceive the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end,
and he does not perceive the emptiness of non-dispersal.
He does not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature, he does not perceive the emptiness of all phenomena, and he does not perceive the emptiness of specific characteristics.
One does not perceive the emptiness of non-apprehension; one does not perceive the emptiness of non-existence. One does not perceive the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
one does not perceive the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
One does not apprehend the applications of mindfulness,
one does not apprehend the right efforts,
and one does not apprehend the bases of psychic power.
One does not perceive the sense faculties, one does not perceive the powers, and one does not perceive the factors of enlightenment.
One does not perceive the noble eightfold path, one does not perceive the noble truths, and one does not perceive the meditative absorptions.
He does not perceive the immeasurables, he does not perceive the formless attainments,
and he does not perceive the liberations.
One does not perceive the attainments of the successive dwellings;
one does not perceive the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
nor does one perceive the superknowledges.
He does not apprehend the meditative concentrations, he does not apprehend the gateways of mnemonic formulas, and he does not apprehend the powers of a Tathāgata.
He does not perceive the grounds of self-confidence, he does not perceive the analytical knowledges, and he does not perceive great loving-kindness.
One does not apprehend great compassion,
nor does one apprehend the unique qualities of a Buddha;
one does not apprehend the fruit of stream-entry.
One does not perceive the fruit of once-returning, one does not perceive the fruit of non-returning,
and one does not perceive arhatship.
One does not apprehend the awakening of a pratyekabuddha,
one does not apprehend the knowledge of the aspects of the path, and one does not apprehend the knowledge of all aspects.
Not perceiving [anything], he does not intend harm for himself, nor does he intend harm for others, nor does he intend harm for both;
he attains unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and he surveys the minds of all sentient beings. Why is that?
In this very science, the past Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment;
those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who will exist in the future time shall also awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment by training in this very science;
and those immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones who currently exist right now in the ten directions [do so likewise].

They too, training in this very knowledge, will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Furthermore, Kauśika, wherever this perfection of wisdom is written down, maintained, grasped, but not recited, not read aloud, not mastered, and not correctly attended to—
Furthermore, neither a human nor a non-human being shall find an opportunity to gain entry into that house, village, or city. Why is that?

It is because, for the sake of honoring this very perfection of wisdom, the sons of the gods belonging to the realm of the Four Great Kings, the sons of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, the sons of the gods of the Yāma heaven, and the sons of the gods of the Tuṣita heaven [will be present] throughout the triple-thousand great-thousand world system.

the sons of the gods of the Nirmāṇarati heaven, the sons of the gods of the Paranirmitavaśavartin heaven, the sons of the gods of the Brahmakāyika heaven, the sons of the gods of the Brahmapurohita heaven, the sons of the gods of the Brahmapārṣadya heaven, the Mahābrahmā gods, the Ābhā gods, the Parīttābhā gods, the Apramāṇābhā gods,
the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, and the Apramāṇaśubha gods.

The Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Bṛha gods, the Parīttabṛha gods, the Apramāṇabṛha gods, the Bṛhatphala gods, the Abṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods; as well as the sons of the gods belonging to the Cāturmahārājakāyika realm, the Trāyastriṃśa realm, and the Yāma realm, throughout immeasurable and incalculable world-systems.
