the appearance of the powers will occur in the world; the appearance of the factors of enlightenment will occur in the world.
The appearance of the noble eightfold path will occur in the world;
the appearance of the noble truths will occur in the world;
the appearance of the meditative absorptions will occur in the world.
There will be the manifestation of the immeasurables in the world; there will be the manifestation of the formless attainments in the world;
there will be the manifestation of the liberations in the world.
The manifestation of the nine successive meditative attainments will occur in the world;
the manifestation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—will occur in the world;
and the manifestation of the concentrations will occur in the world.
The manifestation of the gateways of dhāraṇīs will occur in the world;
the manifestation of the powers of a Tathāgata will occur in the world; the manifestation of the grounds of self-confidence will occur in the world.
The manifestation of the analytical knowledges will occur in the world; the manifestation of great loving-kindness will occur in the world;
the manifestation of great compassion will occur in the world.
The unique qualities of a Buddha will appear in the world;
omniscience will appear in the world;
and the knowledge of the aspects of the path will appear in the world.
The manifestation of the knowledge of all aspects will occur in the world;
likewise, the manifestation of great śāla clans will occur in the world, and the manifestation of great śāla brahmin clans will occur in the world.
There will be the appearance in the world of great wealthy householder families;
there will be the appearance in the world of the gods of the Four Great Kings;
there will be the appearance in the world of the Trāyastriṃśa gods.
There will be an appearance in the world of the Yāma gods;
there will be an appearance in the world of the Tuṣita gods;
there will be an appearance in the world of the Nirmāṇarati gods.

there will be an appearance in the world of the Mahābrahmā gods.
There will be an appearance in the world of the Ābhā devas;
there will be an appearance in the world of the Parīttābhā devas;
there will be an appearance in the world of the Apramāṇābhā devas.
There will be an appearance in the world of the Ābhāsvara gods;
there will be an appearance in the world of the Śubha gods;
there will be an appearance in the world of the Parīttaśubha gods.
The appearance of the Apramāṇaśubha gods in the world will occur;
the appearance of the Śubhakṛtsna gods in the world will occur;
the appearance of the Bṛhatphala gods in the world will occur.

The manifestation of the Parīttabṛhatphala gods will occur in their world; the manifestation of the Apramāṇabṛhatphala gods will occur in their world; the manifestation of the Bṛhatphala gods will occur in their world.
An appearance will occur in the world of the Abṛha devas;
an appearance will occur in the world of the Atapa devas;
an appearance will occur in the world of the Sudṛśa devas.
The appearance of the Sudarśana devas in the world will occur;
the appearance of the Akaniṣṭha devas in the world will occur;
the appearance of the stream-enterers in the world will occur.
There will be the appearance of once-returners in the world;
there will be the appearance of non-returners in the world;
there will be the appearance of arhats in the world.
The appearance of Pratyekabuddhas will occur in the world; the full realization of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas will be known,
the unsurpassed Buddha-knowledge will be known,
and the turning of the wheel of Dharma will be known.
The ripening of sentient beings will be discerned,
and the purification of the buddha-field will be discerned.

Then, indeed, those gods belonging to the class of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśas, the Yāmas, the Tuṣitas, the Nirmāṇaratis, the Paranirmitavaśavartins, the Brahmakāyikas, the Brahmapurohitas, the Brahmapārṣadyas, the Mahābrahmans, the Ābhās, the Parīttābhās, the Apramāṇābhās, the Ābhāsvaras, the Śubhas, the Parīttaśubhas, and the Apramāṇaśubhas who were in this trichiliocosm;
The Śubhakṛtsna, Bṛhat, Parīttabṛhat, Apramāṇabṛhat, Bṛhatphala, Abṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha gods addressed Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"O friend, the Prajñāpāramitā should be taken up; O friend, the Prajñāpāramitā should be maintained; O friend, the Prajñāpāramitā should be recited; O friend, the Prajñāpāramitā should be mastered."
And, friend, the perfection of wisdom must be attended to in a proper manner.

Friend, by this perfection of wisdom being taken up, retained, recited, mastered, and attended to in a proper manner, and by the lineage of the Buddhas being recited and mastered and attended to in a proper manner, there will be no interruption of the lineage of the Buddhas.

The guidance of the Dharma will not be interrupted; the guidance of the Saṅgha will not be interrupted. O worthy one, the guidance of the Buddha will not be interrupted, the guidance of the true Dharma will not be interrupted, and the guidance of the true Saṅgha will not be interrupted. The perfection of generosity will appear in the world.
The perfection of ethical discipline will appear in the world; the perfection of patience will appear in the world;
the perfection of vigor will appear in the world.
The perfection of meditation will appear in the world; the perfection of wisdom will appear in the world.
The emptiness of the internal will appear in the world.
The appearance of external emptiness will occur in the world;
the appearance of internal-external emptiness will occur in the world;
the appearance of the emptiness of emptiness will occur in the world.
The appearance of great emptiness will occur in the world;
the appearance of ultimate emptiness will occur in the world;
the appearance of conditioned emptiness will occur in the world.
The manifestation of the emptiness of the unconditioned will occur in the world;
the manifestation of absolute emptiness will occur in the world; the manifestation of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end will occur in the world.
The emptiness of non-dispersal will appear in the world;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature will appear in the world;
the emptiness of all phenomena will appear in the world.
The emptiness of specific characteristics will appear in the world;
the emptiness of non-apprehension will appear in the world;
the emptiness of non-existence will appear in the world.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature will appear in the world;
the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence will appear in the world.
The applications of mindfulness will appear in the world.
The appearance of the right efforts in the world will occur;
the appearance of the bases of psychic power in the world will occur;
the appearance of the faculties in the world will occur.
The powers will appear in the world;
the factors of enlightenment will appear in the world;
the noble eightfold path will appear in the world.
The appearance of the noble truths will occur in the world;
the appearance of the meditative absorptions will occur in the world;
the appearance of the immeasurables will occur in the world.
The manifestation of the formless attainments will occur in the world;
the manifestation of the liberations will occur in the world;
the manifestation of the serial attainments will occur in the world.
The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—will appear in the world;
the superknowledges will appear in the world;
and the meditative concentrations will appear in the world.
The manifestation of the gateways of dhāraṇīs will occur in the world;
the manifestation of the powers of a Tathāgata will occur in the world; the manifestation of the grounds of self-confidence will occur in the world.
The manifestation of the analytical knowledges will occur in the world;
the manifestation of great loving-kindness will occur in the world.
The manifestation of great compassion will occur in the world;
the manifestation of the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) will occur in the world;
the manifestation of the bodhisattva practice will occur in the world.
The fruit of stream-entry will appear in the world;
the fruit of once-returning will appear in the world;
the fruit of non-returning will appear in the world.
The manifestation of arhatship will occur in the world;
the manifestation of pratyekabodhi will occur in the world; and the manifestation of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment will occur in the world.
Then the Blessed One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas:
“Kauśika, you should take up this perfection of wisdom; uphold it, recite it, master it, and attend to it with proper mental attention. Why is that?”
Kauśika, when such thoughts arise among the asuras—
thinking, "We shall fight the gods of the Thirty-three; we shall wage war against the gods of the Thirty-three"—
then you, Kauśika, should bring this perfection of wisdom to mind and recite it mentally with thorough attention.
And if one should attend to them in this way, those manifestations of the asuras will once again disappear, and those mental states of theirs will not increase further;
and for those sons of gods and daughters of gods whose time of death has come, they shall see their own rebirth in a state of woe.

Kauśika, you should recite this Perfection of Wisdom in their presence; by that root of merit from hearing the Perfection of Wisdom and by that serene faith in the Perfection of Wisdom, they will be reborn right there in the celestial abodes. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, the hearing of the Perfection of Wisdom is of such great benefit for any son of good family whatsoever.

Whether it be a daughter of good family, a son of the gods, or a daughter of the gods, if this Perfection of Wisdom should come within the range of their hearing, they shall all, by virtue of that root of merit, gradually awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is that?

Because, Kauśika, those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who existed in the past, along with their assemblies of Śrāvakas, also trained in this very Perfection of Wisdom and [attained] unsurpassed...
He will fully awaken to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;

and those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who currently reside, stay, and maintain themselves in the world-systems of the ten directions together with their assemblies of disciples—all of them have awakened to unexcelled, perfect enlightenment right here in this Perfection of Wisdom. Why is that?

For it is thus, Kauśika, that all the factors conducive to awakening—whether the dharmas of the Śrāvakas, the dharmas of the Pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of the Bodhisattvas, or the dharmas of the Buddhas—are contained within this perfection of wisdom.

Śakra said: "O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is a great spell; O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is an unsurpassed spell; O Blessed One, this perfection of wisdom is an unequaled spell. Why is that?"
For thus, Blessed One,
the perfection of wisdom is the sustainer of all wholesome dharmas.
The Blessed One said:

"So it is, Kauśika, so it is! This is a great spell, Kauśika, this spell which is the perfection of wisdom; this is an unsurpassed spell, this spell which is the perfection of wisdom; this is an unequaled spell, this spell which is the perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, those who were the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the past..."

Having relied upon this very knowledge, those who have awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, as well as those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who will appear in the future time, shall likewise awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment by relying upon this very knowledge.

Furthermore, those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who currently reside, remain, and maintain themselves in the world systems of the ten directions—they too have awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment by relying on this very spell. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, it is by relying on this spell that the ten paths of wholesome action are made known in the world.
The four meditative absorptions (dhyānas) are known in the world; the four immeasurables (apramāṇas) are known in the world;
the four formless attainments (ārūpyasamāpattis) are known in the world.
The five superknowledges are known in the world;
the perfection of generosity is known in the world,
and the perfection of ethical discipline is known in the world.
The perfection of patience is known in the world; the perfection of vigor is known in the world;
the perfection of meditation is known in the world.
The perfection of wisdom is known in the world; internal emptiness is known in the world,
and external emptiness is known in the world.
Internal-external emptiness is known in the world; the emptiness of emptiness is known in the world;
great emptiness is known in the world.
Ultimate emptiness is known in the world; conditioned emptiness is known in the world;
unconditioned emptiness is known in the world.
The emptiness of the ultimate is known in the world; the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is known in the world;
the emptiness of non-dispersal is known in the world.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is known in the world; the emptiness of all phenomena is known in the world; the emptiness of specific characteristics is known in the world.
The emptiness of non-apprehension is known in the world; the emptiness of non-existence is known in the world;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is known in the world.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is known in the world;
the applications of mindfulness are known in the world,
and the right efforts are known in the world.
The bases of psychic power are known in the world;
the faculties are known in the world;
the powers are known in the world.
The factors of enlightenment are known in the world; the noble eightfold path is known in the world;
the noble truths are known in the world.
The meditative absorptions are known in the world; the immeasurables are known in the world;
the formless attainments are known in the world.
The liberations are known in the world;
the attainments of successive dwellings are known in the world; the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are known in the world.
The superknowledges are known in the world,
the concentrations are known in the world,
and the gateways of the dhāraṇīs are known in the world.
The powers of a Tathāgata are made known in the world;
the grounds of self-confidence are made known in the world.
The analytical knowledges are known in the world;
great compassion is known in the world;
the unique qualities of a Buddha are known in the world; and the realm of phenomena is known in the world.
The limit of reality is known in the world;
suchness is known in the world;
non-falsity is known in the world.
The non-otherness of suchness is known in the world;
the nature of phenomena is known in the world;
the stability of phenomena is known in the world.
The fixed order of phenomena is known in the world;
the five eyes are known in the world;
the fruit of stream-entry is known in the world.
The fruit of once-returning is known in the world;
the fruit of non-returning is known in the world;
arhatship is known in the world.
Pratyekabuddha-enlightenment is known in the world,
omniscience is known in the world,
and the knowledge of the aspects of the path is known in the world.
The knowledge of all aspects is made known in the world; and it is by depending on the Bodhisattva, Kauśika, that the ten paths of wholesome action are proclaimed, the four dhyānas are proclaimed,
and the four formless attainments are proclaimed.
The five superknowledges are manifested;
the perfection of generosity is manifested in the world,
and the perfection of ethical discipline is manifested in the world.
The perfection of patience is manifested in the world; the perfection of vigor is manifested in the world;
the perfection of meditation is manifested in the world.
The perfection of wisdom is manifested in the world. Internal emptiness is manifested in the world;
external emptiness is manifested in the world.
Internal-external emptiness is manifested in the world;
the emptiness of emptiness is manifested in the world;
great emptiness is manifested in the world.
The emptiness of the ultimate is manifested in the world; the emptiness of the conditioned is manifested in the world;
the emptiness of the unconditioned is manifested in the world.
The emptiness of the ultimate is manifested in the world; the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is manifested in the world;
the emptiness of non-dispersal is manifested in the world.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is manifested in the world; the emptiness of all phenomena is manifested in the world;
the emptiness of specific characteristics is manifested in the world.
The emptiness of non-apprehension is manifested in the world; the emptiness of non-existence is manifested in the world;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature is manifested in the world.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is manifested in the world.
The applications of mindfulness are manifested in the world;
the right efforts are manifested in the world.
The bases of psychic power are manifested in the world; the faculties are manifested in the world;
the powers are manifested in the world.
The factors of enlightenment are manifested in the world;
the noble eightfold path is manifested in the world;
the noble truths are manifested in the world.
The meditative absorptions are manifested in the world;
the immeasurables are manifested in the world;
the formless attainments are manifested in the world.
The liberations are manifested in the world;
the meditative attainments of successive dwellings are manifested in the world; and the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are manifested in the world.
The superknowledges are manifested in the world; the meditative concentrations are manifested in the world;
the gateways of mnemonic formulas are manifested in the world.
The powers of a Tathāgata are manifested in the world; the grounds of self-confidence are manifested in the world.
The analytical knowledges are manifested in the world;
great compassion is manifested in the world;
the unique qualities of a Buddha are manifested in the world.
Omniscience is manifested in the world; the knowledge of the aspects of the path is manifested in the world;
and the knowledge of all aspects is manifested in the world.
The stream-enterer is manifested in the world; the once-returner is manifested in the world;
the non-returner is manifested in the world.
The Arhat is made manifest in the world; the Pratyekabuddha is made manifest in the world;
the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha is made manifest in the world.
It is just as, Kauśika, when the lunar disc has appeared, all medicinal herbs, stars, and constellations are made to shine; even so, Kauśika, when the lunar disc of the Bodhisattva has appeared,

there arise all virtuous practices, right conduct, the ten paths of wholesome action, the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), the immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), the formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), the superknowledges (*abhijñā*), the perfections (*pāramitā*), the emptinesses, the factors of enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*), the emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the noble truths, the liberations (*vimokṣa*), the successive dwellings and attainments, the doors of concentration (*samādhi*) and mnemonic formulas (*dhāraṇī*), the ten powers (*daśabala*), the fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), and the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*).
They are manifested. All the stars and constellations of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas—both those in training and those beyond training—are manifested.
And the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are manifested in the world.
Even when there is no arising of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in the world, [they are manifested].
Even then, bodhisattva mahāsattvas teach mundane and supramundane dharmas to sentient beings. Why is that?
For the vehicles of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the Mahāyāna are produced from bodhisattvas;
and that skill in means of the bodhisattva mahāsattva should be understood as being produced from the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Endowed with which skillful means a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of generosity, practices the perfection of ethical discipline,
and practices the perfection of patience.
He practices the perfection of vigor,
he practices the perfection of meditation,
and he practices the perfection of wisdom.
He practices in internal emptiness, he practices in external emptiness,
and he practices in internal-external emptiness.
He practices in the emptiness of emptiness, he practices in great emptiness,
and he practices in the emptiness of the ultimate truth.
He practices the emptiness of the conditioned, he practices the emptiness of the unconditioned,
and he practices absolute emptiness.
He courses in the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end; he courses in the emptiness of non-dispersal;
he courses in the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
He courses in the emptiness of all phenomena, he courses in the emptiness of specific characteristics,
and he courses in the emptiness of non-apprehension.
He courses in the emptiness of non-existence,
he courses in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and he courses in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
He practices in the foundations of mindfulness; he practices in the right efforts;
he practices in the bases of psychic power; he practices in the faculties.
He courses in the powers, he courses in the factors of enlightenment,
and he courses in the noble eightfold path.
He practices in the noble truths,
he practices in the meditative concentrations,
and he practices in the immeasurables.
He courses in the formless attainments,
he courses in the eight liberations, and he courses in the nine successive meditative attainments.
He practices; he practices in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
he practices in the superknowledges;
he practices in the meditative concentrations.
He courses in the gateways of dhāraṇīs, he courses in the powers of a Tathāgata, and he courses in the grounds of self-confidence.
He courses in the analytical knowledges,
he courses in great compassion,
and he courses in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. Yet he does not fall to the level of a śrāvaka, nor does he realize the level of a pratyekabuddha.
He brings sentient beings to maturity and purifies the buddha-field;
he acquires excellence of lifespan, excellence of sentient beings, and excellence of the buddha-field;
he acquires the excellence of a bodhisattva and attains the knowledge of all aspects.

Furthermore, Kauśika, any son of good family or daughter of good family who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will be endowed with these qualities pertaining to the present life, and will also be endowed with qualities pertaining to future lives.

Śakra asked: “Blessed One, with what qualities pertaining to the present life will that son of good family or daughter of good family be endowed who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One said:
For any son of good family or daughter of good family, Kauśika, who shall take up this perfection of wisdom, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection,
he shall not die by poison,
nor shall he die by a weapon.
He will not die by fire, nor will he die by water,
nor indeed will he die by more than a hundredfold passion.
Setting aside the ripening of past karma,

whatever misfortunes may arise from royal households, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, while reciting this Perfection of Wisdom, should approach a royal household, [they will remain unharmed].
No one seeking an opportunity against him will find such an opening;
and princes and royal ministers will think they should converse with him and think they should address him.
They will think that they ought to greet him with friendly greetings. Why is that?

Because, through the power and majesty of this very perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, while reciting this perfection of wisdom, should approach a royal court, the princes or the king’s high ministers will think that they ought to address him with words of affection.
He will think it appropriate to address them, and he will think it appropriate to greet them. Why is that?

Because, Kauśika, a mind of loving-kindness, a mind of compassion, a mind of sympathetic joy, and a mind of equanimity have been established by those sons of good family or daughters of good family toward all sentient beings.

Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will be endowed with these qualities pertaining to the present life.
And with which qualities pertaining to future lives, Kauśika, will they be endowed?
That is to say: she will never be separated from the ten paths of action,

nor from the four dhyānas, nor from the four immeasurables, nor from the four formless attainments, nor from the six perfections, nor from the foundations of mindfulness, nor from the right efforts, nor from the bases of psychic power, nor from the faculties.

Neither by the powers, nor by the factors of enlightenment, nor by the path, nor by the noble truths, nor by the meditative concentrations, nor by the immeasurables, nor by the formless attainments, nor by the liberations, nor by the serial attainments, nor by the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness,
signlessness, and wishlessness, nor by the superknowledges, nor by the meditative absorptions, nor by the gateways of dhāraṇī, nor by the powers of a Tathāgata, nor by the grounds of self-confidence.
They will never be devoid of the analytical knowledges or the unique qualities of a Buddha;
they will never be reborn in the hells, nor in the animal realm, nor in the world of Yama.
Except by the power of his own vow, he will bring sentient beings to maturity;
he shall never be deficient in any limb,
nor shall he ever be reborn in impoverished families.

Whether among the families of bamboo-workers, or among the families of *puṣkasas*, or among the families of leather-workers, *caṇḍālas*, hunters, pig-butchers, or among the families of *śūdras*—endowed at all times with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man—he will be reborn in those world-systems where the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, reside, dwell, and maintain themselves;
he shall never be separated from the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) of a bodhisattva. If he so desires, he will travel from buddha-field to buddha-field.
Traveling from buddhafield to buddhafield to behold, pay homage to, and attend upon the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, he will bring sentient beings to maturity and purify the buddhafield.
Therefore, Kauśika, noble sons or noble daughters who desire this perfection of qualities should take up, maintain, and recite this Perfection of Wisdom.
They should master [these teachings], attend to them with proper mental attention,
and remain never separated from the mind of omniscience;
thus they will be endowed with these qualities pertaining both to the present life and to future lives.
...until they fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
This is the nineteenth chapter in the *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
Then a hundred wandering mendicants of other sects, with the intention of finding fault, approached the place where the Blessed One was staying.
At that time, it occurred to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"This hundred of wandering mendicants from other sects are approaching the place where the Blessed One is, with the intention of finding fault."

"What if I were now to recite that portion of the Perfection of Wisdom which I have received from the Blessed One, so that if those wanderers of other sects should approach me and create an obstacle while the Perfection of Wisdom is being spoken?"
Then Śakra, lord of the gods, recited from memory as much of the Perfection of Wisdom as he had received from the presence of the Blessed One.
Thereupon, those wandering mendicants of other sects, having circumambulated the Blessed One from a great distance, departed by the very same path and by the very same gate as they had come.
Then this thought occurred to the venerable Śāradvatīputra:
"What is the reason that those other sectarians and wandering mendicants, having circumambulated the Blessed One from afar, have departed by that very same path and through that very same gate?
Then the Blessed One, [knowing] with his own mind the thought in the mind of the venerable Śāradvatīputra, said:

Having conceived this reflection, he addressed the Venerable Śāradvatīputra: "Śāradvatīputra, this Perfection of Wisdom was attended to by Śakra, the lord of the gods; therefore, these other-tīrthika wanderers and mendicants have circumambulated it from afar, keeping it far to their right."
By that very path and by that very gate they departed once again;
for, Śāradvatīputra, I do not perceive even a single virtuous quality (*śuklāṅga*) in any of these heterodox wanderers (*caraka*) and mendicants (*parivrājaka*).
All these heterodox mendicants have hostile minds and intend only to find fault; they imagine they can approach this assembly, but I do not perceive anyone, Śāradvatīputra, [who could do so].

In this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation including recluses and brahmins, it is impossible that anyone whose mind is hostile toward this perfection of wisdom, or who approaches it with the intent to find fault, should succeed. Why is that?
Śāradvatīputra, it is because whoever belongs to the realm of the Four Great Kings in this triple-thousand great thousandfold world system...
The sons of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin realms;

the sons of the gods of the Brahmakāyika, Brahmapurohita, and Brahmapārṣadya realms, as well as those of Mahābrahmāṇa; the Ābhāsvara gods of the Ābhā, Parīttābhā, Apramāṇābhā, and Śubha realms; the Śubhakṛtsna gods of the Parīttaśubha, Apramāṇaśubha, and Śubhakṛtsna realms; and the Bṛhat gods of the Bṛha, Parīttabṛha, and Apramāṇabṛha realms.
The Bṛhatphala, Anabhraka, Abṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha gods;
and those who are śrāvakas, those who are pratyekabuddhas, and even those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—all of them have taken up this perfection of wisdom. For what reason?
For it is in this way that they have all emerged from the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Śāradvatīputra, as for those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, the pratyekabuddhas, the bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas in the world systems of the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—
All of them are sustained by this perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

Because all those who exist—even the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of disciples, in the world systems of the southern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—have emerged from this perfection of wisdom.
Pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattva mahāsattvas, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—all these are sustained by this perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because all of them have emerged from the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, as well as the pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas in the world systems of the western direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—
all of them uphold this perfection of wisdom. For what reason?
For it is from the perfection of wisdom that all these have emerged:

even those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of disciples, as well as the Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas who reside in the world systems of the northern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
All of them are sustained by this perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who reside in world systems as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the northeastern direction, have emerged from this very perfection of wisdom.

The Pratyekabuddhas together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—all these are sustained by this Perfection of Wisdom. Why is that?
Because all of them have emerged from the Perfection of Wisdom.

Furthermore, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, as well as the pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas in the world systems of the southeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—
all of them have taken up this perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

For it is thus: all those who have emerged from the perfection of wisdom—including the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of disciples, the Pratyekabuddhas, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, who reside in the world-systems of the south-west direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—all of them are sustained by this perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
For it is from the perfection of wisdom that all these have emerged:

even those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of disciples, as well as the Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas who reside in the world systems of the northwestern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
All of them are sustained by this perfection of wisdom. Why is that?

Because all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of disciples, who reside in the world-systems of the lower direction—as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges—have emerged from the perfection of wisdom.
The pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—all these are sustained by this perfection of wisdom. Why is that?
Because all of them have emerged from the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of śrāvakas, as well as the pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas in the world systems of the upper direction, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā—
all these are sustained by this perfection of wisdom. For what reason?
For it is from the perfection of wisdom that they have all emerged.
Then, indeed, this thought occurred to Māra, the Evil One:

These four assemblies of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, are present here, as are these gods of the desire realm and the form realm. Without doubt, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas will here receive their predictions regarding unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; what if I were now to approach the Blessed One so that he might grant me his vision?
Then Māra the Evil One, having conjured up an army of four divisions, desired to approach the Blessed One.
Then it occurred to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"Ah, this is Māra the Evil One who, having conjured up an army of four divisions, desires to approach the Blessed One."

And as for this array of the fourfold army belonging to Māra, the Evil One— such an array of a fourfold army does not belong to King Bimbisāra, nor to King Prasenajit, nor to the Śākyas, nor to the Licchavis; such is the array of this excellent fourfold body conjured by Māra, the Evil One, over a long period of time.
Furthermore, Māra the Evil One, seeking an opportunity and searching for a vulnerability against the Blessed One, and with the intention of harassing those beings who are correctly applied, thought:
"What if I were to... (ŚsP II-4 63)
"I shall attend to the perfection of wisdom and perform its recitation with mindfulness.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, attended to this perfection of wisdom and performed its recitation with mindfulness.
In whatever manner Śakra, the lord of the gods, recited this Perfection of Wisdom, in that very manner Māra, the Evil One, turned back again by that same path and through that same gate.
Then, in that assembly, the sons of the gods from the realm of the Four Great Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha gods, having manifested divine flowers and garments, remained in the sky above in the air.
They cast [the flowers] toward where the Blessed One was, and they scattered them over where the Blessed One was. And they spoke these words:
"Ah, for a long time indeed has this Perfection of Wisdom been [taught] by the Blessed Ones to the humans of Jambudvīpa, until now it has come to be known as this."

As long as human beings of Jambudvīpa follow the perfection of wisdom, for that long there will be no disappearance of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha; the true Dharma will endure for a long time,
and the Jewel of the Saṅgha will appear in the world.

The distinctive conduct of the bodhisattvas, the mahāsattvas, will be made known; and in whichever direction those sons of good family or daughters of good family shall write down this perfection of wisdom, or preserve it, even having made it into a book, that direction is to be expected as having become filled with light, as being well-protected, and as being free from darkness and obscurity.
"And that direction should be looked forward to by me.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to Śakra, the lord of the gods, and to the sons of the gods from the Heaven of the Thirty-three up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven:
"So it is, Kauśika, so it is! So it is, sons of the gods, so it is!
For as long as humans in Jambudvīpa shall follow this perfection of wisdom..."

Until the disappearance of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and until the long endurance of the True Dharma and the Jewel of the Saṃgha are made known in the world— extending from this trichiliocosm mahāsāhasra world system as far as the world systems in all ten directions— the disappearance of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha will occur.
The long endurance of all dharmas will come to pass; the appearance of the Jewel of the Saṃgha in the world will come to pass;
and the distinguished conduct of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas will be made known.

And in whichever direction those sons of good family or daughters of good family shall write down this Perfection of Wisdom and preserve it, even having made it into a book, that direction is to be expected as having become filled with light, as being well-protected, and as being free from darkness; that direction appears to me as one devoid of gloom.
Then those sons of the gods, having again miraculously produced divine flowers, scattered them over the Blessed One and spoke these words:
"Blessed One, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family shall take up this perfection of wisdom..."
He will uphold, recite, master, and attend to it with wise reflection. Neither Māra nor the deities belonging to Māra’s host who seek an opportunity for attack will find an opening against him.
O Blessed One, we too shall constantly and perpetually provide protection, shelter, and guardianship for that son of good family or daughter of good family. Why is that?

“Blessed One, that son of good family or daughter of good family who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, and attend to this perfection of wisdom in a proper manner— him indeed the Blessed One, the Great Teacher, or one of his [disciples],
will regard. Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One:

"Blessed One, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who will take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and attend to this perfection of wisdom with wise attention will not be endowed with merely inferior roots of virtue."

"Blessed One, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who will take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will possess the mental attention of all the Victors;
and, Blessed One, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will have attended upon many Buddhas."

Moreover, Blessed One, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who will take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and attend to this perfection of wisdom with proper mental attention will be sustained by spiritual friends. Why is that?
Because, Blessed One, it is from this very perfection of wisdom that omniscience is to be sought.
Furthermore, Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom should be sought after in this way:
namely, from omniscience. Why is that?

Because, Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is not other than omniscience, and omniscience is not other than the perfection of wisdom; for the perfection of wisdom and omniscience are not different, they are non-dual and indivisible.
The Blessed One said:

"So it is, Kauśika, so it is. For, Kauśika, the knowledge of all aspects of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones is produced from the perfection of wisdom, and the perfection of wisdom is produced from the knowledge of all aspects. Why is that?"

For in this way, Kauśika, the perfection of wisdom is not other than omniscience, and omniscience is not other than the perfection of wisdom; for the perfection of wisdom and omniscience are non-dual, and this is an indivisible unity. This is the twentieth chapter in the Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines.
Then the venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
“The Blessed One does not proclaim the name of the perfection of giving in such a manner,”
He does not proclaim the name of the perfection of ethical discipline in that way; he does not proclaim the name of the perfection of patience in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of the perfection of vigor in that way.
He does not proclaim the name of the perfection of meditation in that manner,
nor does he proclaim the name of the perfection of wisdom in that manner.
The Blessed One does not proclaim the name of internal emptiness in that manner.
He does not proclaim the name of external emptiness in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of internal-external emptiness in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of the emptiness of emptiness in that way.
He does not proclaim the name of great emptiness in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of ultimate emptiness in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of conditioned emptiness in that way.
He does not proclaim the name of the emptiness of conditioned phenomena in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of absolute emptiness in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of the emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end in that way.
He does not proclaim the name of the emptiness of non-dispersal in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of the emptiness of intrinsic nature in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of the emptiness of all phenomena in that way.

He does not proclaim the name of the emptiness of specific characteristics to such an extent, nor does he proclaim the name of the emptiness of non-apprehension to such an extent, nor does he proclaim the name of the emptiness of non-existence to such an extent.
He does not proclaim the name of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor does he proclaim the name of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
in the same way that he proclaims the name of the perfection of wisdom.
He does not proclaim the names of the applications of mindfulness in that way;
he does not proclaim the names of the right efforts in that way;
he does not proclaim the names of the bases of psychic power in that way.
He does not proclaim the names of the faculties in that manner, nor does he proclaim the names of the powers in that manner,
nor does he proclaim the names of the factors of enlightenment in that manner.
He does not proclaim the name of the noble eightfold path as much as he proclaims the name of the perfection of wisdom; he does not proclaim the name of the noble truths as much as that,
nor does he proclaim the name of the meditative concentrations as much as that.

He does not proclaim the names of the formless attainments in the same way that he proclaims the name of the perfection of wisdom. He does not proclaim the names of the eight gates of liberation in that manner,
nor does he proclaim the names of the nine successive meditative attainments in that manner.

He does not proclaim the names of the doors of liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— in the same way that he proclaims the name of the perfection of wisdom. He does not proclaim the names of the meditative concentrations in that same way.

He does not proclaim the names of the gateways to the dhāraṇīs in the same way that he proclaims the name of the perfection of wisdom. He does not proclaim the names of the ten powers of a Tathāgata in that manner,
nor does he proclaim the names of the four grounds of self-confidence in that manner.
He does not proclaim the name of the four analytical knowledges in that way; he does not proclaim the name of great loving-kindness in that way;
he does not proclaim the name of great compassion in that way.
He does not proclaim the names of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha as much as he proclaims the name of the perfection of wisdom.
The Blessed One said:
Ānanda, the perfection of wisdom is the precursor and the leader of the five perfections, of all the modes of emptiness, of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment,

of the four noble truths, of the four meditative concentrations, of the four immeasurables, of the four formless attainments, of the eight liberations, of the nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling, and of the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.

of the superknowledges, the concentrations, the gateways of mnemonic formulas, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, the analytical knowledges, great loving-kindness, great compassion, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. What do you think, Ānanda? Is a gift that has not been dedicated toward omniscience considered the perfection of giving?
He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, does morality that has not been dedicated toward omniscience constitute the perfection of morality?"
He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, does patience that has not been dedicated toward omniscience become the perfection of patience?"
He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, does vigor that is not dedicated toward omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*) constitute the perfection of vigor (*vīryapāramitā*)?"
He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, does meditation that has not been dedicated toward omniscience constitute the perfection of meditation?"
He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said:
"In that case, does wisdom that has not been dedicated toward omniscience become the perfection of wisdom?"
He said: "Certainly not, Blessed One. However, Blessed One, how does the perfection of giving become the perfection of giving within the knowledge of all aspects?

How, Blessed One, does the perfection of ethical discipline become the perfection of ethical discipline within the knowledge of all aspects? How, Blessed One, does the perfection of patience become the perfection of patience within the knowledge of all aspects?"
How, Blessed One, does the perfection of vigor become the perfection of vigor within the knowledge of all aspects?

How, Blessed One, does the perfection of meditation become the perfection of meditation within the knowledge of all aspects? How, Blessed One, does the perfection of wisdom become the perfection of wisdom within the knowledge of all aspects?
The Blessed One said:

"Ānanda, when dedicated through the yoga of non-duality, the perfection of giving becomes the perfection of giving for the sake of omniscience; when dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension, the perfection of giving becomes the perfection of giving for the sake of omniscience.

When dedicated through the yoga of non-duality, morality becomes the perfection of morality for the sake of omniscience; when dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension, morality becomes the perfection of morality for the sake of omniscience."

Patience dedicated through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of patience for the sake of the knowledge of all aspects; patience dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension becomes the perfection of patience for the sake of the knowledge of all aspects;
vigor dedicated through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of vigor for the sake of the knowledge of all aspects.
Vigor dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension becomes the perfection of vigor for the sake of the knowledge of all aspects;

meditation dedicated through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of meditation for the sake of the knowledge of all aspects; and meditation dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension becomes the perfection of meditation for the sake of the knowledge of all aspects.

Wisdom dedicated through the yoga of non-duality becomes the perfection of wisdom in the state of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*). Wisdom dedicated through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension [becomes the perfection of wisdom in the state of omniscience].
He asked: "Blessed One, how does a gift dedicated through the yoga of non-duality become the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) in the state of omniscience?
How [does it become so] through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension?"
“Blessed One, how does morality dedicated by means of non-duality become the perfection of morality in omniscience?
How [does it become so] by means of the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension?
Blessed One, how does patience dedicated by means of non-duality become the perfection of patience in omniscience?”
How is it through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension?
Blessed One, how does diligence dedicated by means of the yoga of non-duality become the perfection of diligence for the sake of the knowledge of all aspects?
How is it through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension?
"How, Blessed One, does meditation transformed by means of non-duality become the perfection of meditation in the context of the knowledge of all aspects?
How [is this] through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension?
How, Blessed One, does wisdom transformed by means of non-duality [become the perfection of wisdom] in the context of the knowledge of all aspects?"
How does the perfection of wisdom come to be?
How is it through the yoga of non-arising and the yoga of non-apprehension?

through the application of non-duality to feeling, and through the application of non-duality to perception,

by means of the non-duality of consciousness,
and by means of the non-duality of the eye.

Through the non-dual application of the body,
through the non-dual application of the mind,
and through the non-dual application of form.
through the non-dual application of sound, through the non-dual application of odor, and through the non-dual application of taste;
Through the non-dual application of contact,
through the non-dual application of phenomena,
and through the non-dual application of eye-consciousness.

through the application of non-duality to auditory consciousness, through the application of non-duality to olfactory consciousness, and through the application of non-duality to gustatory consciousness;

through the yoga of non-duality of mind-consciousness, and through the yoga of non-duality of eye-contact.

by way of the non-duality of the water element, by way of the non-duality of the fire element,

through the yoga of non-duality with the element of consciousness,

through the application of non-duality to the formative forces,

through the non-dual application of the emptiness of the unconditioned,

by means of the non-dual application of the right exertions,

[This is] by way of the non-dual yoga of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

How is there the application of non-duality to the six sense bases?
How is there the application of non-duality to contact?
How is there the application of non-duality to feeling?
How is there the application of non-duality to craving?
How is there the application of non-duality to grasping?
How is there the application of non-duality to becoming?
How is there the application of non-duality to birth?
How is there the yoga of non-duality regarding old age and death?
How is there the yoga of non-duality regarding the perfection of generosity?
How is there the yoga of non-duality regarding the perfection of ethical discipline?
How [is there] the non-dual application of the perfection of patience? How [is there] the non-dual application of the perfection of vigor?
How [is there] the non-dual application of the perfection of meditative concentration?
How is it through the non-dual application of the perfection of wisdom? How is it through the non-dual application of internal emptiness,
and how is it through the non-dual application of external emptiness?
How is there the yoga of non-duality with internal-external emptiness?
How is there the yoga of non-duality with the emptiness of emptiness? How is there the yoga of non-duality with great emptiness?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of the ultimate?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of the conditioned?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of the unconditioned?
How is it through the non-dual application of absolute emptiness?
How is it through the non-dual application of the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end?
How is it through the non-dual application of the emptiness of non-dispersal?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of intrinsic nature?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of all phenomena?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of specific characteristics?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of non-apprehension?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of non-existence?
How is there the non-dual application of the emptiness of intrinsic nature?
How is there the non-dual application regarding the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence?
How is there the non-dual application regarding the applications of mindfulness,
and how is there the non-dual application regarding the right efforts?
How is it through the application of non-duality regarding the bases of psychic power?
How is it through the application of non-duality regarding the faculties?
How is it through the non-dual application of the powers?
How is it through the non-dual application of the factors of enlightenment?
How is it through the non-dual application of the noble eightfold path?
How is there the application of non-duality to the noble truths?
How is there the application of non-duality to the meditative absorptions?
How is there the application of non-duality to the immeasurables?
How is it that the formless attainments are through the yoga of non-duality?
How are the eight liberations through the yoga of non-duality?
How are the serial attainments of meditative dwelling through the yoga of non-duality?
How is it through the non-dual application of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
how is it through the non-dual application of the superknowledges;
and how is it through the non-dual application of the meditative concentrations?
How, through the yoga of non-duality, are the gateways of the dhāraṇīs [to be understood]?
How, through the yoga of non-duality, are the ten powers of a Tathāgata [to be understood]?
How, through the yoga of non-duality, are the four grounds of self-confidence [to be understood]?
How, by means of the yoga of non-duality, are the four analytical knowledges [attained]?
How, by means of the yoga of non-duality, is great loving-kindness [attained]?
How, by means of the yoga of non-duality, is great compassion [attained]?
How is it that the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are through the application of non-duality?
How is it that the fruit of stream-entry is through the application of non-duality?
How is it that the fruit of once-returning is through the application of non-duality?
How is there the application of non-duality to the fruit of the non-returner?
How is there the application of non-duality to arhatship?
How is there the application of non-duality to individual enlightenment?
How is there a non-dual application regarding the knowledge of the aspects of the path;
how is there a non-dual application regarding the knowledge of all aspects; and how is there a non-dual application regarding unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment?
For form is empty of form. Why is that?
Because form and the perfection [of wisdom] are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Feeling is empty of feeling. Why is that?
For in this way, feeling and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Perception is empty of perception. Why is that?
For in this way, perception and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Formations are empty of formations. Why is that?
Because formations and the perfection [of wisdom] are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Consciousness is empty of consciousness. Why is that?
For in this way, consciousness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The eye is empty of the eye. Why is that?
For in this way, the eye and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The ear is empty of the ear. Why is that?
Because the ear and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The nose is empty of the nose. Why is that?
For in this way, the nose and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The tongue is empty of the tongue. Why is that?
For in this way, the tongue and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The body is empty of the body. Why is that? Because the body and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The mind is empty of the mind. Why is that?
For in this way, emptiness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Form is empty of form. Why is that?
Because form and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Sound is empty of sound; for what reason?
Because sound and the perfection are non-dual, this being an indivisible unity.
Odor is empty of odor; for what reason?
For in this way, fragrance and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Taste is empty of taste. Why is that? For in this way, taste and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Contact is empty of contact. Why is that?
Because contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two, for phenomena are empty of phenomena. Why is that?
For in this way, the dharmas and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Eye-consciousness is empty of eye-consciousness. Why is that?
For in this way, eye-consciousness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Auditory consciousness is empty of auditory consciousness. Why is that?
Because auditory consciousness and the perfection [of wisdom] are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Olfactory consciousness is empty of olfactory consciousness. Why is that?
For in this way, olfactory consciousness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Tongue-consciousness is empty of tongue-consciousness. Why is that?
For in this way, tongue-consciousness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Body-consciousness is empty of body-consciousness. Why is that?
Because body-consciousness and the perfection (pāramitā) are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Mind-consciousness is empty of mind-consciousness. Why is that?
For in this way, mental consciousness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Eye-contact is empty of eye-contact. Why is that?
For in this way, eye-contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Auditory contact is empty of auditory contact. Why is that?
Because auditory contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Olfactory contact is empty of olfactory contact. Why is that?
For in this way, olfactory contact and the perfection are non-dual and indivisible;
gustatory contact is empty of gustatory contact. Why is that?
For in this way, tongue-contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Body-contact is empty of body-contact. Why is that?
For in this way, body-contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Mental contact is empty of mental contact. Why is that?
Because mental contact and the perfection [of wisdom] are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Feeling conditioned by visual contact is empty of feeling conditioned by visual contact. Why is that?
For in this way, the feeling conditioned by eye-contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The feeling conditioned by ear-contact is empty of the feeling conditioned by ear-contact. Why is that?
For in this way, the sensation conditioned by auditory contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The sensation conditioned by olfactory contact is empty of the sensation conditioned by olfactory contact. Why is that?
For in this way, the sensation conditioned by olfactory contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Feeling conditioned by tongue-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by tongue-contact. Why is that?
Because feeling conditioned by tongue-contact and the perfection [of wisdom] are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Feeling conditioned by body-contact is empty of feeling conditioned by body-contact. Why is that?
For in this way, the feeling conditioned by bodily contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The feeling conditioned by mental contact is empty of the feeling conditioned by mental contact. Why is that?
For in this way, the feeling conditioned by mental contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The earth element is empty of the earth element. Why is that? Because the earth element and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The water element is empty of the water element. Why is that?
For thus, the water element and the perfection are non-dual; this is not a state of duality.
The fire element is empty of the fire element. Why is that?
For thus, the fire element and the perfection are non-dual; this is not a state of duality.
The wind element is empty of the wind element. For what reason?
Because the wind element and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The space element is empty of the space element. For what reason?
For thus, the element of space and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The element of consciousness is empty of the element of consciousness. Why is that?
For thus, the element of consciousness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Ignorance is empty of ignorance. For what reason?
Because ignorance and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Formations are empty of formations. For what reason?
For in this way, the formative forces and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Consciousness is empty of consciousness. Why is that?
For in this way, consciousness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Name-and-form is empty of name-and-form. Why is that?
Because name-and-form and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The six sense bases are empty of the six sense bases. Why is that?
For in this way, the six sense bases and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Contact is empty of contact. Why is that?
For in this way, contact and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Feeling is empty of feeling. For what reason?
Because feeling and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Craving is empty of craving. For what reason?
For in this way, craving and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Appropriation is empty of appropriation. Why is that?
For in this way, appropriation and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Existence is empty of existence. Why is that?
Because existence and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two. Birth is empty of birth. Why is that?
Because birth and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Old age and death are empty of old age and death. Why is that?
Because name-and-form and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Internal emptiness is empty of internal emptiness. Why is that?
For thus, internal emptiness and the perfection are non-dual; this is an undivided unity.
External emptiness is empty of external emptiness. Why is that?
For thus, external emptiness and the perfection are non-dual; this is an undivided unity.
Internal-external emptiness is empty of internal-external emptiness. For what reason?
Because internal-external emptiness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Emptiness of emptiness is empty of emptiness of emptiness. For what reason?
For emptiness and the emptiness of emptiness, as well as the perfection, are non-dual and not divided into two;
the great emptiness is empty of the great emptiness. Why is that?
For the great emptiness and the perfection are non-dual and not divided into two.
Ultimate emptiness is empty of ultimate emptiness. Why is that?
Because ultimate emptiness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Conditioned emptiness is empty of conditioned emptiness. Why is that?
For thus, conditioned emptiness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two, because unconditioned emptiness is empty of unconditioned emptiness. Why is that?
For thus, unconditioned emptiness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Absolute emptiness is empty of absolute emptiness. For what reason?
Because absolute emptiness and the perfection are non-dual and cannot be divided.
Emptiness without beginning or end is empty of emptiness without beginning or end. For what reason?
For thus, the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The emptiness of non-dispersal is empty of the emptiness of non-dispersal. Why is that?
For thus, the emptiness of non-dispersal and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Why is that?
Because the emptiness of intrinsic nature and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The emptiness of all phenomena is empty of the emptiness of all phenomena. Why is that?

For thus, the emptiness of all dharmas and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two, for the emptiness of specific characteristics is empty of the emptiness of specific characteristics. Why is that?
For thus, the emptiness of specific characteristics and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.

The emptiness of non-apprehension is empty of the emptiness of non-apprehension. Why is that? Because the emptiness of non-apprehension and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two, as they are the emptiness of non-existence.
It is empty by way of the emptiness of non-existence. Why is that?

Because the emptiness of non-existence and the perfection (pāramitā) are non-dual; they are not divided into two, for the emptiness of intrinsic nature is empty by way of the emptiness of intrinsic nature. Why is that?
For thus, intrinsic-nature emptiness and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is empty by virtue of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence. Why is that?
For thus, emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The foundations of mindfulness are empty of the foundations of mindfulness. Why is that?
Because the foundations of mindfulness and the perfections are fundamentally non-dual.
The right efforts are empty of the right efforts. Why is that?
For in this way, the right efforts and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The bases of psychic power are empty of the bases of psychic power. Why is that?
For in this way, the bases of psychic power and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The sense faculties are empty of sense faculties. Why is that? Because the sense faculties and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The powers are empty of powers. Why is that?
For indeed, the powers and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The factors of enlightenment are empty of the factors of enlightenment. Why is that?
For indeed, the factors of enlightenment and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The path is empty of the path. For what reason? Because the path and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The noble truths are empty of the noble truths. For what reason?
For in this way, the noble truths and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two, as the meditative concentrations are empty of meditative concentrations. Why is that?
Because the meditative concentrations and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The immeasurables are empty of the immeasurables. Why is that?
Because the immeasurables and the perfections are non-dual and cannot be divided;
the formless attainments are empty of the formless attainments. Why is that?
For in this way, the formless attainments and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two, as the liberations are empty of liberations. Why is that?
Because the liberations and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The successive attainments of meditative dwelling are empty of the successive attainments of meditative dwelling. Why is that?
Because the successive attainments of meditative dwelling and the perfections are non-dual and not divided;
the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are empty of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. Why is that?
For emptiness, the signless, and the wishless—the gateways to liberation—and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The superknowledges are empty of superknowledges. Why is that?
Because the superknowledges and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.

The concentrations are empty of concentrations. Why is that? Because the concentrations and the perfections are non-dual and not divided; the doors of dhāraṇī are empty of the doors of dhāraṇī. Why is that? Because... (ŚsP_II-4_76)
The gateways of dhāraṇī and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The ten powers of a Tathāgata are empty of the ten powers of a Tathāgata. Why is that?
Because the ten powers of a Tathāgata and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The grounds of self-confidence are empty of the grounds of self-confidence. Why is that?
Because the grounds of self-confidence and the perfections are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The analytical knowledges are empty of the analytical knowledges. Why is that?
For indeed, the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) and the perfections (*pāramitā*) are non-dual; this is not a state of duality, for great compassion is empty of great compassion. Why is that?

For indeed, great compassion and the perfections are non-dual; this is not a state of duality, and the unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇikabuddhadharma*) are empty of the unique qualities of a Buddha. Why is that?
For thus, the unique qualities of a Buddha and the perfections are non-dual and not divided;
the fruit of stream-entry is empty of the fruit of stream-entry. Why is that?
For thus, the fruit of stream-entry and the perfections are non-dual and not divided.
The fruit of once-returning is empty of the fruit of once-returning. Why is that?
Because the fruit of once-returning and the perfection are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
The fruit of non-returning is empty of the fruit of non-returning. Why is that?
For thus, the fruit of non-returning and the perfection are non-dual; this is not a state of duality.
Arhatship is empty of arhatship. Why is that?
For thus, arhatship and the perfection are non-dual; this is not a state of duality.
Pratyekabodhi is empty of pratyekabodhi. For what reason?
Because pratyekabodhi and the perfection (pāramitā) are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Mārgākārajñatā is empty of mārgākārajñatā. For what reason?

For in this way, the knowledge of the aspects of the path and the perfection are non-dual; they are not two and cannot be divided. Unsurpassed perfect enlightenment is empty of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Why is that?
For in this way, the bodhisattva and the perfection are non-dual; they are not two and cannot be divided.
Therefore, Ānanda, the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor to these five perfections;

the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor to all the modes of emptiness; the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor to the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment; the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor to the four noble truths; [the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor] to the four...
For the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*), the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor; for the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*), the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor;

for the four formless attainments (*ārūpyasamāpatti*), the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor; for the eight liberations (*vimokṣa*), the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor; for the nine successive attainments (*anupūrvavihārasamāpatti*), the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor; and for the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness (*śūnyatā-nimitta-apraṇihita-vimokṣamukha*).
The perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor of the superknowledges; the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor of the meditative concentrations;
the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor of all the gateways of dhāraṇīs.

Of the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor; of the four grounds of self-confidence, the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor; of the four analytical insights, the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor.
For great loving-kindness, the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor; for great compassion, the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor;
for the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor.
For omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor;
for the knowledge of the aspects of the path (*mārgākārajñatā*), the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor;
for the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*), the perfection of wisdom alone is the precursor.
It is just as if, Ānanda, seeds scattered upon the great earth were to grow when they obtain the necessary conditions;
for their support is the great earth, and it is because they are supported by the great earth that those seeds sprout.
In the very same way, these five perfections grow with the perfection of wisdom as their support.
Internal emptiness grows; external emptiness grows;
internal-external emptiness grows.
The emptiness of emptiness grows; the great emptiness grows;
the emptiness of the ultimate truth grows.
The emptiness of the conditioned grows; the emptiness of the unconditioned grows;
the absolute emptiness grows.
The emptiness of that which has no beginning or end arises;
the emptiness of non-dispersal arises;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature arises.
The emptiness of all phenomena arises; the emptiness of specific characteristics arises;
the emptiness of non-apprehension arises.
The emptiness of non-existence arises;
the emptiness of intrinsic nature arises; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence arises.
The foundations of mindfulness grow;
the right efforts grow;
the bases of psychic power grow.
The faculties grow, the powers grow, and the factors of enlightenment grow.
The noble eightfold path grows; the noble truths grow;
the meditative absorptions grow.
The immeasurables grow;
the formless attainments grow;
the eight liberations grow.
The nine successive attainments of meditative dwelling flourish;
the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—flourish;
and the superknowledges flourish.
The concentrations flourish; the gateways of dhāraṇī flourish; the ten powers of a Tathāgata flourish.
The four fearlessnesses grow, the four analytical knowledges grow,
and great loving-kindness grows.
Great compassion grows;
the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha grow;
omniscience grows.
The knowledge of the aspects of the path grows,
and the knowledge of all aspects grows.
Furthermore, Ānanda, it is by being established in the knowledge of all aspects that the five perfections grow.
All the emptinesses grow forth established in the knowledge of all aspects; the four foundations of mindfulness grow forth established in the knowledge of all aspects;
the four right efforts grow forth established in the knowledge of all aspects.
The four bases of psychic power grow established in omniscience;
the five faculties grow established in omniscience;
the five powers grow established in omniscience.
The seven factors of enlightenment grow established in omniscience; the noble eightfold path grows established in omniscience;
