the four noble truths grow established in omniscience.
The four dhyānas, not abiding in all-aspect omniscience, grow;
the four immeasurables, not abiding in all-aspect omniscience, grow; the four formless attainments, not abiding in all-aspect omniscience, grow.
The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—grow forth established in omniscience;
all meditative concentrations grow forth established in omniscience;
and all gateways to the dhāraṇīs grow forth established in omniscience.
The ten powers of a Tathāgata grow while being established in the knowledge of all aspects; the four grounds of self-confidence grow while being established in the knowledge of all aspects;
and the four analytical knowledges grow while being established in the knowledge of all aspects.
Great loving-kindness grows, established in the knowledge of all aspects; great compassion grows, established in the knowledge of all aspects;
and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha grow, established in the knowledge of all aspects.
All-knowledge grows by being established in the knowledge of all aspects;
the knowledge of the paths grows by being established in the knowledge of all aspects; and the knowledge of all aspects grows by being established in the knowledge of all aspects.
Therefore, Ānanda, the perfection of wisdom alone is the leader of these five perfections; it is the leader of all the emptinesses;
it is the leader of the four foundations of mindfulness.
She is the guide of the four right efforts, the guide of the four bases of psychic power,
and the guide of the five faculties.
She is the leader of the five powers,
the leader of the seven factors of enlightenment,
and the leader of the noble eightfold path.
It is the guide to the four noble truths, the guide to the four meditative concentrations,
and the guide to the four immeasurables.
It is the guide to the four formless attainments,
the guide to the eight liberations,
and the guide to the nine successive meditative attainments.
It is the guide to the doors of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
it is the guide to the superknowledges;
it is the guide to the meditative concentrations.
It is the guide to the gateways of dhāraṇīs, the guide to the ten powers of a Tathāgata,
and the guide to the four grounds of self-confidence.
She is the guide of the four analytical knowledges,
the guide of great loving-kindness, and the guide of great compassion.
It is the guide to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
it is the guide to omniscience;
it is the guide to the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
It is the guide to the knowledge of all modes.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“Blessed One, all the qualities of the perfection of wisdom have not been fully proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly awakened Buddha, which have been taken up, retained, and recited by me in the presence of the Blessed One; yet that son of good family or daughter of good family will acquire those very qualities by taking up, retaining, reciting, and mastering this perfection of wisdom.”

And attending to it with wise reflection, O Blessed One, those qualities of this perfection of wisdom which I have grasped, mastered, retained, recited, and set forth in the presence of the Blessed One— by that perfection of wisdom having been grasped, retained, recited, mastered, set forth, and attended to with wise reflection, there is [the fulfillment] of the ten paths of wholesome action.
The manifestation of these occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the five superknowledges occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four immeasurables occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the four formless attainments occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the perfection of generosity occurs in the world; the manifestation of the perfection of ethical discipline occurs in the world.
The perfection of patience appears in the world; the perfection of vigor appears in the world;
the perfection of meditation appears in the world.
The perfection of wisdom appears in the world.
The emptiness of the internal appears in the world;
the emptiness of the external appears in the world.
The appearance of internal-and-external emptiness occurs in the world;
the appearance of the emptiness of emptiness occurs in the world; the appearance of great emptiness occurs in the world.
The emptiness of the ultimate meaning appears in the world; the emptiness of the conditioned appears in the world;
the emptiness of the unconditioned appears in the world.
The manifestation of absolute emptiness occurs in the world; the manifestation of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of non-dispersal occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of all phenomena occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of specific characteristics occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the emptiness of non-apprehension occurs in the world; the manifestation of the emptiness of non-existence occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature occurs in the world.
The emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence appears in the world.
The four foundations of mindfulness appear in the world;
the four right efforts appear in the world.
The manifestation of the four bases of psychic power occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the five faculties occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the five powers occurs in the world.
The appearance of the seven factors of awakening occurs in the world;
the appearance of the noble eightfold path occurs in the world;
the appearance of the four noble truths occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the four dhyānas occurs in the world;
she is the guide for the four immeasurables;
and the manifestation of the four formless attainments occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the eight liberations occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the nine successive meditative attainments occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the superknowledges occurs in the world;
and the manifestation of all meditative concentrations occurs in the world.
The manifestation of all the gateways of dhāraṇīs occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the ten powers of a Tathāgata occurs in the world; the manifestation of the four grounds of self-confidence occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the four analytical knowledges occurs in the world; the manifestation of great loving-kindness occurs in the world;
the manifestation of great compassion occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha occurs in the world.

Blessed One, through the perfection of wisdom being taken up, maintained, recited, mastered, set in motion, and correctly attended to, there occurs the manifestation of great kshatriya clans in the world, and the manifestation of great brahmin clans in the world.
The appearance of great wealthy householder families occurs in the world; the gods of the Realm of the Four Great Kings become known in the world,
and the Trāyastriṃśa gods become known in the world.
The Yāma gods are known in the world;
the Tuṣita gods are known in the world;
the Nirmāṇarati gods are known in the world.
The Paranirmitavaśavartin gods are known in the world;
the Brahmakāyika gods are known in the world;
the Brahmapurohita gods are known in the world.
The Brahmā-pārṣadya gods are known in the world;
the Mahābrahmā gods are known in the world;
the Ābhāsvara gods are known in the world; and the Parīttābha gods are known in the world.
The gods of Infinite Light are known in the world; the gods of Radiant Purity are known in the world;
the gods of Purity are known in the world.
The Parīttāśubha gods are known in the world; the Apramāṇaśubha gods are known in the world;
the Śubhakṛtsna gods are known in the world.
In the world, the Bṛhat devas are known;
the Parīttabṛhat devas are known in the world; and the Apramāṇabṛhat devas are known in the world.
The Bṛhatphala gods are known in the world;
the Abṛha gods are known in the world;
the Atapa gods are known in the world.
In the world, the Sudṛśa gods are known; in the world, the Sudarśana gods are known;
in the world, the Akaniṣṭha gods are known.
“Blessed One, it is through the perfection of wisdom— when it has been taken up, maintained, recited, mastered, set in motion, and properly attended to— that stream-enterers are known in the world,
once-returners are known in the world,
and non-returners are known in the world.”
Arhats are known in the world; pratyekabuddhas are known in the world;
bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, are known in the world.

"O Blessed One, through the Perfection of Wisdom being taken up, maintained, recited, mastered, set in motion, and correctly attended to, there is the manifestation of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, in the world. The Blessed One said:

Furthermore, Kauśika, I do not speak of these very qualities for that son of good family or daughter of good family by whom this perfection of wisdom will have been taken up, maintained, recited, mastered, and properly attended to with right reflection. Why is that?

Kauśika, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who will take up, maintain, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will be endowed with an immeasurable mass of ethical discipline.
They will never be separated from the mind of omniscience;

those sons of good family and daughters of good family who take up, uphold, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will be endowed with an immeasurable aggregate of meditative concentration.
They will never be separated from the mind of omniscience;

those sons of good family and daughters of good family who take up, maintain, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will be endowed with an immeasurable aggregate of wisdom.
They will never be separated from the mind of omniscience;

those sons of good family and daughters of good family who take up, maintain, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will be endowed with the immeasurable aggregate of liberation.
They will never be separated from the mind of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatācitta*);

those sons of good family and daughters of good family who take up, maintain, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) will be endowed with the immeasurable aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha*).
And they will never be separated from the mind of omniscience.

Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom should be known as having set out toward the state of a Tathāgata.
And they will never be separated from the mind of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Moreover, Kauśika, whatever aggregate of ethical discipline, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, and aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation belongs to all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and whatever aggregate of ethical discipline belongs to those sons of good family or daughters of good family—

The aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation. Kauśika, compared to this aggregate of morality, this aggregate of concentration, this aggregate of wisdom, this aggregate of liberation, and this aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, the aggregate of morality, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas do not even amount to a hundredth part.
It does not approach a [mere] portion;
it does not approach even a thousandth part,
nor does it approach even a hundred-thousandth part.
It does not approach even a ten-millionth part, it does not approach even a hundred-ten-millionth part,
nor does it approach even a thousand-ten-millionth part.
It does not approach even a hundred-thousandth part of it,
nor even a hundred-thousand-billionth part of it; it does not even admit of calculation, nor does it approach a fraction thereof.
It does not approach even a fraction of a comparison, nor can it bear even a slight resemblance. Why is that?
Because the minds of those sons of good family and daughters of good family have been liberated from the levels of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

Furthermore, Kauśika, there is no dharma whatsoever that has been fully understood; yet those sons of good family or daughters of good family who, having written down this perfection of wisdom, shall take it up, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection, and who shall honor, revere, esteem, and worship it— [they shall gain great merit].
With flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags,

and with various musical instruments— O son of good family, for those sons and daughters of good family, I declare these very same qualities, both pertaining to this present life and pertaining to future lives.

Śakra said: "O Blessed One, I too shall constantly and perpetually provide protection, shelter, and defense for that son of good family or daughter of good family who will take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom;
who will not be separated from the mind of omniscience; and who, having written down this perfection of wisdom, will honor, revere, and worship it."
With flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of musical instruments.
The Blessed One said:
Furthermore, Kauśika, for that son of good family or daughter of good family who is reciting this Perfection of Wisdom, [there will be such honors].
Many thousands of sons of the gods will approach to hear the Dharma from the mind. Furthermore,

as that son of good family or daughter of good family teaches the Dharma connected with the perfection of wisdom, those sons of the gods will consider it their duty to provide him with inspired eloquence.
Furthermore, Kauśika, even if those Dharma-preachers should have some desire for this,
the sons of the gods will think that eloquence should be bestowed upon them out of that very reverence for the Dharma;
that son of good family or daughter of good family, Kauśika, will also acquire this quality pertaining to the present life.
Whoever shall take up this perfection of wisdom, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection; and whoever, having written it down, shall honor, revere, esteem,
and worship it with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, and parasols—
With banners, flags, and various musical instruments.

Furthermore, Kauśika, as this son of good family or daughter of good family speaks this perfection of wisdom before the fourfold assembly, they will be unshakable, thinking: "Someone will question me and find fault with me. Why is that?
For this is how it will be: this perfection of wisdom will provide protection, defense, and shelter for that son of good family or daughter of good family. Why is that?

Because herein, within this perfection of wisdom, all dharmas are undifferentiated—whether mundane or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows, common or wholesome, unwholesome, conditioned or unconditioned, and even the dharmas of the śrāvakas.
And the dharmas of the pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of the bodhisattvas, and the dharmas of the buddhas. For what reason?
Because this is the treasury of all wholesome dharmas;
and that son of good family or daughter of good family—
Abiding in internal emptiness, abiding in external emptiness, abiding in internal and external emptiness,
abiding in the emptiness of emptiness, abiding in great emptiness, and abiding in the emptiness of the ultimate.

He abides in the emptiness of the conditioned, he abides in the emptiness of the unconditioned, he abides in absolute emptiness, he abides in the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end, he abides in the emptiness of non-dispersal,
he abides in the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and he abides in the emptiness of all phenomena.
Abiding in the emptiness of specific characteristics, abiding in the emptiness of non-apprehension, abiding in the emptiness of non-existence,

abiding in the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and abiding in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence— he, abiding in the perfection of wisdom which is free from apprehension, does not perceive anyone who even apprehends.
He does not perceive even that perfection of wisdom,

nor does he perceive him who reproaches it. In this way, O Kauśika, for that son of good family or daughter of good family who has grasped the perfection of wisdom, there is no one else whatsoever who can [reproach] that son of good family or daughter of good family as they grasp this perfection of wisdom.
For one who upholds, recites, masters, and attends to it with wise reflection, the mind will not waver, will not be terrified, will not be frightened, and will not fall into terror. Why is that?
Because that son of good family or daughter of good family does not perceive any objective entity.

Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family who will take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and properly attend to this perfection of wisdom will acquire these qualities pertaining to the present life— [qualities] by which one might otherwise become discouraged, cowed, terrified, utterly terrified, or fall into terror.
And having written it down, he will honor, revere, respect,
and worship it with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of musical instruments.
Furthermore, Kauśika, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family shall take up this perfection of wisdom, bear it in mind, recite it, master it, and attend to it with wise reflection,
and having written it down, shall honor it, revere it, and respect it—
He will worship with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags,
and various kinds of musical instruments. He will become dear to his parents, friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood relations.

He will be dear to kings, royal ministers, śramaṇas, and brahmins; and he will also be dear to those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, pratyekabuddhas, arhats, anāgāmins, sakṛdāgāmins, and srotaāpannas who reside in the world systems of the ten directions.
He will be pleasing to the world including its gods, its Brahmās, and its generation of śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas, including gods, humans, and asuras;
he will be beloved and possess an uninterrupted eloquence.
His perfection of generosity will be uninterrupted.
The perfection of ethical discipline will be uninterrupted; the perfection of patience will be uninterrupted;
the perfection of vigor will be uninterrupted.
The perfection of meditation will be uninterrupted;
the perfection of wisdom will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of internal emptiness will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of external emptiness will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of internal-external emptiness will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the emptiness of emptiness will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of the great emptiness will be uninterrupted; the cultivation of the emptiness of the ultimate truth will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the emptiness of the conditioned will be uninterrupted.
There will be the cultivation of the unassailable emptiness of the unconditioned;
there will be the cultivation of the unassailable ultimate emptiness; there will be the cultivation of the unassailable emptiness of that which has neither beginning nor end.
There will be the uninterrupted cultivation of the emptiness of non-dispersal; there will be the uninterrupted cultivation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
there will be the uninterrupted cultivation of the emptiness of all phenomena.
The cultivation of the emptiness of specific characteristics will be uninterrupted; the cultivation of the emptiness of non-apprehension will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the emptiness of non-existence will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature will be uninterrupted; the cultivation of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence will be uninterrupted.
Furthermore, his cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of the four right efforts will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the four bases of psychic power will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the five faculties will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of the five powers will be uninterrupted; the cultivation of the seven factors of enlightenment will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the noble eightfold path will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of the four noble truths will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the four dhyānas will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of the four immeasurables will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the four formless attainments will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the eight liberations will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of the nine successive meditative attainments will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—will be uninterrupted;
and the cultivation of the superknowledges will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of meditative concentration will be uninterrupted; the cultivation of the gateways of dhāraṇī will be uninterrupted;
and the cultivation of the ten powers of a Tathāgata will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of the four grounds of self-confidence will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the four analytical knowledges will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of great loving-kindness will be uninterrupted.
The cultivation of great compassion will be uninterrupted;
the cultivation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha will be uninterrupted.
Furthermore, his ripening of sentient beings will be uninterrupted, and the purification of his buddha-field will be uninterrupted.

Furthermore, his omniscience shall become indestructible, and he will be capable of providing, in accordance with the Dharma, the means of deliverance for every successive inquiry that arises before him; this son of good family or daughter of good family who takes up, retains, and recites this perfection of wisdom will also acquire these qualities pertaining to the present life.
He will master it, attend to it with wise reflection, and remain never separated from the mind of omniscience;

and having written it down, he will honor, revere, respect, and worship it with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and various kinds of musical instruments.

Furthermore, Kauśika, if any son of good family or daughter of good family, having made this Perfection of Wisdom into a book, should preserve it, then, Kauśika, those sons of the gods belonging to the assembly of the Four Great Kings in this trichiliocosm who have set out for unsurpassed,
perfect enlightenment— those of the Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin [heavens]— [will all come to that place].

The gods of the Brahma-realm, the gods who are ministers of Brahmā, the gods who are the retinue of Brahmā, the Great Brahmas; the Ābhāsvara gods, the Parīttābha, the Apramāṇābha, and the Ābhāsvara gods; the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha, the Apramāṇaśubha, and the Śubhakṛtsna gods; the Bṛha gods, the Parīttabṛha, the Apramāṇabṛha, and the Bṛhatphala gods—all of whom have set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Having come there, they will think that after reading, taking up, mastering, bowing to, and paying homage to this Perfection of Wisdom, they should depart once again. Those gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host— the Abṛhas, Atapas, Sudṛśas, Sudarśanas, and Akaniṣṭhas— they too,
having come there, will think that after reading, taking up, mastering, bowing to, and paying homage to this Perfection of Wisdom, they should depart once again.

In that regard, Kauśika, those sons of the gods belonging to the assembly of the Four Great Kings in the world-systems of the ten directions who have set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment—those of the Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, and Paranirmitavaśavartin heavens;
the gods of the Brahma-kāyika, Brahma-purohita, Brahma-pārṣadya, and Mahābrahmā realms; and those of the Ābhā, Parīttābhā, and Apramāṇābhā heavens—[all these].

The Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, the Apramāṇaśubha gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Bṛha gods, the Parīttabṛha gods, the Apramāṇabṛha gods, and the Bṛhatphala gods who have set out for unexcelled perfect enlightenment;
as well as those gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host— the Abṛha, Atapa, Sudṛśa, Sudarśana, and Akaniṣṭha gods— [all these have come].

Furthermore, those other beings of great majesty— the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas— will come there, and having recited, taken up, mastered, saluted, and paid homage to this perfection of wisdom, they will think it right to depart once again.
In that regard, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family should generate this thought:

"Those sons of the gods belonging to the retinue of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa, Yāma, Tuṣita, Nirmāṇarati, Paranirmitavaśavartin, Brahmakāyika, and Brahmapurohita gods who reside in the world-systems in the ten directions..."
The gods of the Retinue of Brahmā, the gods of Mahābrahmā, the Ābhā gods, the Parīttābhā gods, the Apramāṇābhā gods,
the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, the Apramāṇaśubha gods,
the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Bṛha gods, the Parīttabṛha gods, the Apramāṇabṛha gods, and the Bṛhatphala gods.
Those who have set out for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment;
and also those gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa host— the Abṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods—
as well as other powerful and mighty gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.

"May this gift of Dharma be given to those who have come here to recite, memorize, master, worship, and honor this Perfection of Wisdom; and may they, having recited, memorized, mastered, honored, worshipped, and paid homage to this Perfection of Wisdom, depart once again. Furthermore, Kauśika, for that son of good family—

Or, son of good family or daughter of good family, those gods of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapurohita gods, the Brahmapārṣadya gods, and the Mahābrahmā gods who are here in this trichiliocosm;

the Ābhā gods, the Parīttābhā gods, the Apramāṇābhā gods, the Ābhāsvara gods, the Śubha gods, the Parīttaśubha gods, the Apramāṇaśubha gods, the Śubhakṛtsna gods, the Bṛha gods, the Parīttabṛha gods, the Apramāṇabṛha gods, the Bṛhatphala gods, the Abṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods.

Furthermore, those gods belonging to the retinue of the Four Great Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa gods, the Yāma gods, the Tuṣita gods, the Nirmāṇarati gods, the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods, the Brahmakāyika gods, the Brahmapurohita gods, the Brahmapārṣadya gods, the Mahābrahmā gods, the Ābhā gods, and the Parīttābhā gods who dwell in the world systems of the ten directions—
the gods of Immeasurable Light, the gods of Radiant Light, the Pure gods, the Limited-Pure gods, the Immeasurable-Pure gods,
the All-Pure gods, the Vast gods, the Limited-Vast gods, the Immeasurable-Vast gods, and the Vast-Fruit gods.

The Abṛha gods, the Atapa gods, the Sudṛśa gods, the Sudarśana gods, and the Akaniṣṭha gods will provide protection through this supreme Dharma. O Kauśika, no one seeking an opportunity for entry or searching for a vulnerability shall find such an opening against him,
except as a result of the ripening of past karma.
Furthermore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family will also acquire this present-life virtue:

those sons of the gods who have set out for unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment will think, "We should go there," for the sake of honoring this perfection of wisdom and for the protection, defense, and guardianship of that son or daughter of good family. Why is that?

For it is thus, Kauśika: those sons of good family have set out for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment; they have appeared for the sake of protecting all beings and for the sake of the welfare and happiness of all beings.
Śakra said: "Blessed One, how will a son of good family or a daughter of good family recognize that 'the gods belonging to the realm of the Four Great Kings are coming here'?"
Here the Trāyastriṃśa gods come;
here the Yāma gods come;
here the Tuṣita gods come.
Here the Nirmāṇarati gods come;
here the Paranirmitavaśavartin gods come;
here the Brahmakāyika gods come.
Here the gods who are Ministers of Brahmā come;
here the gods who are Retainers of Brahmā come;
here the gods who are Great Brahmās come.
Here the Ābhā devas come; here the Parīttābhā devas come; here the Apramāṇābhā devas come.
Here the Ābhāsvara gods come;
here the Śubha gods come;
here the Parīttaśubha gods come.
Here the Apramāṇaśubha gods come;
here the Śubhakṛtsna gods come;
here the Bṛhat gods come.
Here the Parīttabṛha devas come; here the Apramāṇabṛha devas come;
here the Bṛhatphala devas come.
Here the Abṛha gods come;
here the Atapa gods come;
here the Sudṛśa gods come.
Here the Sudarśana gods come;

here the Akaniṣṭha gods come. From the world-systems of the ten directions all around, they come to recite, take up, master, venerate, pay homage to, honor, revere, respect, and worship this Perfection of Wisdom.
The Blessed One said:

"Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family perceives a sublime radiance wherever this perfection of wisdom has been placed, that son of good family or daughter of good family should conclude: 'These are beings of great renown, of great majesty, possessed of great supernatural power, and of great influence.'"
Deities of great majesty have come here to recite, take up, master, salute, pay homage to, honor, revere, respect, and worship this Perfection of Wisdom.

Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family is pure in their conduct, the deities will come because of that purity of conduct; having approached, they will cause them to recite, memorize, master, revere, honor, respect, and worship this perfection of wisdom, and they will be uplifted in mind.
And those minor deities who dwell in that region will think they should approach him there; being unable to endure the splendor, glory, and majesty of those highly exalted deities,
they will think that they must approach those deities who are more and more highly exalted, possessed of great supernatural power, and of great majesty.
In that way, that son of good family or daughter of good family will possess noble resolve. And around that place, no impure conduct should be practiced;

that son of good family or daughter of good family, for the sake of honoring this perfection of wisdom, should sprinkle that area of ground with scented water, scatter flowers and incense, burn incense pots, hang up silk streamers and cloth canopies, and decorate that area of ground so that it is beautiful to behold.

Furthermore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family will experience no physical exhaustion; rather, that son of good family or daughter of good family will perceive physical ease, physical lightness, and physical flexibility. That son of good family or daughter of good family will also perceive mental ease, mental lightness, and mental flexibility.

And then, as he prepares his bed at night, by directing his intention toward this very *Prajñāpāramitā*, he will not see evil dreams; instead, he will see the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man,
adorned with the eighty secondary characteristics, with a body of golden hue, surrounded by a community of monks.

He will hear the Dharma being taught by that Tathāgata, who is preceded by a host of bodhisattvas; that is to say, he will hear the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom. He will hear [the teachings on] internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, and great emptiness.

Ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness, unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness without beginning or end, non-dispersal emptiness, natural emptiness, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of specific characteristics,
the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.

the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, the noble eightfold path, the noble truths, the meditative absorptions, the immeasurables, the formless attainments, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments,
and the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;

the superknowledges, the concentrations, the doors of dhāraṇī, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, great compassion, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They will hear the meaning of that perfection of generosity being analyzed, and they will hear the meaning of that perfection of ethical discipline being analyzed.
And he will hear the meaning of that perfection of vigor being analyzed;
he will hear the meaning of that perfection of patience being analyzed; and he will hear the meaning of that perfection of meditative concentration being analyzed.
And he will hear the meaning of that perfection of wisdom being analyzed;
he will hear the meaning of its internal emptiness being analyzed; and he will hear the meaning of its external emptiness being analyzed.
And he will hear the meaning of that internal-and-external emptiness being analyzed;
likewise [he will hear it] regarding the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, conditioned emptiness,
unconditioned emptiness, absolute emptiness, emptiness without beginning or end, non-dispersive emptiness, essential emptiness, and the emptiness of all phenomena.

He will hear the meaning of the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, and the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence as it is being analyzed;
and he will hear the meaning of those four applications of mindfulness as it is being analyzed.
And he will hear the meaning of those four right efforts being analyzed;
he will hear the meaning of those four bases of psychic power being analyzed; and he will hear the meaning of those five faculties being analyzed.

He will hear the meaning of these five powers being analyzed; he will hear the meaning of these seven factors of enlightenment being analyzed; and he will hear the meaning of this noble eightfold path being analyzed.
He will hear the meaning of those noble truths being analyzed; he will hear the meaning of those four meditative absorptions being analyzed;
and he will hear the meaning of those four immeasurables being analyzed.
And he will hear the meaning of those four formless attainments being analyzed;
he will hear the meaning of those eight liberations being analyzed; and he will hear the meaning of those nine successive meditative attainments being analyzed.
And he will hear the meaning of those doors of liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness— as it is being analyzed;
and he will hear the meaning of those supernormal knowledges as it is being analyzed.
And he will hear the meaning of those samādhis being analyzed; he will hear the meaning of those dhāraṇī-gates being analyzed;
and he will hear the meaning of those powers of the Tathāgata being analyzed.
He will hear the meaning of those four fearlessnesses being analyzed;
he will hear the meaning of those four analytical knowledges being analyzed;
and he will hear the meaning of that great compassion being analyzed.
And therein he will hear the meaning of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha being analyzed;

he will see the Bodhi tree; he will see the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva approaching the foot of the Bodhi tree; he will see him awakening to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment; and having thus awakened, he will see him turning the wheel of Dharma.

And he will see many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas chanting the Dharma together. "In this way, omniscience (sarvākārajñatā) is to be grasped; in this way, sentient beings are to be matured; in this way, a buddha-field [is to be purified]; and in this way, Māra along with his retinue is to be defeated. Furthermore, from the eastern direction, he will hear the voice of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas: "In such-and-such a world-system, there is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so."
Surrounded and honored by this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas and this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of śrāvakas, he teaches the Dharma;
in the southern direction, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas in such-and-such a world-system.

A Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by this many hundreds of thousands of koṭīs of niyutas of bodhisattvas and this many hundreds of thousands of koṭīs of niyutas of śrāvakas, is teaching the Dharma;
in the western direction, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of koṭīs of niyutas of Buddhas in such-and-such a world-system.

A Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas and this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of śrāvakas, is teaching the Dharma.
In the northern direction, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas in such-and-such a world-system.

A Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by this many hundreds of thousands of koṭī-niyutas of bodhisattvas and this many hundreds of thousands of koṭī-niyutas of śrāvakas, is teaching the Dharma;
in the northeastern direction, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of koṭī-niyutas of Buddhas in that place.

In such-and-such a world-system, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas and this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of śrāvakas, teaches the Dharma.

In the southeastern direction, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, [hearing]: "In such-and-such a world-system, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by so many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas and so many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Śrāvakas, is teaching the Dharma."

In the southwestern direction, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas: "In such-and-such a world-system, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by so many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas and so many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Śrāvakas, is teaching the Dharma."

In the northwestern direction, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, [hearing]: "In such-and-such a world-system, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas and this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Śrāvakas, is teaching the Dharma."

In the downward direction, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas: "In such-and-such a world-system, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas and this many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Śrāvakas, is teaching the Dharma."

In the direction above, he will hear the voices of many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas: "In such-and-such a world-system, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named so-and-so, surrounded and honored by so many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattvas and so many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Śrāvakas, is teaching the Dharma."
In the eastern direction, they will behold many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas entering final nirvana;
and they will behold many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stupas made of the seven precious gems belonging to those Tathāgatas,
and they will honor those stupas of the Tathāgatas with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags.
He will see them being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with many kinds of offerings;
he will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas passing into final nirvana in the southern direction,
and he will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stupas made of the seven precious gems for those Tathāgatas.

And he will see those stūpas of the Tathāgatas being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags, and with many kinds of offerings;
and in the western direction, he will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas entering final nirvāṇa.
They will behold them,
and they will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stūpas made of the seven precious gems belonging to those Tathāgatas;
and they will honor those stūpas of the Tathāgatas with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags.
He will see them being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with many kinds of offerings;
he will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas passing into parinirvāṇa in the northern direction;
and he will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stupas made of the seven precious gems for those Tathāgatas.

And he will see those Tathāgata stūpas being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags, and with many kinds of offerings;
and in the northeastern direction, he will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas entering final nirvāṇa.
And they shall behold many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stūpas made of the seven precious gems belonging to those Tathāgatas;

and they shall see those stūpas of the Tathāgatas being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags, and with various other kinds of offerings.
In the southeastern direction, they will behold many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas entering final nirvana;
and they will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stupas made of the seven precious gems belonging to those Tathāgatas,
and they will honor those stupas of the Tathāgatas with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags.
They will see [the Buddhas] being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with many kinds of offerings;
they will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas entering final nirvana in the southwestern direction;
and they will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stupas made of the seven precious gems for those Tathāgatas.

And he will see those Tathāgata stūpas being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags, and with many kinds of offerings;
and in the northwestern direction, he will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas entering final nirvāṇa.
And they will see many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stūpas made of the seven precious gems belonging to those Tathāgatas;

and they will see those stūpas of the Tathāgatas being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags, and with many kinds of offerings.
In the direction below, they will see many hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of Buddhas entering parinirvāṇa;
and they will see many hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of stūpas made of the seven precious gems belonging to those Tathāgatas,
and they will honor those stūpas of the Tathāgatas with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags.
They will see [the Buddhas] being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with many kinds of offerings;
they will see, in the direction above, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas entering parinirvāṇa,
and they will see for those Tathāgatas many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of stūpas made of the seven precious gems.

And he will see those stūpas of the Tathāgatas being honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags, and with many kinds of offerings.

Furthermore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family will indeed see such auspicious dreams; they will lie down in comfort, wake up in comfort, and their body will feel as if it has been cast into a stream.

A perception of lightness will arise regarding the body, not a perception of heaviness, and they will have no intense craving for food, no craving for robes, and no craving for medicinal requisites for the sick.
His perception of food will be slight; his perception of robes will be slight; his perception of medicinal requisites for the sick will be slight.

Just as, Kauśika, a monk who is a practitioner of yoga, having emerged from meditative concentration, possesses a mind overflowing with mental attention, yet through that mind he has no strong greed for food and his perception of food is slight—even so, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family will have no strong greed for food. Why is that?
For indeed, a stream shall enter the body of that human being.

Those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and Bodhisattvas who are in the eastern direction, as well as the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—they shall cause a stream to enter his body.

And those Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and Bodhisattvas who are in the southern direction, as well as the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—they too shall cause a stream to enter his body.

The Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and the Bodhisattvas who are in the western direction, as well as the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—they shall pour forth streams [of offerings] into his body; and the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and the Bodhisattvas who are in the northern direction, as well as the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—they shall pour forth streams [of offerings] into his body.

The Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and the Bodhisattvas, as well as the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas who are in the northeastern direction—they shall pour forth a stream [of offerings] into his body; the Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and the Bodhisattvas, as well as the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas who are in the southeastern direction—they shall pour forth a stream [of offerings] into his body.

In the southwestern direction, whatever Buddhas, Blessed Ones, Bodhisattvas, and gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas there may be—they shall pour forth a stream [of blessings] into his body.

In the northwestern direction, whatever Buddhas, Blessed Ones, Bodhisattvas, and gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas there may be—they shall pour forth a stream [of blessings] into his body.

In the direction below, whatever Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and Bodhisattvas there may be, and whatever gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas there may be—they shall pour forth a stream [of blessings] into his body.

In the direction above, whatever Buddhas, Blessed Ones, and Bodhisattvas there may be, and whatever gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas there may be—they shall pour forth a stream into his body.
Furthermore, Kauśika, by a son of good family or a daughter of good family who desires to acquire these very qualities pertaining to the present life...

Or rather, this very Perfection of Wisdom should be heard, taken up, retained, recited, mastered, and properly attended to with right mental focus; and one should never be separated from the mind of omniscience. Now, Kauśika, if that son of good family or daughter of good family were not to take up this Perfection of Wisdom...

If that son of good family or daughter of good family were neither to uphold it, nor recite it, nor master it, nor attend to it with wise reflection, then they should, having written this Perfection of Wisdom and placed it in the form of a book, honor it, revere it, respect it, and worship it with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, and parasols.
With banners, flags, and various musical instruments—
thus, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family will be practicing for the welfare of many people and practicing for the happiness of many people;
for whatever merit any son of good family or daughter of good family shall produce, Kauśika, it cannot be equaled by us.

Suppose one were to honor, revere, respect, and worship for as long as life lasts the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas in the world systems of the ten directions, providing them with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick;

and suppose one were to construct stupas made of the seven precious gems for those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas together with their assemblies of Śrāvakas after they have entered parinirvāṇa.
And for as long as life lasts, one should honor, revere, and worship them with flowers, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, flags, and various kinds of musical instruments.
This is the twenty-first chapter of the *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*.

Then the Blessed One addressed Śakra, the lord of the gods: "Kauśika, if you were to receive this Jambudvīpa filled to the brim with the relics of the Tathāgata, on one hand, and if this Prajñāpāramitā were written down in a book and offered to you,
what would you take from those two?"

Śakra said: "If, Blessed One, this Jambudvīpa were filled to the brim with reliquaries containing the bodily relics of the Tathāgatas and offered to me, and this Prajñāpāramitā were written down in a book and presented to me, I would take up this very Prajñāpāramitā, Blessed One. For what reason?"

"Blessed One, it is not that I lack reverence for those relics of the Tathāgata, nor do I lack confidence in them, nor do I lack great respect for them. Blessed One, it is not that I do not wish to honor, revere, esteem, and worship the relics of the Tathāgata.
Rather, Blessed One, it is because those relics have been produced from the perfection of wisdom that they are the relics of the Tathāgata."
Because the bodies are permeated by the perfection of wisdom, they are honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped;
it is for that reason that those relics of the Tathāgata receive worship.
Therefore, Blessed One, when I would honor, revere, esteem, and worship the relics of the Tathāgata with divine [offerings]...
With divine flowers, divine garlands, divine perfumes, divine ointments, divine powders, divine robes, divine parasols, divine banners, divine flags, and divine musical instruments—
regarding them as being permeated by the perfection of wisdom— one [honors] those relics of the Tathāgata together with the world of gods, humans, and asuras.
They are honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped by the world because they have been permeated by the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
Then, the venerable Śāradvatīputra said this to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
"Kauśika, this perfection of wisdom is ungraspable, formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and has but a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics."

How then can you conceive that the perfection of wisdom—which is ungraspable, formless, invisible, non-obstructive, and of a single characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being characterless—is something to be grasped? For what reason?
Because the perfection of wisdom does not stand for grasping nor for relinquishing; it is not for decrease nor for increase, nor for accumulation.
It does not lead to elevation, nor to affliction, nor to purification; it is neither a giver of the qualities of a Buddha, nor a discarder of the qualities of ordinary persons;
it is neither a giver of the qualities of Bodhisattvas, nor a giver of the qualities of Pratyekabuddhas, nor a giver of the qualities of Śrāvakas;

it is neither a giver of the qualities of those in training (śaikṣa) nor of those beyond training (aśaikṣa), nor a discarder of the qualities of ordinary persons, nor [a giver] of the unconditioned realm (asaṃskṛtadhātu).

She is not a giver of the conditioned realm, nor a discarder of the perfection of generosity; she is not a giver of the perfection of ethical discipline, nor a giver of the perfection of patience, nor a giver of the perfection of diligence, nor a giver of the perfection of meditative concentration, nor a giver of the perfection of wisdom.
She is not a giver of internal emptiness.
It is not the giver of external emptiness,
nor the giver of internal-and-external emptiness, nor the giver of the emptiness of emptiness.
It is not the giver of great emptiness, nor the giver of ultimate emptiness,
nor the giver of conditioned emptiness.
It is not the giver of the emptiness of the unconditioned,
nor the giver of the emptiness of the ultimate,
nor the giver of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.
It is not the giver of the emptiness of non-dispersal, nor the giver of the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
nor the giver of the emptiness of all phenomena.
It is not the giver of the emptiness of specific characteristics, nor the giver of the emptiness of non-apprehension,
nor the giver of the emptiness of non-existence.
It is not the giver of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor the giver of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
It is not the giver of the applications of mindfulness.
She is not the giver of the right efforts, nor the giver of the bases of psychic power, nor the giver of the faculties.
She is not the giver of the powers,
nor the giver of the factors of enlightenment,
nor the giver of the noble eightfold path.
She is not the giver of the noble truths, nor the giver of the meditative absorptions,
nor the giver of the immeasurables.
She is not the giver of the formless attainments, nor the giver of the liberations, nor the giver of the successive meditative attainments.
She is not the giver of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; she is not the giver of the superknowledges; she is not the giver of the meditative concentrations.
She is not the giver of the gateways of dhāraṇīs,
nor the giver of the powers of a Tathāgata,
nor the giver of the grounds of self-confidence.
It is not the giver of the analytical knowledges,
nor the giver of great compassion,
nor the giver of the unique qualities of a Buddha.
She is not the giver of the fruit of stream-entry, nor the giver of the fruit of once-returning, nor the giver of the fruit of non-returning.
It is not the giver of arhatship, nor the giver of pratyekabuddha-enlightenment,
nor the giver of the knowledge of the aspects of the path.
"It does not bestow omniscience.

Śakra said: "So it is, venerable Śāradvatīputra; so it is. Venerable Śāradvatīputra, one who understands thus knows that the perfection of wisdom does not bestow the qualities of a Buddha, nor does it discard the qualities of ordinary persons, nor does it [bestow] the qualities of a bodhisattva."

She is not the giver of the qualities of a Pratyekabuddha, nor the giver of the qualities of a Śrāvaka, nor the giver of the qualities of those in training (śaikṣa) or those beyond training (aśaikṣa), nor the giver of the qualities of ordinary worldlings (pṛthagjana). She is not the discarder of the unconditioned realm (asaṃskṛtadhātu), nor the discarder of the conditioned realm (saṃskṛtadhātu). She is not the giver of the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā), nor the giver of the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā), nor the giver of the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā), nor the giver of the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā), nor the giver of the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyānapāramitā), nor the giver of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
She is not the giver of internal emptiness, nor the giver of external emptiness,
but she is the giver through internal and external emptiness.
It is not the giver of the emptiness of emptiness,
nor the giver of the great emptiness; it is not the giver of the emptiness of the ultimate truth,
nor the giver of the emptiness of the conditioned.
It is not the giver of the emptiness of the unconditioned,
nor the giver of the emptiness of the ultimate,
nor the giver of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.
She is not the giver of the emptiness of non-dispersal, nor is she the giver of the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
It is not the giver of the emptiness of all phenomena, nor the giver of the emptiness of specific characteristics, nor the giver of the emptiness of non-apprehension.
It is not the giver of the emptiness of non-existence, nor the giver of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, nor the giver of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
She is not the giver of the foundations of mindfulness, nor the giver of the right efforts, nor the giver of the bases of psychic power.
It is not the giver of the sense faculties, nor the giver of the powers,
nor the giver of the factors of enlightenment.
She is not the giver of the Noble Eightfold Path, nor the giver of the Noble Truths, nor the giver of the meditative absorptions.
She is not the giver of the immeasurables,
nor the giver of the formless attainments,
nor the giver of the liberations.
She is not the giver of the successive meditative attainments; she is not the giver of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
nor is she the giver of the superknowledges.
She is not the giver of meditative concentrations, nor the giver of the gateways of dhāraṇīs, nor the giver of the powers of a Tathāgata.
She is not the giver of the fearlessnesses, nor the giver of the analytical knowledges,
nor the giver of great compassion.
She is not the giver of the unique qualities of a Buddha,
nor the giver of the fruit of stream-entry,
nor the giver of the fruit of once-returning.
She is not the giver of the fruit of once-returning, nor the giver of arhatship,
nor the giver of solitary enlightenment.
It is not the giver of the knowledge of the aspects of the path, nor is it the giver of the knowledge of all aspects. He courses in the perfection of wisdom; he cultivates the perfection of wisdom.
The perfection of wisdom is not to be apprehended as dualistic.
For the perfection of wisdom is non-dual;
the perfection of meditation should not be followed as dual, for the perfection of meditation is indeed non-dual.
The perfection of vigor is not to be followed as a duality,
for the perfection of vigor is non-dual;
the perfection of patience is not to be followed as a duality.
For the perfection of patience is non-dual;
the perfection of ethical discipline should not be pursued as dualistic, for the perfection of ethical discipline is indeed non-dual.
The perfection of generosity should not be pursued as a duality,
for the perfection of generosity is non-dual.
Then the Blessed One gave his approval to Śakra, the lord of the gods:
Excellent, excellent, Kauśika! It is just as you have pointed out;
for the perfection of wisdom is not to be followed by way of duality. Why is that?
Because the perfection of wisdom is non-dual.
For the perfection of meditation is not to be pursued as dual;
why is that?
Because the perfection of meditation is non-dual.
For the perfection of wisdom is not to be followed as a duality. Why is that?
Because the perfection of wisdom is non-dual;
indeed, the perfection of meditative concentration is not to be followed as a duality.
For what reason?
Because the perfection of meditation is non-dual;
indeed, the perfection of vigor is not to be pursued as dual. For what reason?
For the perfection of vigor is non-dual;
indeed, the perfection of patience is not to be pursued as a duality.
Why is that?
For the perfection of patience is non-dual;
indeed, the perfection of ethical discipline is not to be pursued as dualistic. Why is that?
Because the perfection of ethical discipline is non-dual.
For the perfection of generosity is not to be pursued by way of duality;
why is that?
Because the perfection of generosity is non-dual.
O Kauśika, he who would desire duality in the perfection of wisdom would desire duality in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). For what reason?

Because, O Kauśika, the realm of phenomena and the perfection of wisdom are non-dual and not divided; he who would desire duality in the realm of phenomena, O Kauśika, [would desire duality in the perfection of wisdom].
Whoever would desire duality in the perfection of meditation. Why is that?
For, Kauśika, the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) and the perfection of meditation are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would desire duality in the realm of phenomena would likewise desire duality in the perfection of vigor. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) and the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā) are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would seek duality in the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā) would be seeking duality in the realm of phenomena. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the realm of phenomena and the perfection of patience are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
O Kauśika, he who would seek duality in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) would seek duality in the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*). Why is that?
Because, O Kauśika, the realm of phenomena and the perfection of ethical discipline are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
O Kauśika, he who would seek duality in the realm of phenomena would seek duality in the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*). Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) and the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā) are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would seek duality in the perfection of wisdom would be seeking duality in suchness (tathatā). Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, suchness and the perfection of wisdom are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would desire duality in the perfection of meditation would desire duality in suchness. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, suchness and the perfection of meditation are non-dual and not divided; they are one.
Kauśika, whoever would desire duality in the perfection of vigor would desire duality in suchness. Why is that?
For it is thus, Kauśika: suchness and the perfection of vigor are non-dual; they are not divided into two.

Kauśika, whoever would desire duality in the perfection of patience would desire duality in suchness. Why is that? For it is thus, Kauśika: suchness and the perfection of patience are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, he who would desire duality in the perfection of ethical discipline would desire duality in suchness. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, suchness and the perfection of ethical discipline are non-dual and indivisible.
Kauśika, he who would desire duality in the perfection of generosity would desire duality in suchness. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, suchness and the perfection of giving are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would seek duality in the perfection of wisdom would be seeking duality in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, the limit of reality and the perfection of wisdom are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, he who would desire duality in the perfection of meditation would desire duality in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, the limit of reality and the perfection of meditation are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, he who would desire duality in the perfection of vigor would desire duality in the limit of reality. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the limit of reality and the perfection of vigor are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would desire duality in the perfection of patience would desire duality in the limit of reality. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) and the perfection of patience (*kṣāntipāramitā*) are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would desire duality in the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) would desire duality in the limit of reality. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the limit of reality and the perfection of ethical discipline are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
O Kauśika, he who would seek duality in the perfection of giving would seek duality in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Why is that?
Because, O Kauśika, the limit of reality and the perfection of giving are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
O Kauśika, he who would seek duality in the perfection of wisdom would seek duality in the inconceivable realm (*acintyadhātu*). Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the inconceivable realm and the perfection of wisdom are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would seek duality in the perfection of meditation would be seeking duality in the inconceivable realm. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the inconceivable realm and the perfection of meditation are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
O Kauśika, he who would seek duality in the perfection of vigor would seek duality in the inconceivable realm. Why is that?
Because, O Kauśika, the inconceivable realm and the perfection of vigor are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
O Kauśika, he who would seek duality in the perfection of patience would seek duality in the inconceivable realm. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the inconceivable realm and the perfection of patience are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
Kauśika, whoever would seek duality in the perfection of ethical discipline would be seeking duality in the inconceivable realm. Why is that?
For in this way, Kauśika, the inconceivable realm and the perfection of ethical discipline are non-dual; they are not divided into two.
“Kauśika, whoever would desire duality in the perfection of giving would desire duality in the inconceivable realm. Why is that?
Because, Kauśika, the inconceivable realm and the perfection of giving are non-dual; they are not divided into two.”
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, said this to the Blessed One:

"This perfection of wisdom, Blessed One, is worthy of homage by the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, wherein having trained, the bodhisattvas, the great beings, have fully awakened and will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
"Blessed One, when I am seated upon that very throne of Indra in the Sudharmā assembly hall of the gods, and the sons of the gods come there to attend upon me and honor me while I am on my own seat—
if I do not go there and remain seated on that throne— then those sons of the gods,
having arrived at that assembly hall, pay homage to that throne, circumambulate it, and depart once again. Thus it was said here.

Śakra, the lord of the gods, having sat down, teaches the Dharma to the gods of the Thirty-three. It is even so, Blessed One: wherever this perfection of wisdom is written down, maintained, recited, and extensively proclaimed to others.
Therein, those gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas in the world-systems of the ten directions,
having bowed to and paid homage to that perfection of wisdom,
will depart, for from this [perfection of wisdom] have the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas emerged, and from this have all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas emerged.

And from this have issued forth all the requisites for the happiness of sentient beings; even that the relics of the Tathāgatas receive worship is because they have been permeated by the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*). For what reason?
Blessed One, for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, the perfection of wisdom is the basis for the knowledge of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*).

It is the condition, it is the cause, and it is the nourisher; therefore, O Blessed One, from these two factors, I would rather take up this very perfection of wisdom. For when I, O Blessed One, have taken up this perfection of wisdom and, having taken it up, recite it with a mind absorbed in the Dharma, I do not perceive even a sign.
"Blessed One, at that time, I do not perceive any fear or paralysis. Why is that?

Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom is signless, without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization; Blessed One, the perfection of meditative concentration is signless, without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization."
For the perfection of vigor, O Blessed One, is signless; for the perfection of vigor, O Blessed One, is without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For the perfection of patience, O Blessed One, is signless; for the perfection of patience, O Blessed One, is without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For the perfection of ethical discipline, O Blessed One, is signless; for the perfection of ethical discipline, O Blessed One, is without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.

For the perfection of generosity, Blessed One, is signless; it is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization, Blessed One. For internal emptiness, Blessed One, is signless; it is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization, Blessed One.
For external emptiness, Blessed One, is signless; it is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization, Blessed One.
For, Blessed One, internal-external emptiness is signless; for, Blessed One, internal-external emptiness is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, Blessed One, the emptiness of emptiness is signless; for, Blessed One, the emptiness of emptiness is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, Blessed One, great emptiness is signless; for, Blessed One, great emptiness is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.

For, Blessed One, ultimate emptiness is signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for, Blessed One, conditioned emptiness is signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for, Blessed One, unconditioned emptiness is signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For, Blessed One, absolute emptiness is signless; for, Blessed One, absolute emptiness is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.

For, Blessed One, the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is signless; for, Blessed One, the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, O Blessed One, the emptiness of non-dispersal is signless, markless, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression;

for, O Blessed One, the emptiness of nature is signless, markless, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for, O Blessed One, the emptiness of all phenomena is signless, markless, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For, O Blessed One, the emptiness of specific characteristics is signless; for, O Blessed One, the emptiness of specific characteristics is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, O Blessed One, the emptiness of non-apprehension is signless; for, O Blessed One, the emptiness of non-apprehension is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, O Blessed One, the emptiness of non-existence is signless; for, O Blessed One, the emptiness of non-existence is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, Blessed One, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is signless; for, Blessed One, the emptiness of intrinsic nature is without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.

For, Blessed One, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is signless; for, Blessed One, the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For, Blessed One, the applications of mindfulness are signless; for, Blessed One, the applications of mindfulness are without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For the right efforts, O Blessed One, are signless; the right efforts, O Blessed One, are without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For the bases of psychic power, O Blessed One, are signless; the bases of psychic power, O Blessed One, are without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For the faculties, O Blessed One, are signless; the faculties, O Blessed One, are without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.

For the powers, O Blessed One, are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for the faculties, O Blessed One, are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for the factors of enlightenment, O Blessed One, are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for the noble eightfold path, O Blessed One, is signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For the noble truths, O Blessed One, are signless; the noble truths, O Blessed One, are without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For the meditative absorptions, O Blessed One, are signless; the meditative absorptions, O Blessed One, are without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For the immeasurables, O Blessed One, are signless; the immeasurables, O Blessed One, are ineffable and beyond verbal expression.
For, Blessed One, the formless attainments are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression;
for, Blessed One, the liberations are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression;
for, Blessed One, the serial meditative attainments are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.

For the gateways to the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, O Blessed One, are indeed signless; for the gateways to the liberations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, O Blessed One, are without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For the superknowledges, O Blessed One, are signless; for the superknowledges, O Blessed One, are without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, Blessed One, the samādhis are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression;

for, Blessed One, the gateways to the dhāraṇīs are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for, Blessed One, the powers of a Tathāgata are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For, Blessed One, the grounds of self-confidence are signless; indeed, Blessed One, the grounds of self-confidence are without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, Blessed One, the analytical knowledges are signless; indeed, Blessed One, the analytical knowledges are without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
For, Blessed One, great compassion is signless; indeed, Blessed One, great compassion is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.

For, O Blessed One, the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for, O Blessed One, the state of omniscience (sarvajñatā) is signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression; for, O Blessed One, the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) is signless, without marks, ineffable, and beyond verbal expression.
For, O Blessed One, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*) is signless; for, O Blessed One, the knowledge of all aspects is without marks, inexpressible, and beyond verbalization.
If, O Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom were to have signs rather than being signless, then the Tathāgata would not have taught it.
The Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, having realized that all phenomena are signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible,
and having awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, will teach to sentient beings the Dharma which is signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible.
Therefore, Blessed One, because the perfection of wisdom is signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible, the Tathāgata,

having understood all phenomena as markless, ineffable, and inexpressible, and having fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, will teach to sentient beings the Dharma that is signless, markless, ineffable, and inexpressible. Therefore...
