Householder families of great śāla trees are known;
the gods of the Four Great Kings are known;
the Trāyastriṃśa gods are known.
The Yāma gods are known;

and the stream-enterers are discerned.
Once-returners are known,
non-returners are known,
and arhats are known.
Pratyekabuddhas are known;
bodhisattva mahāsattvas are known; and Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas are known.

“Kauśika, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the sentient beings in as many world-systems in the upward direction as there are grains of sand in the river Ganges in the four meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*).”

One would establish them in the four formless attainments and the five superknowledges. What do you think, Kauśika, would that son of good family or daughter of good family generate much merit on that account?
He replied: "Much, Blessed One; much, Sugata."
The Blessed One said:

"Therefore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family would generate much more merit who would give a book of this Perfection of Wisdom to another for the purpose of reading, writing, or reciting it. Why is that?"

For it is thus, Kauśika, that in this perfection of wisdom the untainted dharmas are taught in detail; having trained therein, sons and daughters of good family have entered, are entering, and will enter the fixed course of rightness;
they have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of stream-entry.
They have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of once-returning;
they have attained, are attaining, and will attain the fruit of non-returning;
they have attained, are attaining, and will attain arhatship.
Those belonging to the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas have attained, are attaining, and will attain pratyekabodhi;

and bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas, having entered, are entering, and will enter the bodhisattva-determination (nyāma), and they have awakened, are awakening, and will awaken to unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

And what, Kauśika, are those untainted dharmas? They are as follows: the perfection of giving, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom; and internal emptiness.
emptiness of the external,
emptiness of the internal and external,
and emptiness of emptiness;
great emptiness,
emptiness of the ultimate truth,
and emptiness of the conditioned;
unconditioned emptiness,
absolute emptiness,
and emptiness without beginning or end;
emptiness of non-dispersal, emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and emptiness of all phenomena.
emptiness of specific characteristics,
emptiness of non-apprehension,
and emptiness of non-existence;
emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
and the four foundations of mindfulness;
the four right efforts,
the four bases of psychic power, and the five faculties.
the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, the noble eightfold path, the four noble truths, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditative attainments,
the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, the six superknowledges, all concentrations, and all gateways to the dhāraṇīs.

The ten powers of a Tathāgata, the four grounds of self-confidence, the four analytical knowledges, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as other immeasurable qualities of a Buddha, have been taught in detail. Therefore, Kauśika, by this very method you should understand it thus:
if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, having written the perfection of wisdom in a book, were to give it to others for the purpose of reading, writing, or reciting it;
This person alone would generate much more merit than that. Why is that?
Because here in this *prajñāpāramitā*, Kauśika, all dharmas are taught in detail—those by which the great noble families of Kṣatriyas are known, and the great noble families of Brāhmaṇas are known.
Families of great householders are known;
the gods of the Four Great Kings are known;
the Trāyastriṃśa gods are known.
The Yāma gods are known;
the Tuṣita gods are known;
the Nirmāṇarati gods are known.
The gods who wield power over the creations of others are known;
the gods of the Brahma-realm are known;
the gods who are ministers of Brahma are known.
The Brahmā-pārṣadya gods are known;
the Mahābrahmā gods are known;
the Ābhā gods are known.
The gods of Limited Radiance are known; the gods of Immeasurable Radiance are known; the gods of Utmost Purity of Radiance are known.
The Śubha devas are known; the Parīttaśubha devas are known; the Apramāṇaśubha devas are known.
The Śubhakṛtsna gods are known;
the Bṛhat gods are known;
the Parīttabṛhat gods are known.
The Apramāṇaśubha gods are known;
the Bṛhatphala gods are known;
the Abṛha gods are known.
The Atapa gods are known; the Sudṛśa gods are known;
the Sudarśana gods are known.
The Akaniṣṭha gods are known; the Ākāśānantyāyatana gods are known;
the Vijñānānantyāyatana gods are known;
the Ākiñcanyāyatana gods are known.
The gods of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception are discerned;
the perfection of generosity is discerned.
The perfection of ethical discipline is discerned, the perfection of patience is discerned,
and the perfection of vigor is discerned.
The perfection of meditation is discerned;
the perfection of wisdom is discerned. Internal emptiness is discerned.
External emptiness is discerned; internal-external emptiness is discerned;
the emptiness of emptiness is discerned.
Great emptiness is discerned, ultimate emptiness is discerned,
and conditioned emptiness is discerned.
Unconditioned emptiness is discerned;
ultimate emptiness is discerned;
emptiness without beginning or end is discerned.
The emptiness of non-dispersal is discerned; the emptiness of intrinsic nature is discerned;
the emptiness of all phenomena is discerned.
The emptiness of specific characteristics is discerned;
the emptiness of non-apprehension is discerned; the emptiness of non-existence is discerned.
The emptiness of intrinsic nature is discerned; the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence is discerned.
The applications of mindfulness are discerned.
The right efforts are discerned;
the bases of psychic power are discerned; the faculties are discerned.
The powers are discerned, the factors of enlightenment are discerned,
and the noble eightfold path is discerned.
The noble truths are discerned; the meditative absorptions are discerned;
the immeasurables are discerned.
The formless attainments are discerned;
the eight liberations are discerned; the nine successive meditative attainments are discerned.
The gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are discerned;
the superknowledges are discerned;
and the meditative concentrations are discerned.
The gateways of dhāraṇī are made known;
the powers of a Tathāgata are made known; the grounds of self-confidence are made known.
The analytical knowledges are discerned;
great loving-kindness is discerned; great compassion is discerned.
The unique qualities of a Buddha are discerned;
the fruit of stream-entry is discerned;
the fruit of once-returning is discerned.
The fruit of non-returning is discerned,
arhatship is discerned,
and solitary enlightenment is discerned.
The knowledge of the aspects of the path is made known;
the knowledge of all aspects is made known;
and the stream-enterers are made known.
Once-returners are known,
non-returners are known,
and arhats are known.
Pratyekabuddhas are known; bodhisattva mahāsattvas are known;
and Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas are known.

Furthermore, Kauśika, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family shall take up, bear in mind, recite, master, and correctly attend to this perfection of wisdom, they will generate far more merit than that.

But it is not so for one who establishes the humans of Jambudvīpa in the ten paths of wholesome action, and establishes them in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges;

nor is it so for one who establishes all sentient beings in the world-system of four continents in the ten paths of wholesome action, and establishes them in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments.
Having established them in the five superknowledges,
it is not at all comparable to establishing all sentient beings in a thousandfold world-system in the ten paths of wholesome action,
or having established them in the four meditative concentrations, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges.
But it is not so, even if one were to establish all beings in a dichiliocosm or a great dichiliocosm in the ten paths of wholesome action,

and establish them in the four meditative concentrations, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges; nor is it so, even if one were to establish all beings in a trichiliocosm great trichiliocosm in the ten paths of wholesome action.

Having established them in the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the five superknowledges, therein this is the appropriate mental attention (*yoniśo-manaskāra*):
that one will not, by means of a cognition characterized by duality nor by a cognition characterized by non-duality, take up, master, retain, recite, or appropriately attend to the *prajñāpāramitā*.
One will not take up, master, retain, recite, or properly attend to the perfection of meditation with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality;
one will not take up, master, retain, recite, or properly attend to the perfection of vigor with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality.
One will not take up, master, retain, recite, or attend to the perfection of patience with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
one will not take up, master, retain, recite, or attend to the perfection of ethical discipline with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not grasp, master, retain, recite, or properly attend to the perfection of generosity with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dualistically.
He will not properly attend to internal emptiness with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dualistically;
he will not properly attend to external emptiness with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dualistically.
He will not correctly attend to internal and external emptiness with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the emptiness of emptiness with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to great emptiness with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not correctly attend to ultimate emptiness with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to conditioned emptiness with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not properly attend to the emptiness of the unconditioned with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that does not course in duality;
he will not properly attend to absolute emptiness with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that does not course in duality;
he will not properly attend to the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that does not course in duality.
He will not correctly attend to the emptiness of non-dispersal with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the emptiness of intrinsic nature with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the emptiness of all phenomena with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not correctly attend to the emptiness of specific characteristics with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the emptiness of non-apprehension with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the emptiness of non-existence with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality.
He will not correctly attend to the emptiness of intrinsic nature with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dualistically;
he will not correctly attend to the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dualistically.
He will not correctly attend to the applications of mindfulness with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dualistically.
He will not properly attend to the right efforts with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not properly attend to the bases of psychic power with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not properly attend to the faculties with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not correctly attend to the powers with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the factors of enlightenment with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the noble eightfold path with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not correctly attend to the noble truths with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the meditative concentrations with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the immeasurables with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality.
He will not attend properly to the formless attainments with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dually;

he will not attend properly to the eight liberations with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dually; he will not attend properly to the nine successive meditative attainments with a mind that functions dualistically, nor with a mind that functions non-dually.
He will not correctly attend to the gateways of liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the superknowledges with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not correctly attend to the meditative concentrations with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not properly attend to the gateways of mnemonic formulas with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality;
he will not properly attend to the powers of a Tathāgata with a mind characterized by duality, nor with a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not properly attend to the grounds of self-confidence with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality;
he will not properly attend to the analytical knowledges with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality;
he will not properly attend to great compassion with a mind that courses in duality, nor with a mind that courses in non-duality.
He will not attend to the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) through a mind characterized by duality, nor through a mind characterized by non-duality;

he will not attend to omniscience (sarvajñatā) through a mind characterized by duality, nor through a mind characterized by non-duality; he will not attend to the knowledge of the aspects of the path (mārgākārajñatā) through a mind characterized by duality, nor through a mind characterized by non-duality.
He will not attend to the knowledge of all aspects (sarvākārajñatā) through a mind that courses in duality, nor through a mind that courses in non-duality.

Furthermore, Kauśika, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family shall, by this method, extensively explain, teach, illuminate, clarify, and reveal the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) to others.
He will analyze it, he will exalt it, he will reveal it, and he will teach its meaning;
in this regard, Kauśika, this is the meaning of the perfection of wisdom:

The perfection of wisdom is not to be viewed as dual, nor as non-dual; not through signs, nor through accumulation, nor through subtraction; not through addition, nor through subtraction; not through affliction, nor through purification; not through arising, nor through cessation.
Neither by way of grasping nor non-grasping, neither by way of taking up nor relinquishing, neither by way of staying nor not staying, neither by way of reality nor unreality;
neither by way of conjunction nor disjunction, neither by way of cohesion nor non-cohesion, neither by way of condition nor non-condition, neither by way of dharma nor non-dharma;

neither by way of the Tathāgata nor non-Tathāgata, neither by way of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) nor non-limit of reality—this very son of good family or daughter of good family would generate much more merit.
Whoever shall extensively explain, teach, illuminate, analyze, honor, clarify, and fully reveal this perfection of wisdom to others,
and who shall provide instruction upon it— this is what he will do.
But it is not so for one who would take up this very [perfection of wisdom] alone, master it, uphold it, retain it, recite it, and attend to it with wise reflection.
Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family should themselves take up the perfection of wisdom...
He will master it, attend to it with wise reflection, and explain it in detail to others;
he will teach it, illuminate it, make it known, establish it, analyze it, cultivate it, clarify it, and fully reveal it.
Furthermore, he will explain its meaning. It is this very son of good family or daughter of good family, Kauśika, who will produce far more merit.
Śakra said: "In this way indeed, Blessed One, the perfection of wisdom should be taught by a son of good family or a daughter of good family—complete with both its meaning and its phrasing.
The Blessed One said:

In this way, Kauśika, a son of good family or a daughter of good family should teach the perfection of wisdom to others, both in its meaning and its letter. Teaching it in this manner, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family will be endowed with a mass of merit that is immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite.

If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, and worship immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the eastern direction for as long as they live, providing them with all the requisites of happiness— namely, flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags;

Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to explain this perfection of wisdom to another in detail through many methods— with both its meaning and its phrasing— teaching it, proclaiming it, analyzing it, elucidating it, clarifying it, and illuminating it; with various musical instruments as well, that very son or daughter of good family would indeed produce much more [merit].
He would produce merit. Why is that?

For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past, future, and present have fully awakened, are fully awakening, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, respect, and worship with all articles of comfort throughout their lives as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as are immeasurable and incalculable in the southern direction— with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, and banners—

Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to explain, teach, illuminate, analyze, expound, clarify, and fully reveal this Perfection of Wisdom to another in detail through many methods— along with its meaning and its phrasing— and were to do so with various banners and musical instruments, that son of good family indeed [would produce much merit].
Or a daughter of good family would produce even more merit. Why is that?

For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present have awakened, are awakening, and will awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, and worship as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as are immeasurable and incalculable in the western direction throughout their entire lives, providing them with every article of comfort, with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags;

Furthermore, Kauśika, if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to explain, teach, illuminate, analyze, expound, clarify, and elucidate this Perfection of Wisdom to another in detail through many methods— along with its meaning and its phrasing— this very son of good family or daughter of good family would indeed produce much more [merit] than by means of various musical instruments.
He would produce merit. For what reason?

Because it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present have fully awakened, are fully awakening, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, respect, and worship, for as long as life lasts, with every provision for comfort, immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly enlightened Buddhas in the northern direction— with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, and banners—

Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, with various banners and musical instruments, should indeed explain, teach, illuminate, analyze, expound, clarify, and fully reveal this Perfection of Wisdom to another in detail, with its meaning and its phrasing, through many methods— this very son of good family [is the one who truly honors it].
Or a daughter of good family would generate much more merit. Why is that?

For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present have awakened, are awakening, and will awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, and worship as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones as are immeasurable and incalculable in the northeastern direction, throughout their entire lives, with every provision for comfort— namely, with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags—

Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to explain, teach, illuminate, analyze, expound, clarify, and elucidate this perfection of wisdom to another in detail through many methods, providing both the meaning and the phrasing, then this very son of good family or daughter of good family would indeed produce much greater merit than by means of various musical instruments.
He would produce merit. Why is that?

For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past, future, and present have fully awakened, are fully awakening, and will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor, revere, respect, and worship with all articles of comfort throughout their entire lives as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as are immeasurable and incalculable in the southeastern direction— with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, and banners—

Furthermore, Kauśika, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family, with various banners and musical instruments, should indeed explain, teach, illuminate, analyze, expound, clarify, and fully reveal this Perfection of Wisdom to another in many ways, together with its meaning and its phrasing— this very son of good family [would produce greater merit].
Or a daughter of good family would produce even more merit. Why is that?

For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

They have fully awakened and will fully awaken. If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor and revere, for as long as life lasts, with every provision for comfort, immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly awakened Buddhas in the southwestern direction;
One should worship it with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags,

and with various kinds of musical instruments; and furthermore, Kauśika, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family should explain this Perfection of Wisdom to another at length in many ways— with its meaning and its phrasing— teaching it and illuminating it.
One who would reflect upon it, analyze it, clarify it, and illuminate it—this very son of good family or daughter of good family would generate far more merit. Why is that?
For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

They have awakened, and they will awaken. If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor and revere, for as long as life lasts, with every provision for comfort, immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas in the northwestern direction;
One should honor and worship [this perfection] with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags,

and various kinds of musical instruments; and furthermore, Kauśika, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family should explain this perfection of wisdom to another at length in many ways, together with its meaning and its phrasing.

One who would teach, reveal, explain, analyze, clarify, and fully illuminate this [perfection of wisdom] would produce far more merit than that son of good family or daughter of good family. Why is that?

For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past, future, and present have awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

They have awakened and they are awakening. If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor and revere, for as long as life lasts, with every article of comfort, immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Ones in the direction below;
One should worship with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, and flags,

and with various kinds of musical instruments; and furthermore, Kauśika, whichever son of good family or daughter of good family should, in many ways, explain this Perfection of Wisdom in detail to another— along with its meaning and its phrasing— teach it, and illuminate it.
One who would reflect upon it, analyze it, clarify it, and illuminate it—this very son of good family or daughter of good family would produce far more merit. Why is that?
For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats [and Perfectly Enlightened Ones] of the past, future, and present [have attained enlightenment].

By the perfectly awakened ones, unsurpassed perfect awakening has been fully awakened to, is being fully awakened to, and will be fully awakened to. If, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to honor and revere, for as long as life lasts, with every provision for happiness, immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and perfectly awakened ones in the direction above;
One should honor and worship [this perfection of wisdom] with flowers, garlands, perfumes, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, flags,

and various kinds of musical instruments; and furthermore, Kauśika, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family should explain this perfection of wisdom to another at length in many ways, along with its meaning and its phrasing.
If one were to teach, reveal, discuss, analyze, clarify, and fully illuminate [this], that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce far more merit. Why is that?

For it is by training in this perfection of wisdom that the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
They have awakened, and they will awaken.
Furthermore, Kauśika, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family, for immeasurable and incalculable eons, were to practice the perfection of giving by way of apprehension.

For immeasurable and incalculable eons, while practicing the perfection of ethical discipline with the application of apprehension; for immeasurable and incalculable eons, while practicing the perfection of patience with the application of apprehension;
for immeasurable and incalculable eons, while practicing the perfection of vigor with the application of apprehension.

If one were to practice the perfection of meditation for immeasurable and incalculable eons by way of apprehension, or practice the perfection of wisdom for immeasurable and incalculable eons by way of apprehension;

and if another were to explain this perfection of wisdom to others in detail—both in its meaning and its phrasing—teaching it, illuminating it, making it known, establishing it, analyzing it, clarifying it, and fully revealing it; [the latter would generate greater merit].
And that [merit] is by way of non-apprehension;
this very person would generate much more merit than that.
In this regard, Kauśika, "apprehension" refers to a bodhisattva's engagement with apprehension here.

When one gives a gift, it occurs to them: "I am giving a gift; I am giving this gift; I am giving a gift to this person. For one who gives a gift in this way, there will be only the gift itself, and not the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*).

When one guards morality, it occurs to them: "I am guarding morality; I am guarding this morality. For one who guards morality in this way, there will be only the morality itself, and not the perfection of morality (*śīlapāramitā*), because of the application of apprehension (*upalambhayoga*). When one cultivates patience, it occurs to them: "I am cultivating patience; I am cultivating this patience."
As he thus cultivates patience, only patience itself will remain for him, and not the perfection of patience through the application of apprehension;

when he exerts vigor, it occurs to him: "I am exerting vigor; I am exerting vigor for this purpose. As he thus exerts vigor, only vigor itself will remain for him, and not the perfection of vigor through the application of apprehension.

As he enters the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), it occurs to him: "I shall enter these meditative concentrations; having entered them, I will remain within these very concentrations. As he thus enters the meditative concentrations, only the concentrations themselves will persist, and not the perfection of concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*) by way of apprehension. As he cultivates wisdom (*prajñā*), it occurs to him: "I am cultivating wisdom; I am cultivating this [wisdom]. As he thus cultivates wisdom, only wisdom itself will persist, and not the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) by way of apprehension.

In this way, Kauśika, for a son of good family or a daughter of good family who practices with apprehension, the perfection of generosity is not fulfilled; the perfection of ethical discipline is not fulfilled; the perfection of patience is not fulfilled; the perfection of vigor is not fulfilled; the perfection of meditation is not fulfilled; and the perfection of wisdom is not fulfilled.
Śakra asked: "Blessed One, how does the perfection of generosity become fulfilled for a bodhisattva mahāsattva as he practices?
Blessed One, how does the perfection of ethical discipline become fulfilled for a bodhisattva mahāsattva as he practices?
Blessed One, how does the perfection of patience become fulfilled for a bodhisattva mahāsattva as he practices?"

Blessed One, how is the perfection of vigor fulfilled for a bodhisattva mahāsattva as he practices? Blessed One, how is the perfection of meditative concentration fulfilled for a bodhisattva mahāsattva as he practices?
Blessed One, how is the perfection of wisdom fulfilled for a bodhisattva mahāsattva as he practices?
The Blessed One said:
"In this case, Kauśika, a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when giving a gift, does not perceive a giver, nor does he perceive a gift, nor a recipient;
and when guarding morality, he does not perceive morality, nor the undertaking of morality."
While cultivating patience, they do not perceive the cultivation of patience;
while exerting vigor, they do not perceive the exertion of vigor;
and regarding the meditative concentrations, they do not perceive the meditative concentrations nor the cultivation of the meditative concentrations.
He does not perceive wisdom, nor the cultivation of wisdom;

for a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing in this way, Kauśika, the perfection of generosity is fulfilled, the perfection of ethical discipline is fulfilled, the perfection of patience is fulfilled, the perfection of vigor is fulfilled, and the perfection of meditative concentration is fulfilled.
The perfection of wisdom is fulfilled.

In this way, Kauśika, the perfection of wisdom, together with its meaning and its phrasing, should be taught to a son of good family or a daughter of good family who does not yet understand; likewise, the perfection of meditation, together with its meaning and its phrasing, should be taught to one who does not yet understand.

To one who does not understand in this way, the perfection of vigor should be taught with its meaning and its phrasing; to one who does not understand in this way, the perfection of patience should be taught with its meaning and its phrasing;
to one who does not understand in this way, the perfection of ethical discipline should be taught with its meaning and its phrasing.
To one who does not understand in this way, the perfection of giving should be taught with both its meaning and its phrasing. For what reason?

Kauśika, in a future time there will be sons of good family and daughters of good family who will teach a counterfeit version of the perfection of wisdom to those belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle.

Furthermore, noble sons and noble daughters who have set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, upon hearing that counterfeit, will stray from the path; for them, this perfection of wisdom, complete in both meaning and phrasing, should be taught in detail.
Śakra asked: "Blessed One, what is the counterfeit perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One replied:
"In this case, Kauśika, a son of good family or a daughter of good family, thinking 'I shall teach the perfection of wisdom,' [proceeds as follows...]"
They will teach a counterfeit [version] of it.
Śakra asked: "Blessed One, how will those sons of good family and daughters of good family teach a counterfeit version of the perfection of wisdom?
The Blessed One said:
In this case, Kauśika, when a son of good family or a daughter of good family teaches the perfection of wisdom,
they will teach a counterfeit of the perfection of wisdom;
therein, that which is the counterfeit of the perfection of wisdom—
That is to say, they will teach that "form is impermanent," they will teach that "form is suffering," and they will teach that "form is non-self."
They will teach that "form is impure," and they will say, "He who practices in this way practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they teach will seek for form as being impermanent.
They will investigate that form is suffering; they will investigate that form is non-self; they will investigate that form is impure.
Seeking that form is impermanent, seeking that form is suffering, and seeking that form is non-self, they...
Seeking to understand that form is impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom; they will teach that feeling is impermanent,
and they will teach that feeling is suffering.
They will teach that feeling is non-self;
they will teach that feeling is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, they are practicing the perfection of wisdom," to those whom they shall instruct.
They will investigate feeling as impermanent; they will investigate feeling as suffering;
they will investigate feeling as non-self.
They will investigate feeling as impure;
investigating feeling as impermanent,
they will investigate feeling as suffering.

Seeking feeling as non-self and seeking feeling as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom; they will teach that perception is impermanent and they will teach that perception is suffering.
They will teach that perception is non-self;
they will teach that perception is impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom," and to those whom they will thus instruct—
They will investigate perception as impermanent; they will investigate perception as suffering;
they will investigate perception as non-self.
They will seek perception as impure; seeking perception as impermanent, seeking perception as suffering,
seeking perception as non-self, and seeking perception as impure, they will course in a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that conditioned phenomena are impermanent; they will teach that conditioned phenomena are suffering;
they will teach that conditioned phenomena are non-self.

They will teach that conditioned phenomena are impure. And they will say, "One who practices in this way is practicing the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they teach will investigate conditioned phenomena as being impermanent.
They will investigate conditioned phenomena as suffering;
they will investigate conditioned phenomena as non-self;
they will investigate conditioned phenomena as impure.
Seeking formations as impermanent, seeking formations as suffering,
seeking formations as non-self, and seeking formations as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that consciousness is impermanent;
they will teach that consciousness is suffering;
they will teach that consciousness is non-self.

They will teach that consciousness is impure, and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach this will investigate that consciousness is impermanent;
they will investigate that consciousness is suffering.
They will investigate that consciousness is non-self; they will investigate that consciousness is impure;
and investigating that consciousness is impermanent, they...
Seeking consciousness as suffering,
seeking consciousness as non-self,
and seeking consciousness as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the eye is impermanent;
they will teach that the eye is suffering;
they will teach that the eye is non-self.

They will teach that "the eye is impure," and they will say, "He who practices in this way practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will seek out the eye as impermanent;
they will seek out the eye as suffering.
They will investigate that "the eye is non-self," they will investigate that "the eye is impure";
thus investigating that "the eye is impermanent," they...
Seeking "the eye is suffering," seeking "the eye is non-self," and seeking "the eye is impure," they will practice in a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the ear is impermanent;
they will teach that the ear is suffering;
they will teach that the ear is non-self.

They will teach that the ear is impure; and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will investigate that the ear is impermanent;
they will investigate that the ear is suffering.
They will investigate that the ear is non-self; they will investigate that the ear is impure;
and while investigating that the ear is impermanent, they will [realize it].
Seeking that "the ear is suffering," seeking that "the ear is non-self," and seeking that "the ear is impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the nose is impermanent;
they will teach that the nose is suffering;
they will teach that the nose is non-self.

They will teach that "the nose is impure," and they will say, "He who practices in this way practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach this will investigate that "the nose is impermanent" and will investigate that "the nose is suffering."
They will investigate that the nose is not-self;
they will investigate that the nose is impure;
and while investigating that the nose is impermanent, they...
Seeking "the nose is suffering," seeking "the nose is non-self," and seeking "the nose is impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the tongue is impermanent;
they will teach that the tongue is suffering;
they will teach that the tongue is non-self.

They will teach that the tongue is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will seek the tongue as impermanent, they will seek the tongue as suffering, and they will seek the tongue as non-self.
They will seek the tongue as "impure"; seeking the tongue as "impermanent," they will seek the tongue as "suffering."
Seeking the tongue as "not-self," seeking the tongue as "impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom,
and they will teach that the body is "impermanent."

They will teach that "the body is suffering," they will teach that "the body is non-self," and they will teach that "the body is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way is practicing in the perfection of wisdom," to those whom they shall instruct.
They will investigate the body as impermanent; they will investigate the body as suffering;
they will investigate the body as non-self.
They will investigate the body as impure; investigating the body as impermanent, they will investigate the body as suffering.
Seeking the body as non-self and seeking the body as impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom and will teach that the mind is impermanent.

They will teach that "the mind is suffering," they will teach that "the mind is non-self," and they will teach that "the mind is impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom"—and those to whom they will thus teach.
They will investigate that the mind is impermanent;
they will investigate that the mind is suffering;
they will investigate that the mind is non-self.
They will seek the mind as impure; seeking the mind as impermanent, they will seek the mind as suffering.
Seeking that "the mind is not-self" and seeking that "the mind is impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that "form is impermanent."
They will teach that form is suffering;
they will teach that form is non-self;
they will teach that form is impure. And in this way...
They will say, "He who practices in this way is practicing the perfection of wisdom," and those to whom they shall give instruction will seek for form as impermanent,
and they will seek for form as suffering.
They will investigate that form is non-self; they will investigate that form is impure;
and while investigating that form is impermanent, they will [realize it].
Seeking that "form is suffering," seeking that "form is non-self," and seeking that "form is impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that sound is impermanent; they will teach that sound is suffering;
they will teach that sound is non-self.

They will teach that sound is impure, and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach this will seek for sound as impermanent;
they will seek for sound as suffering.
They will investigate sound as being non-self; they will investigate sound as being impure;
and while investigating sound as being impermanent, they [will realize it].
Seeking sound as suffering,
seeking sound as non-self,
and seeking sound as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that odor is impermanent;
they will teach that odor is suffering;
they will teach that odor is non-self.
They will teach that "odor is impure," and they will say, "He who practices in this way practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they teach will seek odor as impermanent;
they will seek odor as suffering.
They will seek out odor as non-self; they will seek out odor as impure;
seeking out odor as impermanent, they...
Seeking scent as suffering,
seeking scent as non-self,
and seeking scent as impure, they will practice in a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that taste is impermanent;

they will seek out taste as suffering.
They will investigate taste as "not-self," they will investigate taste as "impure"; thus investigating taste as impermanent, they...
Seeking flavor as suffering,

they will teach that contact is non-self.
They will teach that contact is impure, and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they teach will seek contact as impermanent;
they will seek contact as suffering.
They will investigate contact as being selfless;
they will investigate contact as being impure.
Seeking contact as impermanent, seeking contact as suffering, and seeking contact as non-self, they...
Seeking contact as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom; they will teach that phenomena are impermanent,
and they will teach that phenomena are suffering.

They will teach that "dharmas are without self," and they will teach that "dharmas are impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, those to whom they will teach will seek out dharmas as being impermanent.
They will investigate that phenomena are suffering;
they will investigate that phenomena are non-self;
they will investigate that phenomena are impure.
Seeking those phenomena as impermanent, seeking those phenomena as suffering, and seeking those phenomena as non-self.
Seeking phenomena as being impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that eye-consciousness is impermanent,
and they will teach that eye-consciousness is suffering.

They will teach that "eye-consciousness is non-self" and they will teach that "eye-consciousness is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will seek [to understand] that "eye-consciousness is impermanent."
They will investigate that eye-consciousness is suffering;
they will investigate that eye-consciousness is non-self;
they will investigate that eye-consciousness is impure.
Seeking that eye-consciousness is impermanent,
seeking that eye-consciousness is suffering,
and seeking that eye-consciousness is non-self, they...
Seeking to understand that eye-consciousness is impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that ear-consciousness is impermanent,
and they will teach that ear-consciousness is suffering.
They will teach that auditory consciousness is non-self;

they will teach that auditory consciousness is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they teach will seek [to understand] that auditory consciousness is impermanent.
They will investigate that ear-consciousness is suffering;
they will investigate that ear-consciousness is non-self;
they will investigate that ear-consciousness is impure.
Seeking that auditory consciousness is impermanent,
seeking that auditory consciousness is suffering,
and seeking that auditory consciousness is non-self, they—
Seeking to understand that auditory consciousness is impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that olfactory consciousness is impermanent,
and they will teach that olfactory consciousness is suffering.

They will teach that "olfactory consciousness is non-self" and they will teach that "olfactory consciousness is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, those to whom they teach will seek out olfactory consciousness as being impermanent.
They will investigate that olfactory consciousness is suffering;
they will investigate that olfactory consciousness is non-self.
They will investigate olfactory consciousness as impure;
investigating olfactory consciousness as impermanent,
they will investigate olfactory consciousness as suffering.
Seeking that "nose-consciousness is non-self" and seeking that "nose-consciousness is impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom,
and they will teach that "tongue-consciousness is impermanent."
They will teach that tongue-consciousness is suffering;
they will teach that tongue-consciousness is non-self;
they will teach that tongue-consciousness is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom," to those whom they shall teach.
They will investigate that tongue-consciousness is impermanent; they will investigate that tongue-consciousness is suffering;
they will investigate that tongue-consciousness is non-self.
They will seek after tongue-consciousness as impure; seeking after tongue-consciousness as impermanent, they will seek after tongue-consciousness as suffering.
Seeking that tongue-consciousness is non-self,
and seeking that tongue-consciousness is impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that body-consciousness is impermanent.
They will teach that body-consciousness is suffering;
they will teach that body-consciousness is non-self;
they will teach that body-consciousness is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, they practice the perfection of wisdom," to those whom they shall thus instruct.
They will investigate that body-consciousness is impermanent; they will investigate that body-consciousness is suffering;
they will investigate that body-consciousness is non-self.
They will investigate that body-consciousness is impure; investigating that body-consciousness is impermanent, they will investigate that body-consciousness is suffering.

Seeking that "body-consciousness is non-self" and seeking that "body-consciousness is impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom and will teach that "mind-consciousness is impermanent."
They will teach that mental consciousness is suffering;
they will teach that mental consciousness is non-self;

they will teach that mental consciousness is impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom," to those whom they shall instruct. Those [beings] regarding mental consciousness...
They will investigate that mental consciousness is impermanent; they will investigate that mental consciousness is suffering;
they will investigate that mental consciousness is non-self.
They will investigate mental consciousness as impure;
investigating mental consciousness as impermanent,
they will investigate mental consciousness as suffering.
Seeking that "mental consciousness is non-self" and seeking that "mental consciousness is impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that "eye-contact is impermanent."
They will teach that eye-contact is suffering;
they will teach that eye-contact is non-self;
they will teach that eye-contact is impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way..."
Those who practice the perfection of wisdom and those to whom they will teach it will investigate eye-contact as impermanent;
they will investigate eye-contact as suffering.
They will investigate eye-contact as non-self;
they will investigate eye-contact as impure;
and while investigating eye-contact as impermanent, they [will proceed].
Seeking eye-contact as suffering,
seeking eye-contact as non-self,
and seeking eye-contact as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that ear-contact is impermanent;
they will teach that ear-contact is suffering;
they will teach that ear-contact is non-self.

They will teach that auditory contact is impure, and they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will seek out auditory contact as impermanent;
they will seek out auditory contact as suffering.
They will investigate ear-contact as non-self;
they will investigate ear-contact as impure;
and while investigating ear-contact as impermanent, they...
Seeking auditory contact as suffering,
seeking auditory contact as non-self,
and seeking auditory contact as impure, they will course in a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that olfactory contact is impermanent;
they will teach that olfactory contact is suffering;
they will teach that olfactory contact is non-self.

They will teach that "olfactory contact is impure," and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach this will investigate olfactory contact as impermanent;
they will investigate olfactory contact as suffering.
They will investigate nose-contact as non-self;
they will investigate nose-contact as impure;
and while investigating nose-contact as impermanent, they...
Seeking nose-contact as suffering,
seeking nose-contact as non-self,
and seeking nose-contact as impure, they will practice in a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that tongue-contact is impermanent;
they will teach that tongue-contact is suffering;
they will teach that tongue-contact is non-self.

They will investigate tongue-contact as non-self;
they will investigate tongue-contact as impure;
and while investigating tongue-contact as impermanent, they...
Seeking the contact of the tongue as suffering,
seeking the contact of the tongue as non-self,
and seeking the contact of the tongue as impure.
Thus seeking, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that "bodily contact is impermanent," and they will teach that "bodily contact is suffering."
They will teach that body-contact is non-self;

they will teach that body-contact is impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will seek [to understand] body-contact as impermanent.
They will investigate bodily contact as suffering;
they will investigate bodily contact as non-self;
they will investigate bodily contact as impure.
Seeking body-contact as impermanent, seeking body-contact as suffering, and seeking body-contact as non-self, they...
Seeking to regard bodily contact as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that mental contact is impermanent,
and they will teach that mental contact is suffering.
They will teach that mental contact is non-self;

They will investigate mental contact as suffering;
they will investigate mental contact as non-self;
they will investigate mental contact as impure.
They investigated mental contact as impermanent; they investigated mental contact as suffering;
they investigated mental contact as non-self.
Seeking to understand that mental contact is impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that feeling born of eye-contact is impermanent;
they will teach that feeling born of eye-contact is suffering.
They will teach that feeling born of eye-contact is non-self;

they will teach that feeling born of eye-contact is impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they teach this will seek out feeling born of eye-contact as impermanent.
They will investigate the sensation born of eye-contact as suffering;
they will investigate the sensation born of eye-contact as non-self;
they will investigate the sensation born of eye-contact as impure.
Seeking the sensation born of eye-contact as impermanent,
seeking the sensation born of eye-contact as suffering,
and seeking the sensation born of eye-contact as non-self;
Seeking to regard the sensation born of eye-contact as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that the sensation born of ear-contact is impermanent,
and they will teach that the sensation born of ear-contact is suffering.
They will teach that feeling born of ear-contact is non-self;

They will investigate the sensation born of ear-contact as impermanent;
they will investigate the sensation born of ear-contact as suffering;
they will investigate the sensation born of ear-contact as non-self.
They will investigate the sensation born of ear-contact as impure;
investigating the sensation born of ear-contact as impermanent,
they will investigate the sensation born of ear-contact as suffering.
Seeking the sensation born of ear-contact as "selfless," and seeking the sensation born of ear-contact as "impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;

Seeking the sensation born of body-contact as suffering,

They will investigate the sensation born of mind-contact as being non-self;

Seeking the feeling born of mind-contact as suffering,

They will investigate the earth element as suffering;

they will investigate the earth element as impure.
Searching for the earth element as impermanent, searching for the earth element as suffering, and searching for the earth element as non-self, they...
Seeking the earth element as "impure," they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that the water element is "impermanent," and they will teach that the water element is "suffering."
They will teach that the water element is non-self;
they will teach that the water element is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom.

Seeking the water element as impermanent, seeking the water element as suffering, and seeking the water element as non-self, they...

they will teach the fire element as "impermanent" and they will teach the fire element as "suffering."
