they will teach that the bases of psychic power are impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom," to those whom they shall instruct.
They will investigate the bases of psychic power as impermanent;
they will investigate the bases of psychic power as suffering;
they will investigate the bases of psychic power as non-self.
They will seek the bases of psychic power as being impure; seeking the bases of psychic power as being impermanent, they will seek the bases of psychic power as being suffering.
Seeking the bases of psychic power as being selfless,
seeking the bases of psychic power as being impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom,
and they will teach that the faculties are impermanent.
They will teach that the sense faculties are suffering;
they will teach that the sense faculties are non-self;
they will teach that the sense faculties are impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom."
And those to whom they shall teach will investigate that the faculties are impermanent;
they will investigate that the faculties are suffering.
They will investigate that the sense faculties are not-self; they will investigate that the sense faculties are impure;
and while investigating them, they will find that the sense faculties are impermanent.
Seeking that the sense faculties are suffering,
seeking that the sense faculties are non-self,
and seeking that the sense faculties are impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the powers are impermanent;
they will teach that the powers are suffering;
they will teach that the powers are non-self.

They will teach that the powers are impure, and they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will investigate the powers as impermanent;
they will investigate the powers as suffering.
They will investigate that the powers are not-self; they will investigate that the powers are impure;
and while investigating them, they will find that the powers are impermanent.
Seeking the powers as suffering,
seeking the powers as non-self,
and seeking the powers as impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the factors of enlightenment are impermanent; they will teach that the factors of enlightenment are suffering;
[they will teach] that the factors of enlightenment are non-self.

They will teach the right efforts as being impure; and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will seek after the factors of enlightenment as being impermanent.
They will investigate that the factors of awakening are suffering; they will investigate that the factors of awakening are non-self; they will investigate that the factors of awakening are impure.
Seeking that the factors of enlightenment are impermanent, seeking that the factors of enlightenment are suffering, and seeking that the factors of enlightenment are non-self.
Seeking to regard the factors of enlightenment as impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that the noble eightfold path is impermanent,
and they will teach that the noble eightfold path is suffering.

They will teach that the noble eightfold path is non-self; they will teach that the noble eightfold path is impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach this will seek the noble eightfold path as impermanent.
They will seek the noble eightfold path as suffering; they will seek the noble eightfold path as non-self; they will seek the noble eightfold path as impure.
Seeking the noble eightfold path as impermanent, seeking the noble eightfold path as suffering,
and seeking the noble eightfold path as non-self.
Seeking the Noble Eightfold Path as something impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom; they will teach that the Noble Truths are impermanent,
and they will teach that the Noble Truths are suffering.
They will teach that the noble truths are selfless;

they will teach that the noble truths are impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, those to whom they will teach will seek out the noble truths as impermanent.
They will investigate the noble truths as suffering;
they will investigate the noble truths as non-self;
they will investigate the noble truths as impure.
Seeking those noble truths as impermanent,
seeking those noble truths as suffering,
and seeking those noble truths as non-self.
Seeking the noble truths as being impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that the meditative absorptions are impermanent,
and they will teach that the meditative absorptions are suffering.
They will teach that the meditative absorptions are without self;

they will teach that the meditative absorptions are impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach this will seek after the meditative absorptions as being impermanent.
They will investigate that the meditative absorptions are suffering;
they will investigate that the meditative absorptions are non-self;
they will investigate that the meditative absorptions are impure.
Seeking that the meditative absorptions are impermanent,
and seeking that the meditative absorptions are suffering, they...
Seeking that the meditative absorptions (dhyāna) are selfless,
and seeking that the meditative absorptions are impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā-prativarṇikā),
and they will teach that the immeasurables (apramāṇa) are impermanent.
They will teach that sufferings are immeasurable; they will teach that [phenomena] are immeasurable and selfless;

they will teach that [phenomena] are immeasurable and impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom. This they will teach to those [beings].
They will investigate that the immeasurables are impermanent;
they will investigate that the immeasurables are suffering;
they will investigate that the immeasurables are non-self.
They will seek the noble truths as being impure; seeking them, they will regard the immeasurables as impermanent, and seeking them, they will regard the immeasurables as suffering.
Seeking the [four] immeasurables as being without self,
and seeking the [four] immeasurables as being impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom; they will teach that the formless attainments are impermanent.
They will teach that the formless attainments are suffering;
they will teach that the formless attainments are non-self;
they will teach that the formless attainments are impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom," to those whom they shall thus instruct.
They will investigate those formless attainments as impermanent; they will investigate the formless attainments as suffering;
they will investigate the formless attainments as selfless.
They will seek the formless attainments as being impure; seeking the formless attainments as impermanent, they will seek the formless attainments as suffering.
Seeking the formless attainments as being selfless,
and seeking the formless attainments as being impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom and will teach that the liberations are impermanent.
They will teach that the liberations are suffering;
they will teach that the liberations are non-self;
they will teach that the liberations are impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom"—and those to whom they will thus teach.
They will seek the liberations as impermanent; they will seek the liberations as suffering;
they will seek the liberations as non-self.
They will seek the liberations as being impure; seeking the liberations as impermanent,
they will seek the liberations as suffering.
Seeking the liberations as being selfless,
and seeking the liberations as being impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that the successive attainments of meditative dwelling are impermanent.
They will teach that the successive attainments of meditative dwelling are suffering;
they will teach that the successive attainments of meditative dwelling are non-self;

they will teach that the successive attainments of meditative dwelling are impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. To those whom they will thus instruct, [they will speak].
They will investigate the successive attainments of meditative dwelling as impermanent;
they will investigate the successive attainments of meditative dwelling as suffering;
[they will investigate] the successive attainments of meditative dwelling... (ŚsP_II-4_209)
They will investigate them as being without self;
they will investigate the successive attainments of meditative dwelling as being impure;
and while investigating those successive attainments of meditative dwelling as being impermanent, they will...
Seeking the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings as suffering, seeking the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings as selfless,
and seeking the meditative attainments of the successive dwellings as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.

They will teach that the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are impermanent; they will teach that the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are suffering; they will teach that the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—are non-self.

They will teach the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as being impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, those to whom they teach will seek out the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as impermanent;
they will seek out the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as suffering.
They will seek the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as being selfless;
they will seek the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as being impure;
and seeking the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as being impermanent, they...
Seeking the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as suffering;
seeking the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as non-self;
and seeking the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—as impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the superknowledges are impermanent;
they will teach that the superknowledges are suffering;
they will teach that the superknowledges are non-self.

They will teach that the superknowledges are impure. And they will say: "He who courses in this way courses in the perfection of wisdom. To those whom they teach, they will seek [the truth] thinking that the superknowledges are impermanent;
they will seek [the truth] thinking that the superknowledges are suffering.
They will investigate that the superknowledges are without self; they will investigate that the superknowledges are impure;
and while investigating that the superknowledges are impermanent, they...
Seeking that the superknowledges are suffering,
seeking that the superknowledges are non-self,
and seeking that the superknowledges are impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that meditative concentrations are impermanent;
they will teach that meditative concentrations are suffering;
they will teach that meditative concentrations are non-self.

They will teach that the concentrations are "impure," and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way is practicing the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, those to whom they teach will seek out the concentrations as "impermanent" and seek out the concentrations as "suffering."
They will seek after meditative concentrations as being selfless;
they will seek after meditative concentrations as being impure;
seeking after meditative concentrations as being impermanent, they—
Seeking meditative concentrations as suffering, seeking meditative concentrations as non-self,
and seeking meditative concentrations as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the gateways of dhāraṇī are impermanent; they will teach that the gateways of dhāraṇī are suffering;
they will teach that the gateways of dhāraṇī are non-self.

They will teach that the gateways of dhāraṇī are impure, and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will seek the gateways of dhāraṇī as impermanent;
they will seek the gateways of dhāraṇī as suffering.
They will seek the gateways of dhāraṇī as being selfless; they will seek the gateways of dhāraṇī as being impure;
seeking the gateways of dhāraṇī as being impermanent, they...
Seeking the gateways of dhāraṇī as suffering, seeking the gateways of dhāraṇī as selfless,
and seeking the gateways of dhāraṇī as impure, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the powers of a Tathāgata are impermanent;
they will teach that the powers of a Tathāgata are suffering;
they will teach that the powers of a Tathāgata are non-self.

They will teach that the powers of a Tathāgata are impure. And they will say, "He who practices in this way practices in the perfection of wisdom. Those to whom they teach will seek out the powers of a Tathāgata as impermanent;
they will seek out the powers of a Tathāgata as suffering.
They will seek the powers of a Tathāgata as being selfless; they will seek the powers of a Tathāgata as being impure;
seeking the powers of a Tathāgata as being impermanent, they...
Seeking the powers of a Tathāgata as suffering, seeking the powers of a Tathāgata as non-self,
and seeking the powers of a Tathāgata as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the grounds of self-confidence are impermanent; they will teach that the grounds of self-confidence are suffering;
they will teach that the grounds of self-confidence are non-self.

They will teach that the grounds of self-confidence are impure; and they will say, "He who practices in this way practices in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, those to whom they teach will seek out the grounds of self-confidence as impermanent, and they will seek out the grounds of self-confidence as suffering.
They will investigate the fearlessnesses as being selfless; they will investigate the fearlessnesses as being impure;
and while investigating the fearlessnesses as being impermanent, they will [proceed].
Seeking the grounds of self-confidence as suffering, seeking the grounds of self-confidence as non-self,
and seeking the grounds of self-confidence as impure, they will practice in a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the analytical knowledges are impermanent;
they will teach that the analytical knowledges are suffering;
they will teach that the analytical knowledges are non-self.

They will teach that the analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) are impure; and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they will teach will seek out the analytical knowledges as impermanent, and they will seek out the analytical knowledges as suffering.

They will investigate that the analytical knowledges (pratisaṃvid) are selfless; they will investigate that the analytical knowledges are impure; and, investigating that the analytical knowledges are impermanent, they will [proceed].
Seeking the analytical knowledges as suffering, seeking the analytical knowledges as non-self, [seeking] the analytical knowledges... (ŚsP_II-4_211)
Seeking what is auspicious, they will practice a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that great compassion is impermanent,
and they will teach that great compassion is suffering.
They will teach that great compassion is selfless;

they will teach that great compassion is impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, those to whom they teach will seek great compassion as impermanent.
They will seek great compassion as suffering;
they will seek great compassion as non-self; they will seek great compassion as impure.
Seeking great compassion as impermanent, seeking great compassion as suffering,
and seeking great compassion as non-self, they...
Seeking great compassion as something impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are impermanent, and they will teach that the unique qualities of a Buddha are suffering.

They will teach that the unique qualities of a Buddha (āveṇikabuddhadharma) are selfless; they will teach that the unique qualities of a Buddha are impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, those to whom they teach will seek out the unique qualities of a Buddha as being impermanent.
They will seek the unique qualities of a Buddha as suffering;
they will seek the unique qualities of a Buddha as non-self; they will seek the unique qualities of a Buddha as impure.
Seeking the unique qualities of a Buddha as impermanent, seeking the unique qualities of a Buddha as suffering,
and seeking the unique qualities of a Buddha as non-self.
Seeking the unique attributes of a Buddha as if they were impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom; they will teach that the fruit of stream-entry is impermanent,
and they will teach that the fruit of stream-entry is suffering.
They will teach that the fruit of stream-entry is selfless;
they will teach that the fruit of stream-entry is impure;
and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way is practicing the perfection of wisdom," to those to whom they teach.
They will investigate the fruit of stream-entry as impermanent; they will investigate the fruit of stream-entry as suffering;
they will investigate the fruit of stream-entry as non-self.
They will seek the fruit of stream-entry as being impure; seeking the fruit of stream-entry as impermanent, they will seek the fruit of stream-entry as suffering.

Seeking the fruit of stream-entry as "selfless" and seeking the fruit of stream-entry as "impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom; they will teach that the fruit of once-returning is "impermanent."
They will teach that the fruit of once-returning is suffering;
they will teach that the fruit of once-returning is non-self;
they will teach that the fruit of once-returning is impure.
And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they shall give instruction will seek the fruit of once-returning as being impermanent.
They will investigate the fruit of once-returning as suffering;
they will investigate the fruit of once-returning as non-self;
they will investigate the fruit of once-returning as impure.
Seeking the fruit of once-returning as impermanent, seeking the fruit of once-returning as suffering,
and seeking the fruit of once-returning as non-self.
Seeking the fruit of once-returning as something impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom;
they will teach that the fruit of non-returning is impermanent,
and they will teach that the fruit of non-returning is suffering.
They will teach that the fruit of non-returning is selfless;
they will teach that the fruit of non-returning is impure;
and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way is practicing the perfection of wisdom," to those to whom they teach.
They will investigate the fruit of non-returning as impermanent; they will investigate the fruit of non-returning as suffering;
they will investigate the fruit of non-returning as non-self.
They will seek the fruit of non-return as something impure; seeking the fruit of non-return as impermanent, they will seek the fruit of non-return as suffering.
Seeking the fruit of non-return as "selfless" and seeking the fruit of non-return as "impure," they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom,
and they will teach that arhatship is impermanent.
They will teach that arhatship is suffering;
they will teach that arhatship is non-self;
they will teach that arhatship is impure.
And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they shall give instruction will seek for arhatship as impermanent;
they will seek for arhatship as suffering.
They will investigate arhatship as being selfless;
they will investigate arhatship as being impure; and while investigating it thus, they will regard arhatship as impermanent.
Seeking arhatship as suffering,
seeking arhatship as non-self,
and seeking arhatship as impure, they will practice in a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that pratyekabodhi is impermanent;
they will teach that pratyekabodhi is suffering;
they will teach that pratyekabodhi is non-self.

They will teach that "pratyekabodhi is impure," and they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom. And those to whom they teach will seek pratyekabodhi as impermanent.
They will seek pratyekabodhi as suffering;
they will seek pratyekabodhi as non-self;
they will seek pratyekabodhi as impure.
Seeking solitary awakening as impermanent, seeking solitary awakening as suffering,
seeking solitary awakening as non-self, and seeking solitary awakening as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that the knowledge of the aspects of the path is impermanent; they will teach that the knowledge of the aspects of the path is suffering;
they will teach that the knowledge of the aspects of the path is non-self.
They will teach that the knowledge of the aspects of the path is "impure. And they will say, "Whoever practices in this way, that person practices in the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, those to whom they will teach will seek for the knowledge of the aspects of the path as being "impermanent."
They will seek the knowledge of the aspects of the path as suffering;
they will seek the knowledge of the aspects of the path as non-self; they will seek the knowledge of the aspects of the path as impure.
Seeking the knowledge of the aspects of the path as impermanent, seeking the knowledge of the aspects of the path as suffering,
seeking the knowledge of the aspects of the path as non-self, and seeking the knowledge of the aspects of the path as impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
They will teach that omniscience is impermanent;
they will teach that omniscience is suffering.
They will teach that omniscience is selfless;
they will teach that omniscience is impure. And they will say: "Whoever practices in this way, he practices in the perfection of wisdom.
And those to whom they will teach—
They will seek omniscience as impermanent; they will seek omniscience as suffering;
they will seek omniscience as non-self.
They will seek omniscience as impure; seeking omniscience as impermanent, they will seek omniscience as suffering.
Seeking omniscience as being selfless, seeking omniscience as being impure, they will practice according to a counterfeit perfection of wisdom. This, Kauśika, is the counterfeit perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will sit down and teach this perfection of wisdom in this manner.
Come, son of good family; by cultivating the perfection of wisdom, you will abide in the first stage.
You will abide in the second stage, the third stage, the fourth stage, the fifth stage, the sixth stage, the seventh stage, the eighth stage, the ninth stage, and the tenth stage.
Come, son of good family; by cultivating the perfection of meditation, you will abide in the first stage.
You will abide in the second stage, the third stage, the fourth stage, the fifth stage, the sixth stage, the seventh stage, the eighth stage, the ninth stage, and the tenth stage.
Come, son of good family; by cultivating the perfection of vigor, you will abide on the first stage.
You will abide on the second stage, the third stage, the fourth stage, the fifth stage, the sixth stage, the seventh stage, the eighth stage, the ninth stage, and the tenth stage.

"Come, son of good family! By cultivating the perfection of patience, you will abide on the first stage; you will abide on the second stage, the third stage, the fourth stage, the fifth stage, the sixth stage, the seventh stage, the eighth stage, the ninth stage, and the tenth stage. Come, son of good family! By cultivating the perfection of ethical discipline, you will abide on the first stage; [you will abide] on the second..."
"You shall abide on the third ground, the fourth ground, the fifth ground, the sixth ground, the seventh ground, the eighth ground, the ninth ground, and the tenth ground.
Come, son of good family; by cultivating the perfection of generosity, you shall abide on the first ground. [And] the second..."

"You will abide on the third ground, the fourth ground, the fifth ground, the sixth ground, the seventh ground, the eighth ground, the ninth ground, and the tenth ground. And that, through association with signs and through association with apprehension, he will cultivate the perfection of wisdom with the notion of time. Kauśika, this is a counterfeit of the perfection of wisdom."

Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will instruct those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle in this way: "Come, son of good family, cultivate the perfection of wisdom! Son of good family, by cultivating the perfection of wisdom, you will transcend the level of the Śrāvakas and you will transcend the level of the Pratyekabuddhas. This, Kauśika, is...
That is a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family or daughters of good family teach the perfection of wisdom to those sons of good family or daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle, saying:

"Come, son of good family, cultivate the perfection of wisdom! By cultivating the perfection of wisdom, you will enter the fixed course of a bodhisattva and will attain the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena."

"Having attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) and remaining established in the superknowledges (*abhijñā*) of a bodhisattva, you will travel from buddhafield to buddhafield, honoring, respecting, revering, and worshiping those Tathāgatas,
Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones. Kauśika, it is not by teaching in this way that those sons of good family and daughters of good family will teach a counterfeit *prajñāpāramitā*."
Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will instruct those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the bodhisattva vehicle as follows:

"Whichever son of good family shall take up, preserve, recite, master, and attend to the perfection of wisdom in a proper manner, he shall produce an immeasurable, incalculable, and infinite mass of merit."
Teaching in this way, they will instruct those sons of good family or daughters of good family in a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will instruct those sons of good family or daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle in this manner: "Come, son of good family, [study] the Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present."

Whatever root of merit belongs to the Arhats and the Perfectly Awakened Ones— from the first production of the thought of awakening until their final nirvana in the realm of nirvana without remainder— all that, having been condensed and rejoiced in, [is dedicated] toward supreme [enlightenment].

"By dedicating [their merit] toward unexcelled perfect enlightenment, those sons of good family and daughters of good family who teach in this way will be teaching a counterfeit of the perfection of wisdom.

Śakra said: "Blessed One, how is it that those sons of good family and daughters of good family do not teach a counterfeit of the perfection of wisdom to those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle?"
The Blessed One said:

"In this regard, Kauśika, sons of good family and daughters of good family will teach the perfection of wisdom to those sons of good family and daughters of good family who belong to the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, saying:
'Come, son of good family, cultivate the perfection of wisdom; do not [neglect it]...'"

And one perceives that form is impermanent. Why is that? Form is empty of intrinsic nature; whatever is the intrinsic nature of form, that is non-existent. That is the perfection of wisdom; in that perfection of wisdom, form is not apprehended as either permanent or impermanent.
Form itself does not exist and is not apprehended. How much less, then, could it be permanent or impermanent?
Teaching in this way, Kauśika, those sons of good family or daughters of good family will not teach a counterfeit of the perfection of wisdom.
Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will instruct those sons of good family or daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle in this manner:
"Come, son of good family, cultivate the perfection of wisdom, but do not perceive feeling as impermanent. Why is that?
The intrinsic nature of feeling, which is empty of the intrinsic nature of feeling, is that non-existence which is existence; that is the perfection of wisdom.
In it, feeling is not apprehended as permanent. Feeling itself does not exist there and is not apprehended;
how much less could it be either permanent or impermanent? Teaching in this way, Kauśika, those sons of good family—

Or daughters of good family will not teach a counterfeit perfection of wisdom. Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will teach the perfection of wisdom to those sons of good family and daughters of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle in this way: "Come, son of good family, [study] the perfection of wisdom."
Cultivate the perception that "formations are impermanent," yet do not regard them as such. Why is that?
Because the nature of perception is empty of the intrinsic nature of perception; that which is its lack of intrinsic nature is non-existence, and that non-existence is the perfection of wisdom.
In that perfection of wisdom, neither a permanent perception nor an impermanent perception is apprehended. Therein, it is simply perception itself.

It does not exist. How, then, could it be either permanent or impermanent? Kauśika, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who teach in this way will not be teaching a counterfeit *prajñāpāramitā*.
Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family [will assist] those sons of good family belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle...

And they will teach the perfection of wisdom to daughters of good family in this way: "Come, son of good family, cultivate the perfection of wisdom, and do not perceive conditioned phenomena as impermanent. Why is that?
Conditioned phenomena are empty by their own nature; that which is the own-nature of conditioned phenomena is non-existence, and that which is non-existence is the perfection of wisdom."

In that perfection of wisdom, no formations are perceived as either permanent or impermanent; for therein, even formations themselves do not exist. How, then, could they be permanent or impermanent? Kauśika, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who teach in this way will not teach a counterfeit perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Kauśika, those sons of good family and daughters of good family will teach the perfection of wisdom to those sons of good family and daughters of good family who belong to the vehicle of the bodhisattvas, saying: "Come, son of good family, cultivate the perfection of wisdom, and do not perceive consciousness as impermanent. Why is that?"

What do you think, Kauśika? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce much merit on that account?
He said: "Much, Blessed One; much, Sugata.
The Blessed One said:
"Therefore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce even more merit than that."

Whoever should explain this Perfection of Wisdom in detail to others—endowed with both meaning and phrasing—should teach it, illuminate it, investigate it, analyze it, make it clear, and fully reveal it. And they should say:
"Come, noble son, take up this Perfection of Wisdom, master it, retain it, uphold it, recite it, attend to it thoroughly, and practice according to the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught."
For what reason? Because,
Kauśika, it is from this perfection of wisdom that the pratyekabuddhas are manifested.

Furthermore, Kauśika, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to encourage all the beings in Jambudvīpa to attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. What do you think, Kauśika, would that son of good family or daughter of good family generate a great deal more merit on that account?
He replied: "A great deal, Blessed One; a great deal, Sugata."
The Blessed One said:
"Therefore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family would generate much more merit."

Whoever should explain this Perfection of Wisdom in detail to others—endowed with both meaning and phrasing—should teach it, illuminate it, investigate it, analyze it, clarify it, and fully reveal it; and should speak thus: "Come, noble son, take up this Perfection of Wisdom, master it, retain it, uphold it, recite it, and attend to it thoroughly."

And attend to it; practice according to the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught. Noble son, when you practice according to the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught, then, noble son, you will be training in the Perfection of Wisdom.
When you, noble son, train in the perfection of wisdom,
then you will attain the qualities of omniscience;
when you attain the qualities of omniscience, [you will realize them].
Then you will bring the perfection of wisdom to a state of greater fulfillment through cultivation;
and when you have brought the perfection of wisdom to a state of greater fulfillment through cultivation, then you will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is that?
For it is from this, Kauśika, that the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have first produced the thought of awakening have emerged.
Let alone, Kauśika, the beings of Jambudvīpa who have been encouraged toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening;

suppose, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to encourage as many beings as there are in a four-continent world system toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening. What do you think?

He replied, “Much, Blessed One; much, Sugata.
The Blessed One said:

both in its meaning and its phrasing, and should say: "Come, son of good family, take up this Perfection of Wisdom, master it, and bear it in mind."

Recite it, attend to it thoroughly, and practice according to the Prajñāpāramitā as it has been taught. Noble son, when you practice according to the Prajñāpāramitā as it has been taught, then, noble son,
you will be training in the Prajñāpāramitā.

then you will attain the qualities of omniscience;

Let alone, Kauśika, the beings in a world-system of four continents who have been inspired toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening.

Come, son of good family, take up the perfection of wisdom, master it, retain it, uphold it, recite it, attend to it thoroughly,

and practice according to the perfection of wisdom as it has been taught. Son of good family, when you practice according to the perfection of wisdom as it has been taught, then, son of good family, you will train in the perfection of wisdom.
When you, noble son, train in the perfection of wisdom, then you will attain all dharmas;
when you attain all dharmas, [you will realize the fruit of arhatship].
Then your cultivation of the perfection of wisdom will reach fulfillment to a greater degree;
and when your cultivation of the perfection of wisdom reaches fulfillment to a greater degree, then you will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. Why is that?

Furthermore, Kauśika, suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all the sentient beings in Jambudvīpa on the stage of non-retrogression. What do you think,
Kauśika, would that son of good family or daughter of good family generate a great deal of merit on that account?
He said: "Much, Blessed One; much, Sugata.
The Blessed One said:
"Therefore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family would generate much merit on that account."

Whoever should explain this Perfection of Wisdom in detail to others— teaching it, revealing it, investigating it, analyzing it, making it clear, and fully illuminating it— and should say: "Come, son of good family, take up this Perfection of Wisdom, master it, retain it, uphold it, recite it, and attend to it with wise reflection according to how it has been taught."
Practice it. Noble son, when you practice according to the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught, then, noble son, you will be training in the Perfection of Wisdom;

Then you will become an attainer of the qualities of omniscience. When you become an attainer of the qualities of omniscience, then your perfection of wisdom will, to a greater degree, reach the fulfillment of its cultivation;

Therefore, Kauśika, it is from the perfection of wisdom that the irreversible stage of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is produced.

Let alone, Kauśika, the beings of Jambudvīpa established in the irreversible stage; even if some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings, Kauśika, who exist in a world-system of four continents, in the irreversible stage—
One should establish it. What do you think, Kauśika? Would that son of good family or daughter of good family generate much more merit on that account?
He said: "Much, Blessed One; much, Sugata."
The Blessed One said:

"Therefore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family would generate much more merit who should extensively teach, explain, reveal, analyze, and expound this Perfection of Wisdom to others, together with its meaning and its phrasing."

One should bring it to light and reveal it. And one should say: "Come, noble son, take up the perfection of wisdom, master it, retain it, uphold it, recite it, attend to it thoroughly, and practice according to this perfection of wisdom as it has been taught.
Noble son, when you have practiced according to this perfection of wisdom as it has been taught,"
Then, noble son, you will train in the perfection of wisdom;
when, noble son, you train in the perfection of wisdom, then you will become an attainer of the qualities of omniscience. When you become an attainer of the qualities of omniscience,
Then you shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, the stage of non-retrogression for bodhisattva mahāsattvas is produced from the perfection of wisdom.

The Blessed One said:

Whoever should teach, explain, reveal, analyze, differentiate, clarify, and fully illuminate this Perfection of Wisdom to others, both in its meaning and its phrasing, in detail, and should speak thus: "Come, noble son, take up this Perfection of Wisdom, master it, retain it, uphold it, and recite it."
Attend to it properly and practice according to the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught. Noble son, when you practice according to the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught, then,
noble son, you will be training in the Perfection of Wisdom.
When you, son of good family, train in the perfection of wisdom,
then you will become an obtainer of the qualities of omniscience;

Then you shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, the irreversible stage of Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, is produced from the perfection of wisdom.

What do you think, Kauśika, would that son of good family or daughter of good family generate much merit on that account?"

Whoever should teach this Perfection of Wisdom to others in detail—possessing both the meaning and the letter—should explain it, illuminate it, analyze it, differentiate it, clarify it, and fully reveal it;
and should speak thus: "Come, son of good family, take up this Perfection of Wisdom, master it, learn it, and retain it."
Recite it, attend to it thoroughly, and practice according to the Prajñāpāramitā as it has been taught. Noble son, when you practice according to the Prajñāpāramitā as it has been taught,
then, noble son, you will be training in the Prajñāpāramitā.

then you will become an attainer of the qualities of omniscience;

Then you shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, the stage of non-retrogression for bodhisattva mahāsattvas is produced from the perfection of wisdom.
Let alone, Kauśika, the beings in a triple-thousand great thousandfold world system who have been inspired toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Kauśika, suppose there were as many beings in the triple-thousand great-thousand world-system as have been established in the stage of non-retrogression; and suppose, Kauśika, some son of good family or daughter of good family were to establish all those beings—as many as there are beings in worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in each of the ten directions—in the stage of non-retrogression. What do you think?
"Kauśika, would that son of good family or daughter of good family generate much merit on that account?
He replied, "Much, Blessed One; much, Sugata.
The Blessed One said:

Therefore, Kauśika, that son of good family or daughter of good family would generate much greater merit who, having taught, shown, revealed, analyzed, explained, clarified, and fully illuminated this Perfection of Wisdom— along with its meaning and its phrasing— to others, should say: "Come, son of good family, take up this Perfection of Wisdom, master it, memorize it, and retain it."

Recite it, attend to it thoroughly, and practice according to the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught. Noble son, when you practice the Perfection of Wisdom as it has been taught, then, noble son, you will be training in the Perfection of Wisdom.
When you, noble son, train in the perfection of wisdom,
then you will become an attainer of the qualities of omniscience;
when you become an attainer of the qualities of omniscience, [then...]
Then you shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. For what reason?
Because, Kauśika, the irreversible stage of the bodhisattva mahāsattvas is produced from the perfection of wisdom.

Furthermore, Kauśika, suppose all the beings in Jambudvīpa were to set out for unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening; and suppose some son of good family or daughter of good family were to teach this Perfection of Wisdom, along with its meaning and its phrasing, in detail to others.
One should teach, reveal, discuss, analyze, clarify, and fully illuminate it;

and one should speak thus: "Come, noble son, take up the perfection of wisdom, master it, retain it, uphold it, recite it, attend to it thoroughly, and practice according to the perfection of wisdom as it has been taught. According to how it has been taught...

One should reflect upon it, analyze it, clarify it, and fully illuminate it;
and thus one should say: "Come, noble son, take up this perfection of wisdom, master it, retain it, uphold it, recite it, and attend to it thoroughly according to its meaning.
When you, noble son, practice in accordance with the perfection of wisdom as it has been taught,"
Then, noble son, you will train in the perfection of wisdom;

when, noble son, you train in the perfection of wisdom, then you will become an attainer of all dharmas. When you become an attainer of the dharmas of omniscience, [you will attain the state of a Buddha].

and were to say, "Come quickly, you shall fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment," yet some son of good family or daughter of good family were to teach this Perfection of Wisdom in detail, with its meaning and its phrasing, to that person—
it is this very son of good family or daughter of good family who would generate far more merit.

"Kauśika, let alone the beings in this trichiliocosm great thousandfold world system who are irreversible from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment; rather, Kauśika, as many beings as there are in worlds as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in each of the ten directions—
if all those beings were to become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, [compared] to those bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas..."
A certain son of good family or daughter of good family would produce much greater merit. Why is that?

For one should not teach the Dharma for any other purpose than for those bodhisattvas who are irreversible; for they are fixed upon supreme enlightenment and will no longer fall back from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening. This was the thought [of the Buddha].
And he is oppressed by great compassion for the sake of cyclic existence.
Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

Blessed One, to the same extent that a bodhisattva mahāsattva becomes practiced in unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, to that same extent should the bodhisattva mahāsattva be exhorted and instructed in the perfection of generosity, and to that same extent should he be exhorted and instructed in the perfection of ethical discipline;
and to that same extent should he be exhorted and instructed in the perfection of patience.
In such and such a manner he should be exhorted and instructed in the perfection of vigor;
in such and such a manner he should be exhorted and instructed in the perfection of meditation; in such and such a manner he should be exhorted and instructed in the perfection of wisdom.
To the extent that a bodhisattva mahāsattva becomes a practitioner of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, to that same extent should he be exhorted and instructed in internal emptiness;
to that same extent should he be exhorted and instructed in external emptiness;
to that same extent should he be exhorted and instructed in internal-and-external emptiness.

In that same way, he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the emptiness of emptiness; in that same way, he should be instructed and exhorted regarding great emptiness; in that same way, he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the emptiness of the ultimate truth.
He should be exhorted and instructed;
he should be exhorted and instructed in such a way regarding the emptiness of the conditioned, and he should be exhorted and instructed in such a way regarding the emptiness of the unconditioned.

In that same way, he should be exhorted and instructed regarding absolute emptiness; in that same way, he should be exhorted and instructed regarding the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end;
in that same way, he should be exhorted and instructed regarding the emptiness of non-dispersal.
In such and such a manner, he should be exhorted and instructed in the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
in such and such a manner, he should be exhorted and instructed in the emptiness of all phenomena;
in such and such a manner, he should be exhorted and instructed in the emptiness of specific characteristics.
In that same way, he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the emptiness of non-apprehension; in that same way, he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the emptiness of non-existence;
in that same way, he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
In that same way, he should be exhorted and instructed in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence.
Just as the bodhisattva mahāsattva becomes more practiced in unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, so too should he be exhorted and instructed in the applications of mindfulness,
and exhorted and instructed in the right efforts.
He should be exhorted and instructed regarding the bases of psychic power;
he should be exhorted and instructed regarding the faculties; he should be exhorted and instructed regarding the powers.
He should be instructed and exhorted regarding the factors of enlightenment and the immeasurables;
he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the noble eightfold path;
he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the noble truths.
He should be exhorted and instructed regarding the meditative absorptions;
he should be exhorted and instructed regarding the immeasurables;
he should be exhorted and instructed regarding the formless attainments.
He should be instructed and exhorted regarding the liberations;
he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the nine successive meditative attainments;
he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the gateways to liberation that are emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
He should be instructed and exhorted regarding the superknowledges;
he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the meditative concentrations; he should be instructed and exhorted regarding the gateways of the dhāraṇīs.

He should be exhorted and instructed in the powers of a Tathāgata; he should be exhorted and instructed in the grounds of self-confidence; he should be exhorted and instructed in the analytical knowledges.
He should be instructed and exhorted in great loving-kindness; he should be instructed and exhorted in great compassion;
he should be instructed and exhorted in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
They should also be assisted with the requisites of robes, alms-bowls, bedding and seats, and medicines for the treatment of illness.

Furthermore, those sons and daughters of good family who assist the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva through both the gathering of the Dharma and the gathering of material goods will produce far more merit than those former ones. It is not at all the case that those former ones [produce such merit].
Noble sons and noble daughters. For what reason?
Because it is thus, Blessed One, for that bodhisattva mahāsattva who is being instructed and exhorted in the perfection of generosity.

He will be instructed and exhorted in the perfection of ethical discipline; he will be instructed and exhorted in the perfection of patience; [he will be instructed and exhorted] in the perfection of vigor.
He will be instructed and exhorted;
he will be instructed and exhorted in the perfection of meditative concentration; he will be instructed and exhorted in the perfection of wisdom.
He will be instructed and exhorted regarding internal emptiness; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding external emptiness;
he will be instructed and exhorted regarding internal and external emptiness.
He will be instructed and exhorted regarding the emptiness of emptiness; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding great emptiness;
he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the emptiness of the ultimate truth. He will be instructed and exhorted regarding the emptiness of the conditioned.
He is exhorted and instructed in the emptiness of the unconditioned;
he is exhorted and instructed in absolute emptiness;
he is exhorted and instructed in the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end.
He is instructed and exhorted in the emptiness of non-dispersal;

he is instructed and exhorted in the emptiness of intrinsic nature. He is instructed and exhorted in the emptiness of all phenomena; he is instructed and exhorted in the emptiness of specific characteristics.
He is instructed and exhorted in the emptiness of non-apprehension; he is instructed and exhorted in the emptiness of non-existence;
he is instructed and exhorted in the emptiness of intrinsic nature.
He is instructed and exhorted in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
he is instructed and exhorted in the applications of mindfulness;
he is instructed and exhorted in the right efforts.
He will be instructed and exhorted regarding the bases of psychic power; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the faculties; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the powers.
He will be instructed and exhorted regarding the immeasurables; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the factors of enlightenment;
he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the paths.

He will be instructed and exhorted regarding the noble truths; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the meditative concentrations; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the immeasurables.
He will be instructed and exhorted regarding the formless attainments;
he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the eight liberations; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the nine successive meditative attainments.

He will be instructed and exhorted in the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness; he will be instructed and exhorted in the superknowledges; he will be instructed and exhorted in the meditative concentrations.
He will be instructed and exhorted regarding the gateways of dhāraṇī; he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the ten powers of a Tathāgata;
he will be instructed and exhorted regarding the four grounds of self-confidence.
He will be instructed and exhorted in the four analytical knowledges; he will be instructed and exhorted in great loving-kindness; he will be instructed and exhorted in great compassion.
He will be instructed and exhorted regarding the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Then the Venerable Subhūti addressed Śakra, the lord of the gods:

"Excellent, excellent, Kauśika! That you give encouragement to the bodhisattvas and assist the bodhisattvas in their undertaking—this is exactly what must be done by you, Kauśika. Any noble disciple who wishes to act for the benefit of sentient beings should provide encouragement to the bodhisattva mahāsattvas toward unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening; and through the gift of the Dharma, he should assist the bodhisattvas and bring them to full maturity. Why is that?"
Therefore, Kausika, you should know that the community of the Blessed One’s disciples consists of these very bodhisattvas,

the mahasattvas; for if a bodhisattva, a mahasattva, were not to resolve his mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, he would not be a bodhisattva, a mahasattva, nor would he train in the six perfections— the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, and so forth.
In the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, and the perfection of wisdom;
in internal emptiness and external emptiness.
In internal-external emptiness,
in the emptiness of emptiness,
and in great emptiness;
in ultimate emptiness,
in conditioned emptiness,
and in unconditioned emptiness;
in absolute emptiness,
in emptiness without beginning or end, and in non-dispersal emptiness;
In the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
in the emptiness of all phenomena,
and in the emptiness of specific characteristics.
in the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence,
and the emptiness of intrinsic nature;
In the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence;
in the applications of mindfulness and the right efforts.
In the bases of psychic power, the faculties, and the powers.
In the factors of enlightenment, in the noble eightfold path,
and in the noble truths.
In the meditative absorptions, the immeasurables, and the formless attainments.
in the eight liberations,
the nine successive meditative attainments,
and the gateways to liberation consisting of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
in the superknowledges, the meditative concentrations, and the gateways of mnemonic formulas;
in the powers of a Tathāgata, the grounds of self-confidence, and the analytical knowledges;
in great loving-kindness, in great compassion,
and in the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;

Neither the Pratyekabuddhas nor the Śrāvakas [excel] in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, nor in wisdom; for this reason, Kauśika, it is because the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva trains in the six perfections— namely, the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and in internal emptiness.
in external emptiness,
in internal-external emptiness,
and in the emptiness of emptiness;
in great emptiness,
in ultimate emptiness,
and in conditioned emptiness;
in the emptiness of the unconditioned,
in the ultimate emptiness,
and in the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end;
in the emptiness of non-dispersal,
in the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
and in the emptiness of all phenomena;
in the emptiness of specific characteristics,
in the emptiness of non-apprehension,
and in the emptiness of non-existence;
In the emptiness of intrinsic nature,
in the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence,
and in the applications of mindfulness.
In the right efforts,
the bases of psychic power, and the faculties.
In the powers, in the factors of enlightenment, and in the noble eightfold path.
In the noble truths, the meditative absorptions, and the immeasurables.
in the formless attainments,
in the eight liberations,
and in the nine successive meditative attainments;
In the gateways to liberation— emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—
in the superknowledges,
and in the meditative concentrations.
in the gateways of dhāraṇīs, in the powers of a Tathāgata, and in the grounds of self-confidence;
In the analytical knowledges,
in great loving-kindness, and in great compassion.
In the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha.
Therefore, the bodhisattva mahāsattva awakens to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
once he has awakened to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, in all world systems, hell is cut off, the animal realm is cut off, and the world of Yama is cut off.
The hosts of asuras decline, while the celestial hosts increase;
there appears in the world the appearance of great kshatriya clans,
and there appears in the world the appearance of great brahmin clans.
There is the appearance in the world of great wealthy householder families;
there is the appearance in the world of the gods of the Four Great Kings;
there is the appearance in the world of the Trāyastriṃśa gods.
There is the manifestation in the world of the Yāma gods;
there is the manifestation in the world of the Tuṣita gods;
there is the manifestation in the world of the Nirmāṇarati gods.
There is the manifestation of gods of the Paranirmitavaśavartin realm in the world;
there is the manifestation of gods of the Brahmakāyika realm in the world; there is the manifestation of gods of the Brahmapurohita realm in the world.
The appearance of beings occurs in the world of the Brahma-pārṣadya gods; the appearance of beings occurs in the world of the Mahābrahmā gods;
the appearance of beings occurs in the world of the Ābhā gods.
The appearance of the gods of Limited Radiance occurs in the world;
the appearance of the gods of Immeasurable Radiance occurs in the world; the appearance of the gods of Utmost Purity occurs in the world.
There is the appearance of the Śubha deities in the world;
there is the appearance of the Parīttaśubha deities in the world;
there is the appearance of the Apramāṇaśubha deities in the world.
There is the manifestation of beings in the world of the Śubhakṛtsna gods, there is the manifestation of beings in the world of the Bṛhat gods,
and there is the manifestation of beings in the world of the Parīttabṛhat gods.
The appearance of the Apramāṇaśubha gods occurs in their world; the appearance of the Bṛhatphala gods occurs in their world;
the appearance of the Atapa gods occurs in their world.
There is a manifestation in the world of the Sudṛśa devas; there is a manifestation in the world of the Sudarśana devas;
there is a manifestation in the world of the Akaniṣṭha devas.
The appearance of the gods of the sphere of infinite space occurs in the world; the appearance of the gods of the sphere of infinite consciousness occurs in the world;
the appearance of the gods of the sphere of nothingness occurs in the world.
The appearance of the gods of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception occurs in the world;
the appearance of the perfection of generosity occurs in the world; the appearance of the perfection of ethical discipline occurs in the world.
The perfection of patience appears in the world; the perfection of vigor appears in the world;
the perfection of meditation appears in the world.
Through the perfection of wisdom, there is the manifestation in the world.
There is the manifestation in the world of internal emptiness; there is the manifestation in the world of external emptiness.
The appearance of internal-external emptiness occurs in the world;
the appearance of the emptiness of emptiness occurs in the world; the appearance of great emptiness occurs in the world.
The manifestation of ultimate emptiness occurs in the world;
the manifestation of conditioned emptiness occurs in the world; the manifestation of unconditioned emptiness occurs in the world.
The manifestation of absolute emptiness occurs in the world; the manifestation of the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of non-dispersal occurs in the world; the manifestation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature occurs in the world.
The emptiness of all phenomena appears in the world; the emptiness of specific characteristics appears in the world;
the emptiness of non-apprehension appears in the world.
The manifestation of the emptiness of non-existence occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the emptiness of intrinsic nature occurs in the world; and the manifestation of the emptiness of the intrinsic nature of non-existence occurs in the world.
The appearance of the foundations of mindfulness occurs in the world;
the appearance of the right efforts occurs in the world;
the appearance of the bases of psychic power occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the sense-faculties occurs in the world; the manifestation of the powers occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the factors of enlightenment occurs in the world.
The appearance of the noble eightfold path occurs in the world;
the appearance of the noble truths occurs in the world;
the appearance of the meditative absorptions occurs in the world.
There is the manifestation in the world of the immeasurables; there is the manifestation in the world of the formless attainments;
there is the manifestation in the world of the eight liberations.
The manifestation of the nine successive meditative attainments occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the gateways to liberation—emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness—occurs in the world;
and the manifestation of the superknowledges occurs in the world.
The manifestation of concentrations occurs in the world; the manifestation of the gateways of dhāraṇīs occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the ten powers of a Tathāgata occurs in the world.
The manifestation of the four grounds of self-confidence occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the four analytical knowledges occurs in the world;
the manifestation of great loving-kindness occurs in the world.
The manifestation of great compassion occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha occurs in the world;
the manifestation of the vehicle of the disciples occurs in the world.
The appearance of the Pratyekabuddha occurs in the world;
the appearance of the Mahāyāna occurs in the world.
This is the twenty-third chapter, titled "Śakra," in the *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*.
